# AURA ClinicOS

# Version 6.1 Quality-Controlled Full Functional, Technical, UI, Data, API, Event, AI, Testing, and Codex Build Specification

**Date:** May 2026  
**Product:** AURA ClinicOS  
**Core modules:** AURA Flow, AURA PreVisit, AURA RevCycle, AURA QualityGuard, AURA InfectionShield, AURA CareOps, AURA Copilot, AURA Command Center  
**Commercial thesis:** Turn a clinic into a world-class outpatient institution where quality, outcomes, revenue integrity, access, safety, patient trust, and staff effectiveness are all higher because the operating system coordinates the clinic in real time.

## How to read v6

Version 6.1 is intentionally additive and quality-controlled. It preserves the exhaustive v4 module specification as a retained baseline, merges the decision-locked v5 assumptions, and adds a larger v6 layer of implementation-grade detail. Codex precedence is strict: (1) v6.1 Normative Build Rules and Correction Log, (2) v6.1 module build contracts and companion artifacts, (3) retained v6/v5/v4 traceability content only where it does not conflict. Retained baseline text is included for traceability, not to override the v6.1 contracts.

## Codex build objective

Codex should be able to use this document as the primary build source. The remaining work should be implementation, not product discovery. The document therefore specifies:

- the business and clinical operating model;
- every module's functional behavior;
- service boundaries and technical architecture;
- role-based UI surfaces and component behavior;
- logical and physical data models;
- FHIR/HL7/X12/integration mappings;
- APIs, events, workflows, rules, and automation boundaries;
- AI agents, RAG, model governance, and safety controls;
- reference primary-care service playbooks;
- security, privacy, audit, compliance, and downtime behavior;
- testing, QA, acceptance criteria, and build backlog.


# 0. v6.1 Quality-Controlled Build Rules and Correction Log

This section is normative. Codex and engineering teams must follow this section before any retained v4/v5/v6 prose. It was added after a full audit of the v6 package to remove ambiguous directions and prevent implementation liberties.

## 0.1 Pristine-build precedence

1. Implement the v6.1 module functional requirements, data contracts, OpenAPI contracts, event schemas, RBAC matrix, AI-agent registry, SQL schema, FHIR mappings, and test plan.
2. Treat retained v4/v5/v6 text as traceability and context only when it does not conflict with v6.1.
3. Ignore any retained phrase that sounds like a scaffolding phrase, generic numbered capability, non-production API draft, or unresolved target-dialect note.
4. Never infer product behavior from missing detail. If a needed behavior is absent, create a `SPEC_GAP` issue rather than inventing functionality.
5. Never implement autonomous diagnosis, code finalization, charge finalization, medical-necessity determination, clinical order finalization, denial of care, infection-control override, or high-impact patient-financial conclusion.
6. Write back only tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and staff-verified pre-visit data. Charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts require human approval.
7. Use the NP-led value-based primary-care model as the v1 reference implementation and keep enterprise multispecialty support as configurable expansion.

## 0.2 Audit issues corrected in v6.1

| Finding | Risk to Codex | v6.1 correction |
|---|---|---|
| Generic module requirements such as numbered workflow capabilities | Codex would have to invent functionality | Replaced all 612 generic FR lines with specific module-level functional requirements. |
| OpenAPI file was labeled as an expanded skeleton and lacked operation IDs | Generated clients and handlers would be ambiguous | Added operation IDs, standard envelopes, request bodies, response schemas, and contract language. |
| SQL was framed as an addendum using mixed schema qualification | Codex could treat the schema as optional or dialect-uncertain | Added canonical v6.1 Azure PostgreSQL conventions and schema-qualified tables. |
| FHIR references used current build URLs in places | Production integrations could target unstable CI-build material | Reframed production baseline as FHIR R4/US Core/SMART stable publications; future FHIR versions are compatibility targets only. |
| FDA CDS reference could be read as 2022-only | Regulatory boundary might be stale | Updated the controlling language to use the January 2026 FDA CDS guidance anchor. |
| Some phrases used scaffolding language | Codex could leave scaffolding incomplete | Replaced scaffolding language with explicit integration-point language and added SPEC_GAP handling. |
| Retained v4/v5/v6 content could conflict | Codex might choose the wrong instruction | Added strict precedence and non-normative treatment for superseded retained content. |

## 0.3 Production standard anchors

- Production FHIR baseline: FHIR R4, US Core, SMART App Launch, CDS Hooks, and applicable Da Vinci/payer APIs where supported by the target integration.
- Azure baseline: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server or Azure SQL by deployment decision, Microsoft Entra ID/OIDC, Azure Key Vault, Azure Monitor/Application Insights, Azure Event Hubs or Service Bus, and Azure Health Data Services FHIR service where selected.
- AI governance baseline: NIST AI RMF-style governance, ONC HTI-1 transparency concepts for certified-health-IT contexts, FDA CDS boundary analysis for clinical decision-support functions, source-linked RAG, model cards, evaluation, drift monitoring, and human approval for high-risk outputs.
- Security baseline: HIPAA Security Rule administrative, physical, and technical safeguards, tenant isolation, least privilege, audit logging, encryption in transit and at rest, business-continuity and downtime procedures, and customer compliance validation.
- Infection-control baseline: CDC outpatient infection-prevention expectations and Standard Precautions operationalized through local policy and InfectionShield stop logic.

## 0.4 Codex no-liberty rule

For every implemented feature, Codex must be able to point to at least one of the following: a v6.1 functional requirement ID, a module registry entry, an OpenAPI endpoint, a SQL table/column, an event schema, a UI screen component, an RBAC permission, an AI-agent permission, or a test case. Features without traceability must not be implemented silently.



# 1. Decision-Locked Product and Operating Assumptions


## Initial ideal customers

NP-led or NP-heavy primary care groups operating in Medicare Advantage/value-based care, with high AWV, TCM, CCM/APCM, quality-gap, risk-adjustment, and revenue-cycle upside; also physician-owned primary-care groups and other primary-care clinic structures.


## Product scope

Enterprise multispecialty platform with primary care fully specified as the reference implementation.


## Reference site model

NP-owned and NP-led clinic with four NPs per site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, NPs seeing all visit types, and a collaborating physician performing chart reviews for three non-autonomous NPs while the autonomous owner and medical director govern the rest.


## Payer optimization

Medicare Advantage and value-based primary care first, preserving configurable payer logic for Medicare FFS, commercial, Medicaid, FQHC, direct primary care, and other structures.


## Revenue posture

Revenue-maximizing only through appropriate, compliant revenue: eliminate missed clinically appropriate services, denials, underdocumentation, and undercapture without upcoding, coercive collections, duplicate billing, or unnecessary care.


## Automation level

Version 1 uses Level 3/4 automation: task routing, drafting, low-risk controlled actions, and human-in-the-loop approvals; Level 5 autopilot is documented as governed future-state capability.


## RTLS

Vendor-neutral hybrid BLE/UWB reference architecture: UWB for room/procedure/sub-room precision, BLE for broader clinic movement and asset tracking, and adapters for RFID/Wi-Fi/phone-based approaches.


## EHR architecture

Vendor-neutral FHIR/HL7 architecture with concrete implementation tracks for Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks.


## EHR writeback

Write back tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and staff-verified pre-visit data. Create charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, and order suggestions for approval only. Never autonomously finalize diagnoses, codes, medical necessity, charges, or clinical orders.


## AI architecture

Vendor/model agnostic but technically specific: rules engine, predictive ML, LLM/RAG, optimization models, knowledge graph, simulation engine, and human-in-loop review.


## Patient engagement

SMS/web-first engagement with optional patient-portal integration.


## Roles

Design all roles separately; allow role bundling for smaller clinics.


## Readiness scoring

Dynamic weighting by visit type with score dissectability down to component, evidence, owner, and rule.


## Stop logic

Configurable by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, safety, infection-control risk, and compliance risk.


## Quality priority

Primary care v1 prioritizes HEDIS/STARS, MIPS/MVP, and internal outcomes.


## InfectionShield

Enterprise architecture supports five levels; v1 implements room/equipment cleaning, respiratory screening, direct-rooming, PPE prompts, and infection-control-ready room status.


## Initial service playbooks

Fully specify AWV, TCM, RPM, injections, spirometry, procedure visits, CCM/APCM, preventive plus E/M, vaccines, ECG, labs, telehealth, and chronic-disease follow-up.


## Delivery strategy

Full enterprise product built module by module so it is functional early and layers on more capability over time.


## UX specificity

Include wireframe-level screen definitions and component behavior.


## Technical stack

Recommended stack with vendor-neutral alternatives; initial build assumes Azure databasing and Microsoft Entra for identity/access.


## Integration scope

Mandatory v1 integrations include EHR schedule, demographics, appointments, encounters, tasks, documents, observations/labs, medications, problem list, allergies, eligibility, messaging, payments/payment links, RTLS feed, and SSO.


## Architecture style

Hybrid platform leaning strongly toward microservices with extractable services and event-driven workflows.


## Data model

Logical and physical schemas for core modules, FHIR mappings, and event payloads.


## Testing

Module-level unit, integration, UI, workflow, AI safety, compliance, RCM, infection-control, FHIR/API contract, RTLS simulation, load, downtime, and audit-log tests.


## Deployment

SaaS platform with optional on-prem/edge gateway for RTLS and integration, plus SMART-on-FHIR embedded launch.


## Brand

AURA ClinicOS, with modules AURA Flow, AURA PreVisit, AURA RevCycle, AURA QualityGuard, AURA InfectionShield, AURA CareOps, AURA Copilot, and AURA Command Center.


# 2. Institutional Ambition: World-Class Clinic Operating System

AURA ClinicOS is designed to make the clinic perform like a world-class institution rather than a collection of disconnected staff, dashboards, and after-the-fact reports. The system assumes that exceptional quality and exceptional revenue integrity come from the same source: reliable preparation, standardized work, closed-loop execution, accurate documentation, respectful patient engagement, and continuous learning.

The platform treats every patient encounter as a synchronized production event. By the time an NP enters the room, the patient should be clinically prepared, financially clear, quality-gap mapped, medication-risk reviewed, infection-control safe, socially supported, and summarized in a concise handoff. The system is intentionally built to avoid the common outpatient failure mode where the provider discovers missing records, incomplete forms, inactive coverage, absent authorizations, open quality gaps, med confusion, patient barriers, or room problems during the encounter itself.

World-class clinic behavior is defined by measurable operational reliability: green readiness before the clinic day, clean authorization workflows, zero preventable no-auth denials, reliable AWV/TCM/care-management preparation, chart review where supervision is required, structured quality gap closure, safe infection-control room release, disciplined AI governance, and no-blame defect learning.


# 3. v6 Reference Architecture Overview



The reference architecture is a SaaS microservice platform deployed on Azure. It uses Microsoft Entra for workforce identity and privileged access, Entra External ID or a patient identity partner for patient/caregiver access, Azure SQL Database or Azure Database for PostgreSQL for transactional data, Azure Service Bus and Event Hubs for event flow, Azure AI Search or pgvector for RAG/vector search, Azure Blob/Data Lake for documents and analytics staging, Azure Monitor/Application Insights/OpenTelemetry for observability, Azure Key Vault for secrets, and AKS or Azure Container Apps for service deployment.

Vendor-neutral alternatives are permitted, but the v6 build should start Azure-first. The platform must still be cloud-portable at the domain level: APIs, events, database schemas, and service boundaries should not depend on Azure-specific semantics more than necessary.

The architecture strongly leans toward microservices, but Codex may implement early modules as extractable bounded contexts if a startup implementation needs speed. Each module must still have a clear service interface, database boundary, event contract, UI route, test suite, and migration path to independent deployment.


# 4. Module Registry and Deep Functional + Technical Specifications



## M00 - Platform Shell, Tenant Administration, and Configuration Studio

**Product surface:** AURA Core.  
**Domain:** `platform`.  
**Primary promise:** controls every clinic, site, module, rule, release, and configuration surface.

### M00.1 Functional purpose and institutional value
This module exists so that AURA ClinicOS can operationalize controls every clinic, site, module, rule,
release, and configuration surface. It must work for the primary-care reference implementation while also
being configurable for enterprise multispecialty deployment. The module is not a passive dashboard. It is a
production control layer that receives signals, applies rules, coordinates work, generates safe AI support,
records outcomes, and feeds continuous improvement. In the reference clinic, the module must support an NP-led
model with four NPs per site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, a collaborating physician reviewing
charts for three non-autonomous NPs, and a medical director responsible for operational clinical governance.

### M00.2 Users, permissions, and role bundling
Primary personas: NP, MA, front desk, flow captain, clinic manager, medical director, revenue integrity specialist, quality analyst, compliance/privacy lead, patient/caregiver. Small clinics may bundle roles, but the service must still store the true permission source and action provenance. Every screen must show only the minimum data necessary for the user's job. Supervising-physician and medical-director users require separate review, override, and attestation permissions. Administrative configuration requires dual-control for high-risk payer, AI, infection-control, standing-order, and writeback settings.

### M00.3 Inputs and source systems
- EHR/FHIR resources and vendor-specific feeds relevant to tenant, site, configuration, feature_flag, environment.
- Practice-management/scheduling context, appointment metadata, patient demographics, and encounter state.
- Payer, eligibility, authorization, quality, registry, RTLS, sensor, messaging, device, or staff-task inputs when relevant.
- AI/RAG source documents, payer policies, clinic protocols, rule versions, and knowledge-graph evidence.
- User-entered corrections, patient-submitted forms, staff-verified data, and audit annotations.

### M00.4 Outputs and downstream effects
- Updated Visit Readiness Graph components and visible readiness score explanations.
- Role-based work queue tasks, SLA timers, escalation items, and huddle-board exceptions.
- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M00.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to platform shell, tenant administration, and configuration studio, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M00.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M00-01: Create, update, version, and deactivate tenants, sites, service lines, care pods, feature flags, policy bundles, and environment configuration with dual-control approval for high-risk settings.
- FR-M00-02: Resolve the active configuration for every request by tenant, site, module, role bundle, payer, service line, and deployment environment before any workflow decision is made.
- FR-M00-03: Expose implementation wizards for NP-led primary care, physician-owned primary care, and multispecialty enterprise deployments, with the NP-led value-based primary care template enabled as the reference configuration.
- FR-M00-04: Enforce configuration promotion flow from draft to sandbox to approved to active to retired, with effective dates, rollback, impact analysis, and audit trace.
- FR-M00-05: Maintain site-level operating assumptions including four NPs per site, one MA per NP, 30-minute default slots, non-autonomous NP chart-review obligations, and medical-director governance defaults.
- FR-M00-06: Allow role bundling for small clinics while preserving the true permission source and actor provenance for every action.
- FR-M00-07: Surface configuration conflicts that could affect care safety, billing compliance, infection control, AI behavior, or EHR writeback before activation.
- FR-M00-08: Publish configuration.changed and feature_flag.changed events with full before/after diff, actor, approver, and effective timestamp.
- FR-M00-09: Provide configuration export/import and tenant cloning only through signed, auditable packages that exclude PHI unless explicitly authorized.
- FR-M00-10: Block activation of modules with missing RBAC, missing stop-logic policy, missing audit route, or unvalidated integration dependencies.
- FR-M00-11: Support Azure-native deployment metadata for Entra tenant IDs, Key Vault secret references, Event Hub namespaces, managed identity IDs, and data residency region.
- FR-M00-12: Generate configuration documentation for implementation teams and Codex from active policy objects, not from stale prose.
- FR-M00-13: Run automated regression checks on every configuration change using fixture patients for AWV, TCM, chronic follow-up, telehealth, respiratory-risk, and non-autonomous NP chart review.
- FR-M00-14: Expose tenant health indicators for integration connectivity, task queue latency, policy version drift, feature flag state, and audit sink availability.
- FR-M00-15: Persist all configuration objects as immutable versions after approval and prevent destructive deletes of production policy history.
- FR-M00-16: Provide APIs for configuration query, validation, approval, activation, rollback, and export with operation IDs and standard response envelopes.
- FR-M00-17: Fail closed for high-risk modules when active configuration cannot be resolved, except for explicitly configured downtime workflows.

### M00.7 Technical requirements and service design
- NFR-M00-01: P95 interactive API latency for core read operations should be <= 300 ms under expected production load, excluding external EHR/payer calls.
- NFR-M00-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M00-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.
- NFR-M00-04: PHI fields must be minimized in events; sensitive payloads are referenced by secure identifiers where possible.
- NFR-M00-05: The service must emit OpenTelemetry traces, structured logs, domain events, and KPI metrics for each state transition.

Service boundary requirements:
- The module should run as an independently deployable microservice or extractable bounded context.
- Transactional data should be stored in Azure SQL Database or Azure Database for PostgreSQL, according to the deployment's selected standard.
- Event publishing should use Azure Service Bus for command/workflow events and Azure Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry such as RTLS or device streams.
- Durable orchestration should use Temporal or Azure Durable Functions; the reference design uses Temporal for long-running workflows.
- Secrets and connection strings must live in Azure Key Vault; authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities wherever possible.
- Every external call must include correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, timeout, and circuit-breaker behavior.

### M00.8 UI surfaces and component behavior
- module summary card with red/yellow/green risk status
- work queue table with owner, SLA, priority, evidence, and next action
- patient/visit side panel with timeline, source links, and audit trail
- rule-result panel explaining why an action was recommended or blocked
- AI draft panel with source citations, confidence, user approval buttons, and edit history
- configuration page for authorized administrators with versioning and test mode

UI acceptance behavior:
- Red means action is required before safe completion or workflow continuation.
- Yellow means staff can resolve the issue during the current operating window.
- Green means the module has no unresolved readiness issue for the selected context.
- Black means the configured stop logic requires leadership, NP, physician, compliance, or flow-captain decision before proceeding.
- Every AI-generated text block must display source count, confidence level, last refresh time, and approval state.

### M00.9 Data model entities
- platform_tenant: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- platform_site: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- platform_configuration: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- platform_feature_flag: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- platform_environment: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.

Required common fields on all module tables: `id`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`, `row_version`, `source_system`, `source_ref`, `confidence_score`, `audit_hash`, and `metadata_json`.

### M00.10 API contract seeds
- GET /api/v1/aura-core/status?tenantId={tenantId}&siteId={siteId} - returns module health, counts, and risk distribution.
- GET /api/v1/aura-core/visits/{visitId} - returns the module-specific view for a visit.
- POST /api/v1/aura-core/visits/{visitId}/evaluate - runs rules, scoring, and AI-safe evaluation.
- POST /api/v1/aura-core/tasks - creates a module-owned task with SLA, owner, evidence, and escalation path.
- PATCH /api/v1/aura-core/tasks/{taskId} - updates task status, outcome, and audit notes.
- POST /api/v1/aura-core/approvals - records human approval or rejection for medium/high-risk actions.
- GET /api/v1/aura-core/audit?entityId={id} - returns immutable action, source, and user history.

### M00.11 Event contract seeds
- PLATFORM_SHELL_TENANT_AD.EVALUATED.v1
- PLATFORM_SHELL_TENANT_AD.TASK_CREATED.v1
- PLATFORM_SHELL_TENANT_AD.STATE_CHANGED.v1
- PLATFORM_SHELL_TENANT_AD.EXCEPTION_RAISED.v1
- PLATFORM_SHELL_TENANT_AD.APPROVAL_RECORDED.v1
- PLATFORM_SHELL_TENANT_AD.DEFECT_LOGGED.v1

Every event uses the canonical envelope: `event_id`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id_hash`, `visit_id`, `producer`, `event_time`, `trace_id`, `idempotency_key`, `payload`, `sensitivity`, and `retention_class`.

### M00.12 AI, rules, and human-in-the-loop behavior
- Rules engine owns deterministic policy, payer, safety, standing-order, stop-logic, eligibility, SLA, and workflow gating decisions.
- Predictive ML may score risk, delay, no-show, denial, readmission, bottleneck, or readiness likelihood, but cannot itself authorize clinical, billing, or patient financial conclusions.
- LLM/RAG may summarize source material, draft messages, draft huddle items, and generate handoff content only with source links and staff verification.
- Optimization models may recommend room, staff, schedule, task, and equipment actions; medium/high-risk recommendations require approval.
- The module must support a simulation mode where rules and models run without writeback to validate impact and safety.

### M00.13 Stop logic, validation gates, and failure modes
- Stop logic is configurable by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, patient risk, infection-control status, and compliance risk.
- Hard stops block continuation until override; overrides require role, reason, source evidence, timestamp, and post-event review flag.
- Soft stops create visible warnings and tasks but allow flow to continue when configured.
- Failure modes include stale data, duplicate chart, payer ambiguity, external service outage, AI uncertainty, conflicting source records, and staff ownership gap.
- Downtime mode must preserve the minimum paper/PDF or cached workflow packet needed to safely continue clinic operations.

### M00.14 Integrations and FHIR/HL7/X12 mapping
- FHIR mappings should use Patient, Appointment, Encounter, Location, Practitioner, Task, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance, Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response, DocumentReference, DiagnosticReport, ServiceRequest, Procedure, CommunicationRequest, and QuestionnaireResponse as applicable.
- HL7 v2 mappings should support SIU scheduling, ADT, ORU results, ORM/orders, and custom vendor feed fallbacks.
- X12 mappings should include 270/271 eligibility and, where available, 278 prior authorization and 837/835/277CA revenue-cycle signals.
- Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks tracks must map the same canonical contract to vendor-specific endpoints, app launch mechanisms, webhook capabilities, and writeback limits.

### M00.15 Security, privacy, audit, and compliance controls
- Enforce tenant isolation, least privilege, just-in-time elevated access, session timeout, device/location controls where required, and break-glass audit review.
- Log who saw, changed, approved, rejected, exported, or wrote back each object.
- Treat staff location and productivity data as sensitive operational data; default to aggregate analytics unless individual visibility is operationally necessary.
- Prevent AI from exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users by applying authorization before retrieval, not only before display.
- Preserve all compliance evidence needed for billing, quality, infection-control, privacy, and AI governance review.

### M00.16 Analytics, KPIs, and observability
KPIs include completion rate, defect rate, SLA compliance, unresolved red/black items, source freshness, user override rate, AI acceptance rate, false-positive rate, false-negative defect rate, workflow cycle time, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, and equity variance. Observability must include traces, service metrics, domain-event lag, queue depth, retry volume, external-integration failure rate, model latency, and dashboard projection freshness.

### M00.17 Test cases and acceptance criteria
- TC-M00-01: Create a normal Platform Shell, Tenant Administration, and Configuration Studio workflow and verify state, task, event, audit, and readiness score updates.
- TC-M00-02: Inject missing source data and verify exception routing, huddle visibility, and no unsafe writeback.
- TC-M00-03: Simulate external EHR/payer/RTLS failure and verify retry, queueing, fallback UI, and user messaging.
- TC-M00-04: Attempt unauthorized access across roles and tenants and verify Entra/RBAC/ABAC enforcement.
- TC-M00-05: Generate an AI recommendation with low confidence and verify it is labeled, source-linked, and blocked from autonomous execution.
- TC-M00-06: Confirm all generated events exclude unnecessary PHI and include trace_id, tenant_id, entity_id, event_time, and schema_version.
- TC-M00-07: Validate dashboard KPI totals against raw events and service database projections.

Acceptance criteria:
- A user can understand the status of Platform Shell, Tenant Administration, and Configuration Studio for a visit in under 30 seconds without leaving the primary workflow.
- Every action has a named owner, deadline, source evidence, and audit trail.
- The module can operate in demo mode with synthetic EHR, payer, and RTLS fixtures.
- Medium/high-risk actions require approval from the configured role before EHR writeback or patient-facing communication.
- Defects from the module can be logged and routed into the Excellence Loop without manual spreadsheet tracking.

### M00.18 Codex implementation checklist
- Create module package, service interface, database migrations, DTOs, OpenAPI routes, event publishers, repository layer, permission policies, UI routes, shared components, tests, and seed fixtures.
- Implement synthetic fixtures for a Medicare Advantage AWV, TCM visit, chronic-disease follow-up, respiratory-risk same-day visit, telehealth visit, and non-autonomous NP chart-review scenario.
- Include mocked Epic, athenahealth/eClinicalWorks, eligibility, RTLS, SMS, and payment provider adapters.
- Create unit tests for rules, integration tests for API/event behavior, UI tests for role-specific screens, and safety tests for writeback restrictions.
- Ensure the module can be run locally with Docker Compose or dev containers using synthetic data and without real PHI.

### M01.4 Outputs and downstream effects
- Updated Visit Readiness Graph components and visible readiness score explanations.
- Role-based work queue tasks, SLA timers, escalation items, and huddle-board exceptions.
- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M01.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to identity, entra access, rbac/abac, consent, and privacy enforcement, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M01.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M01-01: Authenticate workforce users through Microsoft Entra ID/OIDC and support SMART-on-FHIR launch context without bypassing AURA tenant, site, and role controls.
- FR-M01-02: Authorize every API, screen, event consumption, writeback, AI action, and export through RBAC plus ABAC using tenant, site, care pod, role, relationship-to-patient, sensitivity, and purpose of use.
- FR-M01-03: Maintain separate roles for autonomous NP, non-autonomous NP, supervising physician, medical director, MA, front desk, revenue integrity, quality, infection control, compliance, administrator, and support.
- FR-M01-04: Bundle roles for small clinics without losing the underlying permission grants, delegated authority, supervision source, or action provenance.
- FR-M01-05: Capture patient consent, communication preferences, caregiver/guardian permissions, financial communication consent, telehealth consent, care-management consent, and research/analytics exclusions where applicable.
- FR-M01-06: Enforce minimum-necessary data presentation by screen, including PHI masking, sensitive-note restrictions, staff-location privacy, and restricted financial views.
- FR-M01-07: Require step-up authentication or dual approval for payer rule activation, standing-order policy changes, AI model deployment, bulk export, and high-risk EHR writeback.
- FR-M01-08: Log view, create, update, approve, deny, export, AI invocation, and break-glass events with actor, reason, source IP/device, correlation ID, patient/visit context, and policy decision.
- FR-M01-09: Provide break-glass access only with required reason, time-boxed access, compliance notification, and retrospective review queue.
- FR-M01-10: Block patient-context access when no treatment, payment, operations, delegated, or authorized relationship can be established.
- FR-M01-11: Integrate with Azure Key Vault and managed identities for service-to-service authentication and secret rotation.
- FR-M01-12: Provide consent-aware patient messaging and prevent SMS/email transmission of content classified as not permitted for the selected channel.
- FR-M01-13: Publish access.decision, consent.changed, breakglass.opened, and policy.denied events to audit and analytics services.
- FR-M01-14: Expose security posture dashboards for failed logins, suspicious access, excessive exports, break-glass usage, stale accounts, and policy-denied trends.
- FR-M01-15: Support SCIM or equivalent user provisioning and deprovisioning with disabled-user enforcement across sessions and API tokens.
- FR-M01-16: Provide unit, integration, and red-team test fixtures for role bundling, supervision, break glass, PHI masking, delegated chart review, and patient messaging.
- FR-M01-17: Deny by default when identity, tenant, site, patient relationship, consent, or policy context is incomplete.

### M01.7 Technical requirements and service design
- NFR-M01-01: P95 interactive API latency for core read operations should be <= 300 ms under expected production load, excluding external EHR/payer calls.
- NFR-M01-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M01-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.
- NFR-M01-04: PHI fields must be minimized in events; sensitive payloads are referenced by secure identifiers where possible.
- NFR-M01-05: The service must emit OpenTelemetry traces, structured logs, domain events, and KPI metrics for each state transition.

Service boundary requirements:
- The module should run as an independently deployable microservice or extractable bounded context.
- Transactional data should be stored in Azure SQL Database or Azure Database for PostgreSQL, according to the deployment's selected standard.
- Event publishing should use Azure Service Bus for command/workflow events and Azure Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry such as RTLS or device streams.
- Durable orchestration should use Temporal or Azure Durable Functions; the reference design uses Temporal for long-running workflows.
- Secrets and connection strings must live in Azure Key Vault; authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities wherever possible.
- Every external call must include correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, timeout, and circuit-breaker behavior.

### M01.8 UI surfaces and component behavior
- module summary card with red/yellow/green risk status
- work queue table with owner, SLA, priority, evidence, and next action
- patient/visit side panel with timeline, source links, and audit trail
- rule-result panel explaining why an action was recommended or blocked
- AI draft panel with source citations, confidence, user approval buttons, and edit history
- configuration page for authorized administrators with versioning and test mode

UI acceptance behavior:
- Red means action is required before safe completion or workflow continuation.
- Yellow means staff can resolve the issue during the current operating window.
- Green means the module has no unresolved readiness issue for the selected context.
- Black means the configured stop logic requires leadership, NP, physician, compliance, or flow-captain decision before proceeding.
- Every AI-generated text block must display source count, confidence level, last refresh time, and approval state.

- security_role: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- security_permission: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- security_policy: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- security_consent: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- security_audit_log: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.

Required common fields on all module tables: `id`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`, `row_version`, `source_system`, `source_ref`, `confidence_score`, `audit_hash`, and `metadata_json`.

### M01.10 API contract seeds
- GET /api/v1/aura-identity/status?tenantId={tenantId}&siteId={siteId} - returns module health, counts, and risk distribution.
- GET /api/v1/aura-identity/visits/{visitId} - returns the module-specific view for a visit.
- POST /api/v1/aura-identity/visits/{visitId}/evaluate - runs rules, scoring, and AI-safe evaluation.
- POST /api/v1/aura-identity/tasks - creates a module-owned task with SLA, owner, evidence, and escalation path.
- PATCH /api/v1/aura-identity/tasks/{taskId} - updates task status, outcome, and audit notes.
- POST /api/v1/aura-identity/approvals - records human approval or rejection for medium/high-risk actions.
- GET /api/v1/aura-identity/audit?entityId={id} - returns immutable action, source, and user history.

### M01.11 Event contract seeds
- IDENTITY_ENTRA_ACCESS_RB.EVALUATED.v1
- IDENTITY_ENTRA_ACCESS_RB.TASK_CREATED.v1
- IDENTITY_ENTRA_ACCESS_RB.STATE_CHANGED.v1
- IDENTITY_ENTRA_ACCESS_RB.EXCEPTION_RAISED.v1
- IDENTITY_ENTRA_ACCESS_RB.APPROVAL_RECORDED.v1
- IDENTITY_ENTRA_ACCESS_RB.DEFECT_LOGGED.v1

Every event uses the canonical envelope: `event_id`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id_hash`, `visit_id`, `producer`, `event_time`, `trace_id`, `idempotency_key`, `payload`, `sensitivity`, and `retention_class`.

### M01.12 AI, rules, and human-in-the-loop behavior
- Rules engine owns deterministic policy, payer, safety, standing-order, stop-logic, eligibility, SLA, and workflow gating decisions.
- Predictive ML may score risk, delay, no-show, denial, readmission, bottleneck, or readiness likelihood, but cannot itself authorize clinical, billing, or patient financial conclusions.
- LLM/RAG may summarize source material, draft messages, draft huddle items, and generate handoff content only with source links and staff verification.
- Optimization models may recommend room, staff, schedule, task, and equipment actions; medium/high-risk recommendations require approval.
- The module must support a simulation mode where rules and models run without writeback to validate impact and safety.

### M01.13 Stop logic, validation gates, and failure modes
- Stop logic is configurable by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, patient risk, infection-control status, and compliance risk.
- Hard stops block continuation until override; overrides require role, reason, source evidence, timestamp, and post-event review flag.
- Soft stops create visible warnings and tasks but allow flow to continue when configured.
- Failure modes include stale data, duplicate chart, payer ambiguity, external service outage, AI uncertainty, conflicting source records, and staff ownership gap.
- Downtime mode must preserve the minimum paper/PDF or cached workflow packet needed to safely continue clinic operations.

### M01.14 Integrations and FHIR/HL7/X12 mapping
- FHIR mappings should use Patient, Appointment, Encounter, Location, Practitioner, Task, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance, Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response, DocumentReference, DiagnosticReport, ServiceRequest, Procedure, CommunicationRequest, and QuestionnaireResponse as applicable.
- HL7 v2 mappings should support SIU scheduling, ADT, ORU results, ORM/orders, and custom vendor feed fallbacks.
- X12 mappings should include 270/271 eligibility and, where available, 278 prior authorization and 837/835/277CA revenue-cycle signals.
- Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks tracks must map the same canonical contract to vendor-specific endpoints, app launch mechanisms, webhook capabilities, and writeback limits.

### M01.15 Security, privacy, audit, and compliance controls
- Enforce tenant isolation, least privilege, just-in-time elevated access, session timeout, device/location controls where required, and break-glass audit review.
- Log who saw, changed, approved, rejected, exported, or wrote back each object.
- Treat staff location and productivity data as sensitive operational data; default to aggregate analytics unless individual visibility is operationally necessary.
- Prevent AI from exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users by applying authorization before retrieval, not only before display.
- Preserve all compliance evidence needed for billing, quality, infection-control, privacy, and AI governance review.

### M01.16 Analytics, KPIs, and observability
KPIs include completion rate, defect rate, SLA compliance, unresolved red/black items, source freshness, user override rate, AI acceptance rate, false-positive rate, false-negative defect rate, workflow cycle time, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, and equity variance. Observability must include traces, service metrics, domain-event lag, queue depth, retry volume, external-integration failure rate, model latency, and dashboard projection freshness.

### M01.17 Test cases and acceptance criteria
- TC-M01-01: Create a normal Identity, Entra Access, RBAC/ABAC, Consent, and Privacy Enforcement workflow and verify state, task, event, audit, and readiness score updates.
- TC-M01-02: Inject missing source data and verify exception routing, huddle visibility, and no unsafe writeback.
- TC-M01-03: Simulate external EHR/payer/RTLS failure and verify retry, queueing, fallback UI, and user messaging.
- TC-M01-04: Attempt unauthorized access across roles and tenants and verify Entra/RBAC/ABAC enforcement.
- TC-M01-05: Generate an AI recommendation with low confidence and verify it is labeled, source-linked, and blocked from autonomous execution.
- TC-M01-06: Confirm all generated events exclude unnecessary PHI and include trace_id, tenant_id, entity_id, event_time, and schema_version.
- TC-M01-07: Validate dashboard KPI totals against raw events and service database projections.

Acceptance criteria:
- A user can understand the status of Identity, Entra Access, RBAC/ABAC, Consent, and Privacy Enforcement for a visit in under 30 seconds without leaving the primary workflow.
- Every action has a named owner, deadline, source evidence, and audit trail.
- The module can operate in demo mode with synthetic EHR, payer, and RTLS fixtures.
- Medium/high-risk actions require approval from the configured role before EHR writeback or patient-facing communication.
- Defects from the module can be logged and routed into the Excellence Loop without manual spreadsheet tracking.

### M01.18 Codex implementation checklist
- Create module package, service interface, database migrations, DTOs, OpenAPI routes, event publishers, repository layer, permission policies, UI routes, shared components, tests, and seed fixtures.
- Implement synthetic fixtures for a Medicare Advantage AWV, TCM visit, chronic-disease follow-up, respiratory-risk same-day visit, telehealth visit, and non-autonomous NP chart-review scenario.
- Include mocked Epic, athenahealth/eClinicalWorks, eligibility, RTLS, SMS, and payment provider adapters.
- Create unit tests for rules, integration tests for API/event behavior, UI tests for role-specific screens, and safety tests for writeback restrictions.
- Ensure the module can be run locally with Docker Compose or dev containers using synthetic data and without real PHI.



## M02 - Clinic Digital Twin and RTLS Fusion Engine

**Product surface:** AURA Flow.  
**Domain:** `flow`.  
**Primary promise:** turns real-time location and sensor signals into an operational digital twin.

### M02.1 Functional purpose and institutional value
This module exists so that AURA ClinicOS can operationalize turns real-time location and sensor signals into
an operational digital twin. It must work for the primary-care reference implementation while also being
configurable for enterprise multispecialty deployment. The module is not a passive dashboard. It is a
production control layer that receives signals, applies rules, coordinates work, generates safe AI support,
records outcomes, and feeds continuous improvement. In the reference clinic, the module must support an NP-led
model with four NPs per site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, a collaborating physician reviewing
charts for three non-autonomous NPs, and a medical director responsible for operational clinical governance.

### M02.2 Users, permissions, and role bundling
Primary personas: NP, MA, front desk, flow captain, clinic manager, medical director, revenue integrity specialist, quality analyst, compliance/privacy lead, patient/caregiver. Small clinics may bundle roles, but the service must still store the true permission source and action provenance. Every screen must show only the minimum data necessary for the user's job. Supervising-physician and medical-director users require separate review, override, and attestation permissions. Administrative configuration requires dual-control for high-risk payer, AI, infection-control, standing-order, and writeback settings.

### M02.3 Inputs and source systems
- EHR/FHIR resources and vendor-specific feeds relevant to location_ping, zone, room, asset, badge, occupancy_state.
- Practice-management/scheduling context, appointment metadata, patient demographics, and encounter state.
- Payer, eligibility, authorization, quality, registry, RTLS, sensor, messaging, device, or staff-task inputs when relevant.
- AI/RAG source documents, payer policies, clinic protocols, rule versions, and knowledge-graph evidence.
- User-entered corrections, patient-submitted forms, staff-verified data, and audit annotations.

### M02.4 Outputs and downstream effects
- Updated Visit Readiness Graph components and visible readiness score explanations.
- Role-based work queue tasks, SLA timers, escalation items, and huddle-board exceptions.
- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M02.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to clinic digital twin and rtls fusion engine, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M02.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M02-01: Ingest RTLS pings from hybrid BLE/UWB adapters and normalize badge, wristband, phone, asset tag, anchor, room, zone, and timestamp signals into a canonical location stream.
- FR-M02-02: Compute patient, staff, equipment, and room state with confidence scores, smoothing, stale-signal detection, duplicate suppression, and vendor-specific adapter isolation.
- FR-M02-03: Distinguish room-level, bay-level, chair-level, zone-level, and sub-room precision and never present higher precision than the hardware confidence supports.
- FR-M02-04: Maintain a live clinic digital twin of rooms, waiting areas, clinical pods, procedure spaces, infusion/chair areas, lab areas, clean/dirty status, staff load, patient state, and equipment availability.
- FR-M02-05: Infer patient-flow milestones such as arrived, waiting, called, roomed, provider-in-room, procedure-in-progress, checkout, discharged, and room-vacated using RTLS plus EHR/PM/task signals.
- FR-M02-06: Protect staff privacy by supporting aggregate-only analytics, restricted individual lookup, purpose-of-use logging, and configurable staff-location retention windows.
- FR-M02-07: Publish location.updated, room.occupied, room.vacated, equipment.available, equipment.missing, staff.zone.changed, and rtls.signal.stale events.
- FR-M02-08: Feed Flow Command Center, InfectionShield, AssetOps, Charge Integrity, and Visit Readiness Graph without using RTLS alone to bill, discipline staff, or make clinical decisions.
- FR-M02-09: Validate RTLS-derived state transitions against EHR/PM/task signals and route low-confidence or contradictory signals to exception queues.
- FR-M02-10: Provide an RTLS simulation harness for Codex and QA to replay clinic days, late arrivals, respiratory-risk direct rooming, dirty-room block, and equipment search scenarios.
- FR-M02-11: Expose heat maps, room utilization, search, dwell-time analytics, bottleneck sources, and device health without exposing unnecessary PHI.
- FR-M02-12: Support edge gateway buffering and replay when network connectivity is degraded, preserving event order and idempotency keys.
- FR-M02-13: Allow site-specific calibration, zone maps, room aliases, anchor inventory, signal quality thresholds, and device assignment workflows.
- FR-M02-14: Block the optimizer from assigning a room when RTLS says vacant but InfectionShield says not clean or unavailable.
- FR-M02-15: Store raw pings separately from operational state, with shorter retention for raw location data and longer retention for derived audit-relevant events.
- FR-M02-16: Provide APIs for location ingestion, state query, digital twin query, device assignment, calibration, and RTLS event replay.
- FR-M02-17: Fail safely by falling back to manual room board and task state when RTLS confidence is below threshold or gateway connectivity is down.

### M02.7 Technical requirements and service design
- NFR-M02-01: P95 interactive API latency for core read operations should be <= 300 ms under expected production load, excluding external EHR/payer calls.
- NFR-M02-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M02-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.

- NFR-M02-05: The service must emit OpenTelemetry traces, structured logs, domain events, and KPI metrics for each state transition.

- Event publishing should use Azure Service Bus for command/workflow events and Azure Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry such as RTLS or device streams.
- Durable orchestration should use Temporal or Azure Durable Functions; the reference design uses Temporal for long-running workflows.
- Secrets and connection strings must live in Azure Key Vault; authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities wherever possible.
- Every external call must include correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, timeout, and circuit-breaker behavior.

## M03 - Visit Readiness Graph and Shared Encounter State

**Product surface:** AURA VisitGraph.  
**Domain:** `core`.  
**Primary promise:** keeps every visit's clinical, financial, quality, flow, and infection status synchronized.

### M03.1 Functional purpose and institutional value
This module exists so that AURA ClinicOS can operationalize keeps every visit's clinical, financial, quality,
flow, and infection status synchronized. It must work for the primary-care reference implementation while also
being configurable for enterprise multispecialty deployment. The module is not a passive dashboard. It is a
production control layer that receives signals, applies rules, coordinates work, generates safe AI support,
records outcomes, and feeds continuous improvement. In the reference clinic, the module must support an NP-led
model with four NPs per site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, a collaborating physician reviewing
charts for three non-autonomous NPs, and a medical director responsible for operational clinical governance.

### M03.2 Users, permissions, and role bundling
Primary personas: NP, MA, front desk, flow captain, clinic manager, medical director, revenue integrity specialist, quality analyst, compliance/privacy lead, patient/caregiver. Small clinics may bundle roles, but the service must still store the true permission source and action provenance. Every screen must show only the minimum data necessary for the user's job. Supervising-physician and medical-director users require separate review, override, and attestation permissions. Administrative configuration requires dual-control for high-risk payer, AI, infection-control, standing-order, and writeback settings.

### M03.3 Inputs and source systems
- EHR/FHIR resources and vendor-specific feeds relevant to visit, readiness_score, readiness_component, visit_state, evidence_link.
- Practice-management/scheduling context, appointment metadata, patient demographics, and encounter state.
- Payer, eligibility, authorization, quality, registry, RTLS, sensor, messaging, device, or staff-task inputs when relevant.
- AI/RAG source documents, payer policies, clinic protocols, rule versions, and knowledge-graph evidence.
- User-entered corrections, patient-submitted forms, staff-verified data, and audit annotations.

### M03.4 Outputs and downstream effects
- Updated Visit Readiness Graph components and visible readiness score explanations.
- Role-based work queue tasks, SLA timers, escalation items, and huddle-board exceptions.
- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M03.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to visit readiness graph and shared encounter state, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M03.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M03-01: Maintain the canonical Visit Readiness Graph linking patient, appointment, encounter, NP, MA, room, payer, eligibility, authorization, forms, records, medications, quality gaps, infection status, tasks, and handoff.
- FR-M03-02: Calculate dissectible readiness scores by domain, component, evidence, owner, source, confidence, and stop-logic effect rather than a single opaque number.
- FR-M03-03: Apply dynamic weighting by visit type: AWV, TCM, chronic-disease follow-up, urgent/same-day, procedure, vaccine, injection, spirometry, RPM setup, telehealth, preventive plus E/M, and routine follow-up.
- FR-M03-04: Produce green/yellow/red/black readiness labels using configurable stop logic by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, infection-control risk, supervision requirement, and compliance risk.
- FR-M03-05: Expose graph changes to every role-specific cockpit while showing each user only the nodes and actions allowed by RBAC/ABAC and minimum-necessary policy.
- FR-M03-06: Integrate signals from PreVisit, Access, FrontDesk, Records, Medication Sentinel, RevCycle, Auth, QualityGuard, InfectionShield, CareOps, Rooming, Flow, and Charge Integrity.
- FR-M03-07: Require every readiness component to carry source links, freshness, owner, SLA, confidence, and rationale so Codex never infers missing evidence.
- FR-M03-08: Publish readiness.score.changed, readiness.locked, stoplogic.blocked, evidence.updated, and visit.graph.changed events.
- FR-M03-09: Provide graph APIs for query by patient, visit, schedule day, domain, status, owner, and huddle risk.
- FR-M03-10: Prevent writes that would mark a domain complete without required evidence, source link, staff verification, or approved exception reason.
- FR-M03-11: Preserve readiness history snapshots at scheduling, 7 days, 48 hours, 24 hours, huddle, check-in, rooming, NP entry, checkout, and claim-readiness.
- FR-M03-12: Generate root-cause signals when a readiness defect appears after NP entry or after claim submission.
- FR-M03-13: Support external graph export only through privacy-reviewed deidentified analytics or authorized patient/operations exports.
- FR-M03-14: Provide UI drill-down from score to component to task to source document to responsible owner to last action.
- FR-M03-15: Run graph reconciliation jobs that detect orphan tasks, stale forms, missing appointments, duplicate charts, and conflicting payer states.
- FR-M03-16: Provide deterministic fixture outputs for Codex for at least AWV, TCM, chronic, telehealth, respiratory-risk, procedure, RPM, and non-autonomous NP chart-review scenarios.
- FR-M03-17: Deny black-to-green transitions unless the blocking issue has an approved resolution, exception, or documented NP/leadership decision.

### M03.7 Technical requirements and service design
- NFR-M03-01: P95 interactive API latency for core read operations should be <= 300 ms under expected production load, excluding external EHR/payer calls.
- NFR-M03-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M03-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.
- NFR-M03-04: PHI fields must be minimized in events; sensitive payloads are referenced by secure identifiers where possible.
- NFR-M03-05: The service must emit OpenTelemetry traces, structured logs, domain events, and KPI metrics for each state transition.

Service boundary requirements:
- The module should run as an independently deployable microservice or extractable bounded context.
- Transactional data should be stored in Azure SQL Database or Azure Database for PostgreSQL, according to the deployment's selected standard.
- Event publishing should use Azure Service Bus for command/workflow events and Azure Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry such as RTLS or device streams.
- Durable orchestration should use Temporal or Azure Durable Functions; the reference design uses Temporal for long-running workflows.
- Secrets and connection strings must live in Azure Key Vault; authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities wherever possible.
- Every external call must include correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, timeout, and circuit-breaker behavior.

### M03.8 UI surfaces and component behavior
- module summary card with red/yellow/green risk status
- work queue table with owner, SLA, priority, evidence, and next action
- patient/visit side panel with timeline, source links, and audit trail
- rule-result panel explaining why an action was recommended or blocked
- AI draft panel with source citations, confidence, user approval buttons, and edit history
- configuration page for authorized administrators with versioning and test mode

UI acceptance behavior:
- Red means action is required before safe completion or workflow continuation.
- Yellow means staff can resolve the issue during the current operating window.
- Green means the module has no unresolved readiness issue for the selected context.
- Black means the configured stop logic requires leadership, NP, physician, compliance, or flow-captain decision before proceeding.
- Every AI-generated text block must display source count, confidence level, last refresh time, and approval state.

### M03.9 Data model entities
- core_visit: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- core_readiness_score: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- core_readiness_component: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- core_visit_state: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- core_evidence_link: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.

Required common fields on all module tables: `id`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`, `row_version`, `source_system`, `source_ref`, `confidence_score`, `audit_hash`, and `metadata_json`.

### M03.10 API contract seeds
- GET /api/v1/aura-visitgraph/status?tenantId={tenantId}&siteId={siteId} - returns module health, counts, and risk distribution.
- GET /api/v1/aura-visitgraph/visits/{visitId} - returns the module-specific view for a visit.
- POST /api/v1/aura-visitgraph/visits/{visitId}/evaluate - runs rules, scoring, and AI-safe evaluation.
- POST /api/v1/aura-visitgraph/tasks - creates a module-owned task with SLA, owner, evidence, and escalation path.
- PATCH /api/v1/aura-visitgraph/tasks/{taskId} - updates task status, outcome, and audit notes.
- POST /api/v1/aura-visitgraph/approvals - records human approval or rejection for medium/high-risk actions.
- GET /api/v1/aura-visitgraph/audit?entityId={id} - returns immutable action, source, and user history.

### M03.11 Event contract seeds
- VISIT_READINESS_GRAPH_AN.EVALUATED.v1
- VISIT_READINESS_GRAPH_AN.TASK_CREATED.v1
- VISIT_READINESS_GRAPH_AN.STATE_CHANGED.v1
- VISIT_READINESS_GRAPH_AN.EXCEPTION_RAISED.v1
- VISIT_READINESS_GRAPH_AN.APPROVAL_RECORDED.v1
- VISIT_READINESS_GRAPH_AN.DEFECT_LOGGED.v1

Every event uses the canonical envelope: `event_id`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id_hash`, `visit_id`, `producer`, `event_time`, `trace_id`, `idempotency_key`, `payload`, `sensitivity`, and `retention_class`.

### M03.12 AI, rules, and human-in-the-loop behavior
- Rules engine owns deterministic policy, payer, safety, standing-order, stop-logic, eligibility, SLA, and workflow gating decisions.
- Predictive ML may score risk, delay, no-show, denial, readmission, bottleneck, or readiness likelihood, but cannot itself authorize clinical, billing, or patient financial conclusions.
- LLM/RAG may summarize source material, draft messages, draft huddle items, and generate handoff content only with source links and staff verification.
- Optimization models may recommend room, staff, schedule, task, and equipment actions; medium/high-risk recommendations require approval.
- The module must support a simulation mode where rules and models run without writeback to validate impact and safety.

### M03.13 Stop logic, validation gates, and failure modes
- Stop logic is configurable by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, patient risk, infection-control status, and compliance risk.
- Hard stops block continuation until override; overrides require role, reason, source evidence, timestamp, and post-event review flag.
- Soft stops create visible warnings and tasks but allow flow to continue when configured.
- Failure modes include stale data, duplicate chart, payer ambiguity, external service outage, AI uncertainty, conflicting source records, and staff ownership gap.
- Downtime mode must preserve the minimum paper/PDF or cached workflow packet needed to safely continue clinic operations.

### M03.14 Integrations and FHIR/HL7/X12 mapping
- FHIR mappings should use Patient, Appointment, Encounter, Location, Practitioner, Task, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance, Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response, DocumentReference, DiagnosticReport, ServiceRequest, Procedure, CommunicationRequest, and QuestionnaireResponse as applicable.
- HL7 v2 mappings should support SIU scheduling, ADT, ORU results, ORM/orders, and custom vendor feed fallbacks.
- X12 mappings should include 270/271 eligibility and, where available, 278 prior authorization and 837/835/277CA revenue-cycle signals.
- Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks tracks must map the same canonical contract to vendor-specific endpoints, app launch mechanisms, webhook capabilities, and writeback limits.

### M03.15 Security, privacy, audit, and compliance controls
- Enforce tenant isolation, least privilege, just-in-time elevated access, session timeout, device/location controls where required, and break-glass audit review.
- Log who saw, changed, approved, rejected, exported, or wrote back each object.
- Treat staff location and productivity data as sensitive operational data; default to aggregate analytics unless individual visibility is operationally necessary.
- Prevent AI from exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users by applying authorization before retrieval, not only before display.
- Preserve all compliance evidence needed for billing, quality, infection-control, privacy, and AI governance review.

### M03.16 Analytics, KPIs, and observability
KPIs include completion rate, defect rate, SLA compliance, unresolved red/black items, source freshness, user override rate, AI acceptance rate, false-positive rate, false-negative defect rate, workflow cycle time, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, and equity variance. Observability must include traces, service metrics, domain-event lag, queue depth, retry volume, external-integration failure rate, model latency, and dashboard projection freshness.

### M03.17 Test cases and acceptance criteria
- TC-M03-01: Create a normal Visit Readiness Graph and Shared Encounter State workflow and verify state, task, event, audit, and readiness score updates.
- TC-M03-02: Inject missing source data and verify exception routing, huddle visibility, and no unsafe writeback.
- TC-M03-03: Simulate external EHR/payer/RTLS failure and verify retry, queueing, fallback UI, and user messaging.
- TC-M03-04: Attempt unauthorized access across roles and tenants and verify Entra/RBAC/ABAC enforcement.
- TC-M03-05: Generate an AI recommendation with low confidence and verify it is labeled, source-linked, and blocked from autonomous execution.
- TC-M03-06: Confirm all generated events exclude unnecessary PHI and include trace_id, tenant_id, entity_id, event_time, and schema_version.
- TC-M03-07: Validate dashboard KPI totals against raw events and service database projections.

Acceptance criteria:
- A user can understand the status of Visit Readiness Graph and Shared Encounter State for a visit in under 30 seconds without leaving the primary workflow.
- Every action has a named owner, deadline, source evidence, and audit trail.
- The module can operate in demo mode with synthetic EHR, payer, and RTLS fixtures.
- Medium/high-risk actions require approval from the configured role before EHR writeback or patient-facing communication.
- Defects from the module can be logged and routed into the Excellence Loop without manual spreadsheet tracking.

### M03.18 Codex implementation checklist
- Create module package, service interface, database migrations, DTOs, OpenAPI routes, event publishers, repository layer, permission policies, UI routes, shared components, tests, and seed fixtures.
- Implement synthetic fixtures for a Medicare Advantage AWV, TCM visit, chronic-disease follow-up, respiratory-risk same-day visit, telehealth visit, and non-autonomous NP chart-review scenario.
- Include mocked Epic, athenahealth/eClinicalWorks, eligibility, RTLS, SMS, and payment provider adapters.
- Create unit tests for rules, integration tests for API/event behavior, UI tests for role-specific screens, and safety tests for writeback restrictions.
- Ensure the module can be run locally with Docker Compose or dev containers using synthetic data and without real PHI.
