- Hard stops block continuation until override; overrides require role, reason, source evidence, timestamp, and post-event review flag.
- Soft stops create visible warnings and tasks but allow flow to continue when configured.
- Failure modes include stale data, duplicate chart, payer ambiguity, external service outage, AI uncertainty, conflicting source records, and staff ownership gap.
- Downtime mode must preserve the minimum paper/PDF or cached workflow packet needed to safely continue clinic operations.

### M04.14 Integrations and FHIR/HL7/X12 mapping
- FHIR mappings should use Patient, Appointment, Encounter, Location, Practitioner, Task, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance, Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response, DocumentReference, DiagnosticReport, ServiceRequest, Procedure, CommunicationRequest, and QuestionnaireResponse as applicable.
- HL7 v2 mappings should support SIU scheduling, ADT, ORU results, ORM/orders, and custom vendor feed fallbacks.
- X12 mappings should include 270/271 eligibility and, where available, 278 prior authorization and 837/835/277CA revenue-cycle signals.
- Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks tracks must map the same canonical contract to vendor-specific endpoints, app launch mechanisms, webhook capabilities, and writeback limits.

### M04.15 Security, privacy, audit, and compliance controls
- Enforce tenant isolation, least privilege, just-in-time elevated access, session timeout, device/location controls where required, and break-glass audit review.
- Log who saw, changed, approved, rejected, exported, or wrote back each object.
- Treat staff location and productivity data as sensitive operational data; default to aggregate analytics unless individual visibility is operationally necessary.
- Prevent AI from exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users by applying authorization before retrieval, not only before display.
- Preserve all compliance evidence needed for billing, quality, infection-control, privacy, and AI governance review.

### M04.16 Analytics, KPIs, and observability
KPIs include completion rate, defect rate, SLA compliance, unresolved red/black items, source freshness, user override rate, AI acceptance rate, false-positive rate, false-negative defect rate, workflow cycle time, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, and equity variance. Observability must include traces, service metrics, domain-event lag, queue depth, retry volume, external-integration failure rate, model latency, and dashboard projection freshness.

### M04.17 Test cases and acceptance criteria
- TC-M04-01: Create a normal Event Fabric, Workflow Engine, Task Orchestration, and Work Queues workflow and verify state, task, event, audit, and readiness score updates.
- TC-M04-02: Inject missing source data and verify exception routing, huddle visibility, and no unsafe writeback.
- TC-M04-03: Simulate external EHR/payer/RTLS failure and verify retry, queueing, fallback UI, and user messaging.
- TC-M04-04: Attempt unauthorized access across roles and tenants and verify Entra/RBAC/ABAC enforcement.
- TC-M04-05: Generate an AI recommendation with low confidence and verify it is labeled, source-linked, and blocked from autonomous execution.
- TC-M04-06: Confirm all generated events exclude unnecessary PHI and include trace_id, tenant_id, entity_id, event_time, and schema_version.
- TC-M04-07: Validate dashboard KPI totals against raw events and service database projections.

Acceptance criteria:
- A user can understand the status of Event Fabric, Workflow Engine, Task Orchestration, and Work Queues for a visit in under 30 seconds without leaving the primary workflow.
- Every action has a named owner, deadline, source evidence, and audit trail.
- The module can operate in demo mode with synthetic EHR, payer, and RTLS fixtures.
- Medium/high-risk actions require approval from the configured role before EHR writeback or patient-facing communication.
- Defects from the module can be logged and routed into the Excellence Loop without manual spreadsheet tracking.

### M04.18 Codex implementation checklist
- Create module package, service interface, database migrations, DTOs, OpenAPI routes, event publishers, repository layer, permission policies, UI routes, shared components, tests, and seed fixtures.
- Implement synthetic fixtures for a Medicare Advantage AWV, TCM visit, chronic-disease follow-up, respiratory-risk same-day visit, telehealth visit, and non-autonomous NP chart-review scenario.
- Include mocked Epic, athenahealth/eClinicalWorks, eligibility, RTLS, SMS, and payment provider adapters.
- Create unit tests for rules, integration tests for API/event behavior, UI tests for role-specific screens, and safety tests for writeback restrictions.
- Ensure the module can be run locally with Docker Compose or dev containers using synthetic data and without real PHI.



## M05 - Panel Intelligence and Proactive Outreach Engine

**Product surface:** AURA Panel.  
**Domain:** `population_health`.  
**Primary promise:** turns a passive panel into proactive quality, access, and revenue opportunities.

### M05.1 Functional purpose and institutional value
This module exists so that AURA ClinicOS can operationalize turns a passive panel into proactive quality,
access, and revenue opportunities. It must work for the primary-care reference implementation while also being
configurable for enterprise multispecialty deployment. The module is not a passive dashboard. It is a
production control layer that receives signals, applies rules, coordinates work, generates safe AI support,
records outcomes, and feeds continuous improvement. In the reference clinic, the module must support an NP-led
model with four NPs per site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, a collaborating physician reviewing
charts for three non-autonomous NPs, and a medical director responsible for operational clinical governance.

### M05.2 Users, permissions, and role bundling
Primary personas: NP, MA, front desk, flow captain, clinic manager, medical director, revenue integrity specialist, quality analyst, compliance/privacy lead, patient/caregiver. Small clinics may bundle roles, but the service must still store the true permission source and action provenance. Every screen must show only the minimum data necessary for the user's job. Supervising-physician and medical-director users require separate review, override, and attestation permissions. Administrative configuration requires dual-control for high-risk payer, AI, infection-control, standing-order, and writeback settings.

### M05.3 Inputs and source systems
- EHR/FHIR resources and vendor-specific feeds relevant to panel_member, risk_tier, outreach_campaign, care_gap, outreach_attempt.
- Practice-management/scheduling context, appointment metadata, patient demographics, and encounter state.
- Payer, eligibility, authorization, quality, registry, RTLS, sensor, messaging, device, or staff-task inputs when relevant.
- AI/RAG source documents, payer policies, clinic protocols, rule versions, and knowledge-graph evidence.
- User-entered corrections, patient-submitted forms, staff-verified data, and audit annotations.

### M05.4 Outputs and downstream effects
- Updated Visit Readiness Graph components and visible readiness score explanations.
- Role-based work queue tasks, SLA timers, escalation items, and huddle-board exceptions.
- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M05.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to panel intelligence and proactive outreach engine, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M05.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M05-01: Continuously scan panels for patients due, overdue, high-risk, recently discharged, quality-gap eligible, medication-adherence risk, high ED utilization, chronic-disease instability, or care-management opportunity.
- FR-M05-02: Prioritize outreach by clinical risk, value-based impact, quality gap, patient preference, access urgency, no-show risk, social barrier, and capacity availability.
- FR-M05-03: Generate outreach worklists for AWV, chronic follow-up, TCM, uncontrolled hypertension, diabetes monitoring, kidney monitoring, depression follow-up, immunizations, screenings, and missed specialist follow-up.
- FR-M05-04: Use claims, EHR, HIE/ADT, lab, medication, payer quality, and patient engagement data while tracking data freshness and source confidence.
- FR-M05-05: Route outreach to SMS, web, phone, portal, mail, caregiver, interpreter-assisted call, CHW, or care manager based on patient preferences and barriers.
- FR-M05-06: Create scheduling recommendations including visit type, modality, slot length, assigned NP/care pod, interpreter need, forms, and pre-visit workstream.
- FR-M05-07: Generate patient-friendly outreach scripts but require staff approval for sensitive clinical, financial, or behavioral-health messages.
- FR-M05-08: Publish panel.member.flagged, outreach.campaign.created, outreach.sent, outreach.responded, and panel.priority.changed events.
- FR-M05-09: Expose dashboards for recall completion, gap closure, no-show risk reduction, outreach response, equity barriers, and payer quality opportunity.
- FR-M05-10: Prevent outreach that conflicts with consent, communication preference, do-not-contact status, patient safety flags, or payer-specific restrictions.
- FR-M05-11: Support campaign configuration by payer, contract, measure, condition, site, NP panel, social-risk tier, and access capacity.
- FR-M05-12: Allow leadership to protect capacity for TCM, AWV, chronic-care, and high-risk follow-up instead of filling all slots with low-complexity visits.
- FR-M05-13: Link every outreach to a measurable downstream outcome: scheduled visit, gap closed, care-management enrollment, medication issue resolved, or barrier addressed.
- FR-M05-14: Maintain no-blame defect tracking when an eligible patient was missed or outreach created patient confusion.
- FR-M05-15: Provide APIs for panel cohort query, campaign creation, outreach assignment, response ingestion, and recommendation explainability.
- FR-M05-16: Deidentify population analytics where patient-level drill-down is not required for operations.
- FR-M05-17: Fail safely by routing ambiguous outreach candidates to human review rather than sending autonomous clinical or financial communications.

### M05.7 Technical requirements and service design
- NFR-M05-01: P95 interactive API latency for core read operations should be <= 300 ms under expected production load, excluding external EHR/payer calls.
- NFR-M05-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M05-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.
- NFR-M05-04: PHI fields must be minimized in events; sensitive payloads are referenced by secure identifiers where possible.
- NFR-M05-05: The service must emit OpenTelemetry traces, structured logs, domain events, and KPI metrics for each state transition.

Service boundary requirements:
- The module should run as an independently deployable microservice or extractable bounded context.
- Transactional data should be stored in Azure SQL Database or Azure Database for PostgreSQL, according to the deployment's selected standard.
- Event publishing should use Azure Service Bus for command/workflow events and Azure Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry such as RTLS or device streams.
- Durable orchestration should use Temporal or Azure Durable Functions; the reference design uses Temporal for long-running workflows.
- Secrets and connection strings must live in Azure Key Vault; authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities wherever possible.
- Every external call must include correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, timeout, and circuit-breaker behavior.

### M05.8 UI surfaces and component behavior
- module summary card with red/yellow/green risk status
- work queue table with owner, SLA, priority, evidence, and next action
- patient/visit side panel with timeline, source links, and audit trail
- rule-result panel explaining why an action was recommended or blocked
- AI draft panel with source citations, confidence, user approval buttons, and edit history
- configuration page for authorized administrators with versioning and test mode

UI acceptance behavior:
- Red means action is required before safe completion or workflow continuation.
- Yellow means staff can resolve the issue during the current operating window.
- Green means the module has no unresolved readiness issue for the selected context.
- Black means the configured stop logic requires leadership, NP, physician, compliance, or flow-captain decision before proceeding.
- Every AI-generated text block must display source count, confidence level, last refresh time, and approval state.

- population_health_panel_member: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- population_health_risk_tier: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- population_health_outreach_campaign: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- population_health_care_gap: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- population_health_outreach_attempt: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.

Required common fields on all module tables: `id`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`, `row_version`, `source_system`, `source_ref`, `confidence_score`, `audit_hash`, and `metadata_json`.

### M05.10 API contract seeds
- GET /api/v1/aura-panel/status?tenantId={tenantId}&siteId={siteId} - returns module health, counts, and risk distribution.
- GET /api/v1/aura-panel/visits/{visitId} - returns the module-specific view for a visit.
- POST /api/v1/aura-panel/visits/{visitId}/evaluate - runs rules, scoring, and AI-safe evaluation.
- POST /api/v1/aura-panel/tasks - creates a module-owned task with SLA, owner, evidence, and escalation path.
- PATCH /api/v1/aura-panel/tasks/{taskId} - updates task status, outcome, and audit notes.
- POST /api/v1/aura-panel/approvals - records human approval or rejection for medium/high-risk actions.
- GET /api/v1/aura-panel/audit?entityId={id} - returns immutable action, source, and user history.

- PANEL_INTELLIGENCE_AND_P.EVALUATED.v1
- PANEL_INTELLIGENCE_AND_P.TASK_CREATED.v1
- PANEL_INTELLIGENCE_AND_P.STATE_CHANGED.v1
- PANEL_INTELLIGENCE_AND_P.EXCEPTION_RAISED.v1
- PANEL_INTELLIGENCE_AND_P.APPROVAL_RECORDED.v1
- PANEL_INTELLIGENCE_AND_P.DEFECT_LOGGED.v1

Every event uses the canonical envelope: `event_id`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id_hash`, `visit_id`, `producer`, `event_time`, `trace_id`, `idempotency_key`, `payload`, `sensitivity`, and `retention_class`.

- LLM/RAG may summarize source material, draft messages, draft huddle items, and generate handoff content only with source links and staff verification.

- FR-M06-02: Recommend slot length, modality, NP/care pod, room type, interpreter, forms, records, payer checks, and pre-visit tasks using visit type, complexity, payer, patient barriers, and access capacity.
- FR-M06-03: Use 30-minute visits as the reference default for the NP-led primary-care model while allowing service-specific templates and enterprise customization.
- FR-M06-04: Protect dedicated access capacity for TCM windows, same-day urgent needs, AWV/quality work, chronic-care follow-up, behavioral health, and high-risk panel outreach.

- FR-M06-12: Prevent scheduling of services where required credentialing, payer coverage, location, or supervision configuration is missing unless an approved exception exists.
- FR-M06-13: Provide appointment-level simulation for tomorrow’s schedule and enterprise capacity planning across sites.
- FR-M06-14: Support patient self-scheduling only within rules-controlled openings and route ambiguous requests to staff review.
- FR-M06-15: Provide APIs for visit-type classification, slot recommendation, schedule-risk scoring, appointment creation, reschedule, waitlist, and calendar sync.
- FR-M06-16: Test AWV, TCM, chronic, urgent, procedure, telehealth, interpreter, and non-autonomous NP scheduling scenarios with expected readiness outputs.

- scheduling_no_show_risk: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.

Required common fields on all module tables: `id`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`, `row_version`, `source_system`, `source_ref`, `confidence_score`, `audit_hash`, and `metadata_json`.

### M06.10 API contract seeds
- GET /api/v1/aura-access/status?tenantId={tenantId}&siteId={siteId} - returns module health, counts, and risk distribution.
- GET /api/v1/aura-access/visits/{visitId} - returns the module-specific view for a visit.
- POST /api/v1/aura-access/visits/{visitId}/evaluate - runs rules, scoring, and AI-safe evaluation.
- POST /api/v1/aura-access/tasks - creates a module-owned task with SLA, owner, evidence, and escalation path.
- PATCH /api/v1/aura-access/tasks/{taskId} - updates task status, outcome, and audit notes.
- POST /api/v1/aura-access/approvals - records human approval or rejection for medium/high-risk actions.
- GET /api/v1/aura-access/audit?entityId={id} - returns immutable action, source, and user history.

### M06.11 Event contract seeds
- SCHEDULING_ACCESS_VISIT_.EVALUATED.v1
- SCHEDULING_ACCESS_VISIT_.TASK_CREATED.v1
- SCHEDULING_ACCESS_VISIT_.STATE_CHANGED.v1
- SCHEDULING_ACCESS_VISIT_.EXCEPTION_RAISED.v1
- SCHEDULING_ACCESS_VISIT_.APPROVAL_RECORDED.v1
- SCHEDULING_ACCESS_VISIT_.DEFECT_LOGGED.v1

Every event uses the canonical envelope: `event_id`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id_hash`, `visit_id`, `producer`, `event_time`, `trace_id`, `idempotency_key`, `payload`, `sensitivity`, and `retention_class`.

### M06.12 AI, rules, and human-in-the-loop behavior
- Rules engine owns deterministic policy, payer, safety, standing-order, stop-logic, eligibility, SLA, and workflow gating decisions.
- Predictive ML may score risk, delay, no-show, denial, readmission, bottleneck, or readiness likelihood, but cannot itself authorize clinical, billing, or patient financial conclusions.
- LLM/RAG may summarize source material, draft messages, draft huddle items, and generate handoff content only with source links and staff verification.
- Optimization models may recommend room, staff, schedule, task, and equipment actions; medium/high-risk recommendations require approval.
- The module must support a simulation mode where rules and models run without writeback to validate impact and safety.

### M06.13 Stop logic, validation gates, and failure modes
- Stop logic is configurable by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, patient risk, infection-control status, and compliance risk.
- Hard stops block continuation until override; overrides require role, reason, source evidence, timestamp, and post-event review flag.
- Soft stops create visible warnings and tasks but allow flow to continue when configured.
- Failure modes include stale data, duplicate chart, payer ambiguity, external service outage, AI uncertainty, conflicting source records, and staff ownership gap.
- Downtime mode must preserve the minimum paper/PDF or cached workflow packet needed to safely continue clinic operations.

### M06.14 Integrations and FHIR/HL7/X12 mapping
- FHIR mappings should use Patient, Appointment, Encounter, Location, Practitioner, Task, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance, Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response, DocumentReference, DiagnosticReport, ServiceRequest, Procedure, CommunicationRequest, and QuestionnaireResponse as applicable.
- HL7 v2 mappings should support SIU scheduling, ADT, ORU results, ORM/orders, and custom vendor feed fallbacks.
- X12 mappings should include 270/271 eligibility and, where available, 278 prior authorization and 837/835/277CA revenue-cycle signals.
- Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks tracks must map the same canonical contract to vendor-specific endpoints, app launch mechanisms, webhook capabilities, and writeback limits.

### M06.15 Security, privacy, audit, and compliance controls
- Enforce tenant isolation, least privilege, just-in-time elevated access, session timeout, device/location controls where required, and break-glass audit review.
- Log who saw, changed, approved, rejected, exported, or wrote back each object.
- Treat staff location and productivity data as sensitive operational data; default to aggregate analytics unless individual visibility is operationally necessary.
- Prevent AI from exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users by applying authorization before retrieval, not only before display.
- Preserve all compliance evidence needed for billing, quality, infection-control, privacy, and AI governance review.

### M06.16 Analytics, KPIs, and observability
KPIs include completion rate, defect rate, SLA compliance, unresolved red/black items, source freshness, user override rate, AI acceptance rate, false-positive rate, false-negative defect rate, workflow cycle time, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, and equity variance. Observability must include traces, service metrics, domain-event lag, queue depth, retry volume, external-integration failure rate, model latency, and dashboard projection freshness.

### M06.17 Test cases and acceptance criteria
- TC-M06-01: Create a normal Scheduling, Access, Visit-Type Optimization, and Capacity Design workflow and verify state, task, event, audit, and readiness score updates.
- TC-M06-02: Inject missing source data and verify exception routing, huddle visibility, and no unsafe writeback.
- TC-M06-03: Simulate external EHR/payer/RTLS failure and verify retry, queueing, fallback UI, and user messaging.
- TC-M06-04: Attempt unauthorized access across roles and tenants and verify Entra/RBAC/ABAC enforcement.
- TC-M06-05: Generate an AI recommendation with low confidence and verify it is labeled, source-linked, and blocked from autonomous execution.
- TC-M06-06: Confirm all generated events exclude unnecessary PHI and include trace_id, tenant_id, entity_id, event_time, and schema_version.
- TC-M06-07: Validate dashboard KPI totals against raw events and service database projections.

Acceptance criteria:
- A user can understand the status of Scheduling, Access, Visit-Type Optimization, and Capacity Design for a visit in under 30 seconds without leaving the primary workflow.
- Every action has a named owner, deadline, source evidence, and audit trail.
- The module can operate in demo mode with synthetic EHR, payer, and RTLS fixtures.
- Medium/high-risk actions require approval from the configured role before EHR writeback or patient-facing communication.
- Defects from the module can be logged and routed into the Excellence Loop without manual spreadsheet tracking.

### M06.18 Codex implementation checklist
- Create module package, service interface, database migrations, DTOs, OpenAPI routes, event publishers, repository layer, permission policies, UI routes, shared components, tests, and seed fixtures.
- Implement synthetic fixtures for a Medicare Advantage AWV, TCM visit, chronic-disease follow-up, respiratory-risk same-day visit, telehealth visit, and non-autonomous NP chart-review scenario.
- Include mocked Epic, athenahealth/eClinicalWorks, eligibility, RTLS, SMS, and payment provider adapters.
- Create unit tests for rules, integration tests for API/event behavior, UI tests for role-specific screens, and safety tests for writeback restrictions.
- Ensure the module can be run locally with Docker Compose or dev containers using synthetic data and without real PHI.



## M07 - Pre-Visit OS, Chart Scrub, Readiness Lock, and Huddle Engine

**Product surface:** AURA PreVisit.  
**Domain:** `previsit`.  
**Primary promise:** front-loads every staff task before NP entry and drives the one-page NP handoff.

### M07.1 Functional purpose and institutional value
This module exists so that AURA ClinicOS can operationalize front-loads every staff task before NP entry and
drives the one-page NP handoff. It must work for the primary-care reference implementation while also being
configurable for enterprise multispecialty deployment. The module is not a passive dashboard. It is a
production control layer that receives signals, applies rules, coordinates work, generates safe AI support,
records outcomes, and feeds continuous improvement. In the reference clinic, the module must support an NP-led
model with four NPs per site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, a collaborating physician reviewing
charts for three non-autonomous NPs, and a medical director responsible for operational clinical governance.

### M07.2 Users, permissions, and role bundling
Primary personas: NP, MA, front desk, flow captain, clinic manager, medical director, revenue integrity specialist, quality analyst, compliance/privacy lead, patient/caregiver. Small clinics may bundle roles, but the service must still store the true permission source and action provenance. Every screen must show only the minimum data necessary for the user's job. Supervising-physician and medical-director users require separate review, override, and attestation permissions. Administrative configuration requires dual-control for high-risk payer, AI, infection-control, standing-order, and writeback settings.

### M07.3 Inputs and source systems
- EHR/FHIR resources and vendor-specific feeds relevant to chart_scrub, huddle_item, previsit_packet, defect, readiness_lock.
- Practice-management/scheduling context, appointment metadata, patient demographics, and encounter state.
- Payer, eligibility, authorization, quality, registry, RTLS, sensor, messaging, device, or staff-task inputs when relevant.
- AI/RAG source documents, payer policies, clinic protocols, rule versions, and knowledge-graph evidence.
- User-entered corrections, patient-submitted forms, staff-verified data, and audit annotations.

### M07.4 Outputs and downstream effects
- Updated Visit Readiness Graph components and visible readiness score explanations.
- Role-based work queue tasks, SLA timers, escalation items, and huddle-board exceptions.
- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M07.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to pre-visit os, chart scrub, readiness lock, and huddle engine, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M07.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M07-01: Instantiate the staged Pre-Visit OS timeline for every scheduled visit: panel cycle, scheduling, clearance, chart scrub, patient readiness, 24-hour lock, huddle, check-in, rooming, and NP handoff.
- FR-M07-02: Generate visit-specific prep checklists for AWV, TCM, chronic follow-up, preventive plus E/M, RPM, injections, spirometry, procedure visits, CCM/APCM, vaccines, ECG, labs, telehealth, and urgent visits.
- FR-M07-03: Assign named owners and SLAs for identity, eligibility, authorization, estimates/GFE, records, forms, medication review, quality gaps, social barriers, infection screen, and handoff readiness.
- FR-M07-04: Run a day-before chart scrub in the required order: identity, visit type, eligibility, auth/referral, estimate, forms/HRA, outside records, utilization, meds/allergies, care gaps, standing orders, labs/imaging, risk prompts, care-management eligibility, barriers, handoff.
- FR-M07-05: Produce green/yellow/red/black readiness status and send unresolved red/black issues to huddle or leadership/NP decision before the first patient arrives.
- FR-M07-06: Generate the one-page NP handoff with patient context, safety flags, revenue flags, clinical data, quality/outcome gaps, risk evidence, completed tasks, infection status, and NP decisions needed.
- FR-M07-07: Use AI to draft chart-scrub summaries, payer-policy summaries, huddle briefs, and handoff packets only with source links, confidence, and staff verification.
- FR-M07-08: Publish previsit.plan.created, chart.scrub.started, readiness.locked, huddle.item.created, handoff.ready, and previsit.defect.logged events.
- FR-M07-09: Expose the Pre-Visit Command Center, Tomorrow Board, Chart Scrub Workbench, Morning Huddle Board, NP Handoff Composer, and Defect Log.
- FR-M07-10: Prevent handoff.ready when critical source links, owner resolution, infection-control block, payer notice, or safety escalation remains unresolved without an approved exception.
- FR-M07-11: Integrate with EHR chart, PM schedule, HIE/ADT, payer/clearinghouse, patient forms, quality registry, medication source, RTLS, and patient engagement.
- FR-M07-12: Write back staff-verified pre-visit data, forms, structured intake, task completion, and handoff summary according to EHR writeback policy.
- FR-M07-13: Preserve a defect-learning loop when the NP discovers preventable missing records, barriers, quality gaps, revenue risks, infection risks, or patient confusion.
- FR-M07-14: Support small-clinic role bundling while keeping each workstream’s owner, due date, status, and evidence auditable.
- FR-M07-15: Provide APIs for pre-visit plan creation, chart scrub, readiness lock, huddle generation, handoff draft, staff verification, and defect logging.
- FR-M07-16: Test the full patient journey in the uploaded Pre-Visit Operating System, including the example 72-year-old Medicare Advantage patient with diabetes, CKD, ED follow-up, overdue AWV, and transportation needs.
- FR-M07-17: Fail safely by blocking automatic progression to NP-ready when unresolved black-stop criteria remain.

### M07.7 Technical requirements and service design
- NFR-M07-01: P95 interactive API latency for core read operations should be <= 300 ms under expected production load, excluding external EHR/payer calls.
- NFR-M07-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M07-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.
- NFR-M07-04: PHI fields must be minimized in events; sensitive payloads are referenced by secure identifiers where possible.
- NFR-M07-05: The service must emit OpenTelemetry traces, structured logs, domain events, and KPI metrics for each state transition.

Service boundary requirements:
- The module should run as an independently deployable microservice or extractable bounded context.
- Transactional data should be stored in Azure SQL Database or Azure Database for PostgreSQL, according to the deployment's selected standard.
- Event publishing should use Azure Service Bus for command/workflow events and Azure Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry such as RTLS or device streams.
- Durable orchestration should use Temporal or Azure Durable Functions; the reference design uses Temporal for long-running workflows.
- Secrets and connection strings must live in Azure Key Vault; authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities wherever possible.
- Every external call must include correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, timeout, and circuit-breaker behavior.

### M07.8 UI surfaces and component behavior
- module summary card with red/yellow/green risk status
- work queue table with owner, SLA, priority, evidence, and next action
- patient/visit side panel with timeline, source links, and audit trail
- rule-result panel explaining why an action was recommended or blocked
- AI draft panel with source citations, confidence, user approval buttons, and edit history
- configuration page for authorized administrators with versioning and test mode

UI acceptance behavior:
- Red means action is required before safe completion or workflow continuation.
- Yellow means staff can resolve the issue during the current operating window.
- Green means the module has no unresolved readiness issue for the selected context.
- Black means the configured stop logic requires leadership, NP, physician, compliance, or flow-captain decision before proceeding.
- Every AI-generated text block must display source count, confidence level, last refresh time, and approval state.

Required common fields on all module tables: `id`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`, `row_version`, `source_system`, `source_ref`, `confidence_score`, `audit_hash`, and `metadata_json`.

## M08 - Registration, Patient Identity, Consent, and Front Desk Readiness

- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.

### M08.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to registration, patient identity, consent, and front desk readiness, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M08.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M08-01: Verify patient identity using two identifiers and maintain legal name, preferred name, DOB, address, contacts, guarantor, guardian, caregiver permissions, language, interpreter, accommodations, portal status, and communication preferences.
- FR-M08-02: Detect duplicate chart risk and demographic mismatches before chart scrub, quality logic, medication reconciliation, eligibility, or claims workflows rely on the data.
- FR-M08-03: Run front-desk readiness at check-in: identity, consents, insurance, copay/estimate, forms, interpreter, mobility/sensory/cognitive needs, infection screen, and patient-stated agenda.
- FR-M08-04: Escalate inactive coverage, missing authorization, missing consent, wrong visit type, missing interpreter, or patient distress through respectful scripts and flow-captain queues.
- FR-M08-05: Capture consent and release-of-information status for caregiver access, messaging, telehealth, financial communication, care management, and records retrieval.
- FR-M08-06: Write back approved demographic, consent, and structured check-in updates to the EHR/PM while preserving source and verifier.
- FR-M08-07: Publish patient.identity.verified, registration.updated, duplicate.risk.detected, consent.captured, checkin.completed, and checkin.exception.created events.
- FR-M08-08: Expose Front Desk Cockpit with only required actions, patient-friendly scripts, escalation buttons, and clear handoff to financial counselor or flow captain.
- FR-M08-09: Prevent humiliating or coercive financial interactions by routing complex balances or assistance needs to financial counselor workflows.
- FR-M08-10: Support same-day eligibility recheck for high-risk payer categories and document payer response timestamp.
- FR-M08-11: Integrate card/document capture and OCR only as data-entry assistance; staff must verify before persistence.
- FR-M08-12: Provide ABAC controls for sensitive demographics, caregiver permissions, financial fields, and identity documents.
- FR-M08-13: Create patient-friction metrics for repeated forms, failed portal, estimate disputes, interpreter misses, and demographic rework.
- FR-M08-14: Handle walk-ins and late arrivals with configurable policies for urgency, payer, capacity, and patient safety.
- FR-M08-15: Provide APIs for identity verification, duplicate search, consent update, check-in state, demographic update, and exception escalation.
- FR-M08-16: Test duplicate chart, wrong patient, guardian, interpreter, financial escalation, inactive insurance, and respiratory screen scenarios.
- FR-M08-17: Fail safely by requiring manual verification when identity confidence is low or duplicate chart risk is high.

### M08.7 Technical requirements and service design
- NFR-M08-01: P95 interactive API latency for core read operations should be <= 300 ms under expected production load, excluding external EHR/payer calls.
- NFR-M08-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M08-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.
- NFR-M08-04: PHI fields must be minimized in events; sensitive payloads are referenced by secure identifiers where possible.
- NFR-M08-05: The service must emit OpenTelemetry traces, structured logs, domain events, and KPI metrics for each state transition.

Service boundary requirements:
- The module should run as an independently deployable microservice or extractable bounded context.
- Transactional data should be stored in Azure SQL Database or Azure Database for PostgreSQL, according to the deployment's selected standard.
- Event publishing should use Azure Service Bus for command/workflow events and Azure Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry such as RTLS or device streams.
- Durable orchestration should use Temporal or Azure Durable Functions; the reference design uses Temporal for long-running workflows.
- Secrets and connection strings must live in Azure Key Vault; authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities wherever possible.
- Every external call must include correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, timeout, and circuit-breaker behavior.

### M08.8 UI surfaces and component behavior
- module summary card with red/yellow/green risk status
- work queue table with owner, SLA, priority, evidence, and next action
- patient/visit side panel with timeline, source links, and audit trail
- rule-result panel explaining why an action was recommended or blocked
- AI draft panel with source citations, confidence, user approval buttons, and edit history
- configuration page for authorized administrators with versioning and test mode

UI acceptance behavior:
- Red means action is required before safe completion or workflow continuation.
- Yellow means staff can resolve the issue during the current operating window.
- Green means the module has no unresolved readiness issue for the selected context.
- Black means the configured stop logic requires leadership, NP, physician, compliance, or flow-captain decision before proceeding.
- Every AI-generated text block must display source count, confidence level, last refresh time, and approval state.

### M08.9 Data model entities
- registration_patient_identity: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- registration_guarantor: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- registration_guardian: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- registration_demographic_update: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- registration_front_desk_exception: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.

### M08.10 API contract seeds
- GET /api/v1/aura-frontdesk/status?tenantId={tenantId}&siteId={siteId} - returns module health, counts, and risk distribution.
- GET /api/v1/aura-frontdesk/visits/{visitId} - returns the module-specific view for a visit.
- POST /api/v1/aura-frontdesk/visits/{visitId}/evaluate - runs rules, scoring, and AI-safe evaluation.
- POST /api/v1/aura-frontdesk/tasks - creates a module-owned task with SLA, owner, evidence, and escalation path.
- PATCH /api/v1/aura-frontdesk/tasks/{taskId} - updates task status, outcome, and audit notes.
- POST /api/v1/aura-frontdesk/approvals - records human approval or rejection for medium/high-risk actions.
- GET /api/v1/aura-frontdesk/audit?entityId={id} - returns immutable action, source, and user history.

### M08.11 Event contract seeds
- REGISTRATION_PATIENT_IDE.EVALUATED.v1
- REGISTRATION_PATIENT_IDE.TASK_CREATED.v1
- REGISTRATION_PATIENT_IDE.STATE_CHANGED.v1
- REGISTRATION_PATIENT_IDE.EXCEPTION_RAISED.v1
- REGISTRATION_PATIENT_IDE.APPROVAL_RECORDED.v1
- REGISTRATION_PATIENT_IDE.DEFECT_LOGGED.v1

Every event uses the canonical envelope: `event_id`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id_hash`, `visit_id`, `producer`, `event_time`, `trace_id`, `idempotency_key`, `payload`, `sensitivity`, and `retention_class`.

### M08.12 AI, rules, and human-in-the-loop behavior
- Rules engine owns deterministic policy, payer, safety, standing-order, stop-logic, eligibility, SLA, and workflow gating decisions.
- Predictive ML may score risk, delay, no-show, denial, readmission, bottleneck, or readiness likelihood, but cannot itself authorize clinical, billing, or patient financial conclusions.
- LLM/RAG may summarize source material, draft messages, draft huddle items, and generate handoff content only with source links and staff verification.
- Optimization models may recommend room, staff, schedule, task, and equipment actions; medium/high-risk recommendations require approval.
- The module must support a simulation mode where rules and models run without writeback to validate impact and safety.

### M08.13 Stop logic, validation gates, and failure modes
- Stop logic is configurable by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, patient risk, infection-control status, and compliance risk.
- Hard stops block continuation until override; overrides require role, reason, source evidence, timestamp, and post-event review flag.
- Soft stops create visible warnings and tasks but allow flow to continue when configured.
- Failure modes include stale data, duplicate chart, payer ambiguity, external service outage, AI uncertainty, conflicting source records, and staff ownership gap.
- Downtime mode must preserve the minimum paper/PDF or cached workflow packet needed to safely continue clinic operations.

### M08.14 Integrations and FHIR/HL7/X12 mapping
- FHIR mappings should use Patient, Appointment, Encounter, Location, Practitioner, Task, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance, Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response, DocumentReference, DiagnosticReport, ServiceRequest, Procedure, CommunicationRequest, and QuestionnaireResponse as applicable.
- HL7 v2 mappings should support SIU scheduling, ADT, ORU results, ORM/orders, and custom vendor feed fallbacks.
- X12 mappings should include 270/271 eligibility and, where available, 278 prior authorization and 837/835/277CA revenue-cycle signals.
- Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks tracks must map the same canonical contract to vendor-specific endpoints, app launch mechanisms, webhook capabilities, and writeback limits.

### M08.15 Security, privacy, audit, and compliance controls
- Enforce tenant isolation, least privilege, just-in-time elevated access, session timeout, device/location controls where required, and break-glass audit review.
- Log who saw, changed, approved, rejected, exported, or wrote back each object.
- Treat staff location and productivity data as sensitive operational data; default to aggregate analytics unless individual visibility is operationally necessary.
- Prevent AI from exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users by applying authorization before retrieval, not only before display.
- Preserve all compliance evidence needed for billing, quality, infection-control, privacy, and AI governance review.

### M08.16 Analytics, KPIs, and observability
KPIs include completion rate, defect rate, SLA compliance, unresolved red/black items, source freshness, user override rate, AI acceptance rate, false-positive rate, false-negative defect rate, workflow cycle time, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, and equity variance. Observability must include traces, service metrics, domain-event lag, queue depth, retry volume, external-integration failure rate, model latency, and dashboard projection freshness.

### M08.17 Test cases and acceptance criteria
- TC-M08-01: Create a normal Registration, Patient Identity, Consent, and Front Desk Readiness workflow and verify state, task, event, audit, and readiness score updates.
- TC-M08-02: Inject missing source data and verify exception routing, huddle visibility, and no unsafe writeback.
- TC-M08-03: Simulate external EHR/payer/RTLS failure and verify retry, queueing, fallback UI, and user messaging.
- TC-M08-04: Attempt unauthorized access across roles and tenants and verify Entra/RBAC/ABAC enforcement.
- TC-M08-05: Generate an AI recommendation with low confidence and verify it is labeled, source-linked, and blocked from autonomous execution.
- TC-M08-06: Confirm all generated events exclude unnecessary PHI and include trace_id, tenant_id, entity_id, event_time, and schema_version.
- TC-M08-07: Validate dashboard KPI totals against raw events and service database projections.

Acceptance criteria:
- A user can understand the status of Registration, Patient Identity, Consent, and Front Desk Readiness for a visit in under 30 seconds without leaving the primary workflow.
- Every action has a named owner, deadline, source evidence, and audit trail.
- The module can operate in demo mode with synthetic EHR, payer, and RTLS fixtures.
- Medium/high-risk actions require approval from the configured role before EHR writeback or patient-facing communication.
- Defects from the module can be logged and routed into the Excellence Loop without manual spreadsheet tracking.

### M08.18 Codex implementation checklist
- Create module package, service interface, database migrations, DTOs, OpenAPI routes, event publishers, repository layer, permission policies, UI routes, shared components, tests, and seed fixtures.
- Implement synthetic fixtures for a Medicare Advantage AWV, TCM visit, chronic-disease follow-up, respiratory-risk same-day visit, telehealth visit, and non-autonomous NP chart-review scenario.
- Include mocked Epic, athenahealth/eClinicalWorks, eligibility, RTLS, SMS, and payment provider adapters.
- Create unit tests for rules, integration tests for API/event behavior, UI tests for role-specific screens, and safety tests for writeback restrictions.
- Ensure the module can be run locally with Docker Compose or dev containers using synthetic data and without real PHI.



## M09 - Records, HIE, ADT, Diagnostics, and External Data Retrieval

**Product surface:** AURA Records.  
**Domain:** `records`.  
**Primary promise:** pulls missing outside information before the patient reaches the NP.

### M09.1 Functional purpose and institutional value
This module exists so that AURA ClinicOS can operationalize pulls missing outside information before the
patient reaches the NP. It must work for the primary-care reference implementation while also being
configurable for enterprise multispecialty deployment. The module is not a passive dashboard. It is a
production control layer that receives signals, applies rules, coordinates work, generates safe AI support,
records outcomes, and feeds continuous improvement. In the reference clinic, the module must support an NP-led
model with four NPs per site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, a collaborating physician reviewing
charts for three non-autonomous NPs, and a medical director responsible for operational clinical governance.

### M09.2 Users, permissions, and role bundling
Primary personas: NP, MA, front desk, flow captain, clinic manager, medical director, revenue integrity specialist, quality analyst, compliance/privacy lead, patient/caregiver. Small clinics may bundle roles, but the service must still store the true permission source and action provenance. Every screen must show only the minimum data necessary for the user's job. Supervising-physician and medical-director users require separate review, override, and attestation permissions. Administrative configuration requires dual-control for high-risk payer, AI, infection-control, standing-order, and writeback settings.

### M09.3 Inputs and source systems
- EHR/FHIR resources and vendor-specific feeds relevant to external_record, adt_event, diagnostic_result, record_request, source_document.
- Practice-management/scheduling context, appointment metadata, patient demographics, and encounter state.
- Payer, eligibility, authorization, quality, registry, RTLS, sensor, messaging, device, or staff-task inputs when relevant.
- AI/RAG source documents, payer policies, clinic protocols, rule versions, and knowledge-graph evidence.
- User-entered corrections, patient-submitted forms, staff-verified data, and audit annotations.

### M09.4 Outputs and downstream effects
- Updated Visit Readiness Graph components and visible readiness score explanations.
- Role-based work queue tasks, SLA timers, escalation items, and huddle-board exceptions.
- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M09.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to records, hie, adt, diagnostics, and external data retrieval, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M09.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M09-01: Ingest, request, track, summarize, and link external records from HIE, ADT, hospital portals, specialist notes, labs, imaging, pathology, immunization registries, discharge summaries, and prior primary-care records.
- FR-M09-02: Create records work queues with source, requested item, due date, patient/visit linkage, authorization/ROI status, status, owner, and clinical impact.
- FR-M09-03: Detect recent ED, inpatient, specialist, imaging, lab, and procedure activity that may affect TCM, chronic care, quality gaps, medication reconciliation, or risk adjustment.
- FR-M09-04: Summarize external records for the NP handoff with source links and do not dump unfiltered records into the visit workflow.
- FR-M09-05: Classify missing records as routine, important, critical, or blocker based on visit purpose, urgency, and stop logic.
- FR-M09-06: Publish record.requested, record.received, adt.discharge.detected, diagnostic.result.received, record.missing.critical, and record.summary.ready events.
- FR-M09-07: Integrate with HIE/ADT, EHR DocumentReference, lab interfaces, imaging portals, registry data, and patient-authorized records requests.
- FR-M09-08: Use LLM/RAG only to summarize retrieved records with citations, dates, confidence, and conflict detection; staff verifies before handoff/writeback.
- FR-M09-09: Detect conflicting source data such as inconsistent medication lists, discharge dates, diagnoses, immunization history, or duplicate results.
- FR-M09-10: Write back approved record links, summaries, and reconciled structured data according to EHR document and data-writeback policy.
- FR-M09-11: Expose Records Workbench with source status, missing critical items, source reliability, patient authorization, and handoff impact.
- FR-M09-12: Maintain audit and minimum-necessary controls for all external record views, downloads, and summaries.
- FR-M09-13: Provide retry/fallback logic for unavailable APIs, payer portals, fax requests, and manual uploads.
- FR-M09-14: Generate TCM-specific record packets including discharge summary, medication changes, pending tests, home health, DME, and follow-up instructions.
- FR-M09-15: Provide APIs for records request, upload, summary generation, source linking, missing-record escalation, and ADT event ingestion.
- FR-M09-16: Test missing discharge summary, outside lab conflict, duplicate mammogram, immunization registry conflict, and unavailable HIE scenarios.
- FR-M09-17: Fail safely by surfacing missing critical records to the NP rather than fabricating or assuming content.

### M09.7 Technical requirements and service design

- NFR-M09-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M09-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.

3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.

5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M10.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M10-01: Create a medication intelligence workspace combining EHR medication list, eRx history, pharmacy fill history, discharge medications, specialist prescriptions, OTCs, supplements, allergies, formulary, and patient report.
- FR-M10-02: Detect discrepancies, duplicates, high-risk medications, renal-dose concerns, anticoagulant risk, insulin/hypoglycemia risk, controlled-substance review needs, adherence gaps, refill gaps, and affordability barriers.
- FR-M10-03: Route urgent medication safety concerns to RN/NP before visit and routine medication questions to MA/pharmacy work queues.
- FR-M10-04: Support PDMP integration points where clinic policy or state law requires controlled-substance review, without assuming availability or automating clinical decisions.
- FR-M10-05: Prepare medication reconciliation questions, refill needs, pharmacy preference, mail-order options, 90-day synchronization, and formulary alternatives for NP decision.
- FR-M10-06: Publish medication.history.loaded, medication.discrepancy.detected, highrisk.medication.flagged, adherence.risk.flagged, formulary.barrier.detected, and medrec.ready events.
- FR-M10-07: Use AI to summarize medication changes and adherence patterns only with source links and clear uncertainty where source data conflict.
- FR-M10-08: Prevent staff from independently changing therapy outside approved protocol; NP or authorized clinician must decide medication changes.
- FR-M10-09: Feed HEDIS/STARS adherence, chronic-disease outcomes, TCM med reconciliation, risk adjustment evidence, and patient affordability workflows.
- FR-M10-10: Expose Medication Sentinel screen with discrepancy list, source comparison, fill timeline, safety alerts, affordability tasks, and NP questions.
- FR-M10-11: Integrate with EHR meds/allergies, Surescripts/eRx/fill history where available, formulary/benefit checks, payer pharmacy data, PDMP adapters, and patient forms.
- FR-M10-12: Write back staff-verified medication history and reconciliation status, not AI-only suggestions.
- FR-M10-13: Provide configurable alert thresholds to prevent over-alerting and fatigue.
- FR-M10-14: Produce monthly and visit-level metrics for med reconciliation completion, adherence gap closure, formulary barriers, safety escalations, and refill completion.
- FR-M10-15: Provide APIs for medication source ingestion, discrepancy query, medrec task, formulary barrier, adherence risk, and NP question packet.
- FR-M10-16: Test TCM discharge med conflict, CKD renal dose concern, missed antihypertensive refill, SGLT2 cost barrier, and controlled-substance PDMP-required scenario.
- FR-M10-17: Fail safely by labeling unknown medication state as unresolved rather than reconciled.

### M10.7 Technical requirements and service design
- NFR-M10-01: P95 interactive API latency for core read operations should be <= 300 ms under expected production load, excluding external EHR/payer calls.
- NFR-M10-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M10-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.
- NFR-M10-04: PHI fields must be minimized in events; sensitive payloads are referenced by secure identifiers where possible.
- NFR-M10-05: The service must emit OpenTelemetry traces, structured logs, domain events, and KPI metrics for each state transition.

Service boundary requirements:
- The module should run as an independently deployable microservice or extractable bounded context.
- Transactional data should be stored in Azure SQL Database or Azure Database for PostgreSQL, according to the deployment's selected standard.
- Event publishing should use Azure Service Bus for command/workflow events and Azure Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry such as RTLS or device streams.
- Durable orchestration should use Temporal or Azure Durable Functions; the reference design uses Temporal for long-running workflows.
- Secrets and connection strings must live in Azure Key Vault; authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities wherever possible.
- Every external call must include correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, timeout, and circuit-breaker behavior.

### M10.8 UI surfaces and component behavior
- module summary card with red/yellow/green risk status
- work queue table with owner, SLA, priority, evidence, and next action
- patient/visit side panel with timeline, source links, and audit trail
- rule-result panel explaining why an action was recommended or blocked
- AI draft panel with source citations, confidence, user approval buttons, and edit history
- configuration page for authorized administrators with versioning and test mode

UI acceptance behavior:
- Red means action is required before safe completion or workflow continuation.
- Yellow means staff can resolve the issue during the current operating window.
- Green means the module has no unresolved readiness issue for the selected context.
- Black means the configured stop logic requires leadership, NP, physician, compliance, or flow-captain decision before proceeding.
- Every AI-generated text block must display source count, confidence level, last refresh time, and approval state.

### M10.9 Data model entities
- pharmacy_medication_item: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- pharmacy_fill_history: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- pharmacy_pharmacy_barrier: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- pharmacy_interaction_flag: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- pharmacy_formulary_check: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.

Required common fields on all module tables: `id`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`, `row_version`, `source_system`, `source_ref`, `confidence_score`, `audit_hash`, and `metadata_json`.

### M10.10 API contract seeds
- GET /api/v1/aura-medication-sentinel/status?tenantId={tenantId}&siteId={siteId} - returns module health, counts, and risk distribution.
- GET /api/v1/aura-medication-sentinel/visits/{visitId} - returns the module-specific view for a visit.
- POST /api/v1/aura-medication-sentinel/visits/{visitId}/evaluate - runs rules, scoring, and AI-safe evaluation.
- POST /api/v1/aura-medication-sentinel/tasks - creates a module-owned task with SLA, owner, evidence, and escalation path.
- PATCH /api/v1/aura-medication-sentinel/tasks/{taskId} - updates task status, outcome, and audit notes.
- POST /api/v1/aura-medication-sentinel/approvals - records human approval or rejection for medium/high-risk actions.
- GET /api/v1/aura-medication-sentinel/audit?entityId={id} - returns immutable action, source, and user history.

### M10.11 Event contract seeds
- MEDICATION_SENTINEL_AND_.EVALUATED.v1
- MEDICATION_SENTINEL_AND_.TASK_CREATED.v1
- MEDICATION_SENTINEL_AND_.STATE_CHANGED.v1
- MEDICATION_SENTINEL_AND_.EXCEPTION_RAISED.v1
- MEDICATION_SENTINEL_AND_.APPROVAL_RECORDED.v1
- MEDICATION_SENTINEL_AND_.DEFECT_LOGGED.v1

Every event uses the canonical envelope: `event_id`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id_hash`, `visit_id`, `producer`, `event_time`, `trace_id`, `idempotency_key`, `payload`, `sensitivity`, and `retention_class`.

### M10.12 AI, rules, and human-in-the-loop behavior
- Rules engine owns deterministic policy, payer, safety, standing-order, stop-logic, eligibility, SLA, and workflow gating decisions.
- Predictive ML may score risk, delay, no-show, denial, readmission, bottleneck, or readiness likelihood, but cannot itself authorize clinical, billing, or patient financial conclusions.
- LLM/RAG may summarize source material, draft messages, draft huddle items, and generate handoff content only with source links and staff verification.
- Optimization models may recommend room, staff, schedule, task, and equipment actions; medium/high-risk recommendations require approval.
- The module must support a simulation mode where rules and models run without writeback to validate impact and safety.

### M10.13 Stop logic, validation gates, and failure modes
- Stop logic is configurable by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, patient risk, infection-control status, and compliance risk.
- Hard stops block continuation until override; overrides require role, reason, source evidence, timestamp, and post-event review flag.
- Soft stops create visible warnings and tasks but allow flow to continue when configured.
- Failure modes include stale data, duplicate chart, payer ambiguity, external service outage, AI uncertainty, conflicting source records, and staff ownership gap.
- Downtime mode must preserve the minimum paper/PDF or cached workflow packet needed to safely continue clinic operations.

### M10.14 Integrations and FHIR/HL7/X12 mapping
- FHIR mappings should use Patient, Appointment, Encounter, Location, Practitioner, Task, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance, Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response, DocumentReference, DiagnosticReport, ServiceRequest, Procedure, CommunicationRequest, and QuestionnaireResponse as applicable.
- HL7 v2 mappings should support SIU scheduling, ADT, ORU results, ORM/orders, and custom vendor feed fallbacks.
- X12 mappings should include 270/271 eligibility and, where available, 278 prior authorization and 837/835/277CA revenue-cycle signals.
- Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks tracks must map the same canonical contract to vendor-specific endpoints, app launch mechanisms, webhook capabilities, and writeback limits.

### M10.15 Security, privacy, audit, and compliance controls
- Enforce tenant isolation, least privilege, just-in-time elevated access, session timeout, device/location controls where required, and break-glass audit review.
- Log who saw, changed, approved, rejected, exported, or wrote back each object.
- Treat staff location and productivity data as sensitive operational data; default to aggregate analytics unless individual visibility is operationally necessary.
- Prevent AI from exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users by applying authorization before retrieval, not only before display.
- Preserve all compliance evidence needed for billing, quality, infection-control, privacy, and AI governance review.

### M10.16 Analytics, KPIs, and observability
KPIs include completion rate, defect rate, SLA compliance, unresolved red/black items, source freshness, user override rate, AI acceptance rate, false-positive rate, false-negative defect rate, workflow cycle time, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, and equity variance. Observability must include traces, service metrics, domain-event lag, queue depth, retry volume, external-integration failure rate, model latency, and dashboard projection freshness.

### M10.17 Test cases and acceptance criteria
- TC-M10-01: Create a normal Medication Sentinel and Pharmacy Intelligence workflow and verify state, task, event, audit, and readiness score updates.
- TC-M10-02: Inject missing source data and verify exception routing, huddle visibility, and no unsafe writeback.
- TC-M10-03: Simulate external EHR/payer/RTLS failure and verify retry, queueing, fallback UI, and user messaging.
- TC-M10-04: Attempt unauthorized access across roles and tenants and verify Entra/RBAC/ABAC enforcement.
- TC-M10-05: Generate an AI recommendation with low confidence and verify it is labeled, source-linked, and blocked from autonomous execution.
- TC-M10-06: Confirm all generated events exclude unnecessary PHI and include trace_id, tenant_id, entity_id, event_time, and schema_version.
- TC-M10-07: Validate dashboard KPI totals against raw events and service database projections.

Acceptance criteria:
- A user can understand the status of Medication Sentinel and Pharmacy Intelligence for a visit in under 30 seconds without leaving the primary workflow.
- Every action has a named owner, deadline, source evidence, and audit trail.
- The module can operate in demo mode with synthetic EHR, payer, and RTLS fixtures.
- Medium/high-risk actions require approval from the configured role before EHR writeback or patient-facing communication.
- Defects from the module can be logged and routed into the Excellence Loop without manual spreadsheet tracking.

### M10.18 Codex implementation checklist
- Create module package, service interface, database migrations, DTOs, OpenAPI routes, event publishers, repository layer, permission policies, UI routes, shared components, tests, and seed fixtures.
- Implement synthetic fixtures for a Medicare Advantage AWV, TCM visit, chronic-disease follow-up, respiratory-risk same-day visit, telehealth visit, and non-autonomous NP chart-review scenario.
- Include mocked Epic, athenahealth/eClinicalWorks, eligibility, RTLS, SMS, and payment provider adapters.
- Create unit tests for rules, integration tests for API/event behavior, UI tests for role-specific screens, and safety tests for writeback restrictions.
- Ensure the module can be run locally with Docker Compose or dev containers using synthetic data and without real PHI.



## M11 - RevCycle-at-Service: Eligibility, Estimates, Payments, Notices, and Financial Experience

**Product surface:** AURA RevCycle.  
**Domain:** `revenue`.  
**Primary promise:** makes the encounter financially clear without coercive collections.

### M11.1 Functional purpose and institutional value
This module exists so that AURA ClinicOS can operationalize makes the encounter financially clear without
coercive collections. It must work for the primary-care reference implementation while also being configurable
for enterprise multispecialty deployment. The module is not a passive dashboard. It is a production control
layer that receives signals, applies rules, coordinates work, generates safe AI support, records outcomes, and
feeds continuous improvement. In the reference clinic, the module must support an NP-led model with four NPs
per site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, a collaborating physician reviewing charts for three non-
autonomous NPs, and a medical director responsible for operational clinical governance.

### M11.2 Users, permissions, and role bundling
Primary personas: NP, MA, front desk, flow captain, clinic manager, medical director, revenue integrity specialist, quality analyst, compliance/privacy lead, patient/caregiver. Small clinics may bundle roles, but the service must still store the true permission source and action provenance. Every screen must show only the minimum data necessary for the user's job. Supervising-physician and medical-director users require separate review, override, and attestation permissions. Administrative configuration requires dual-control for high-risk payer, AI, infection-control, standing-order, and writeback settings.

### M11.3 Inputs and source systems
- EHR/FHIR resources and vendor-specific feeds relevant to eligibility_check, benefit_summary, estimate, payment_intent, financial_assistance_screen.
- Practice-management/scheduling context, appointment metadata, patient demographics, and encounter state.
- Payer, eligibility, authorization, quality, registry, RTLS, sensor, messaging, device, or staff-task inputs when relevant.
- AI/RAG source documents, payer policies, clinic protocols, rule versions, and knowledge-graph evidence.
- User-entered corrections, patient-submitted forms, staff-verified data, and audit annotations.

### M11.4 Outputs and downstream effects
- Updated Visit Readiness Graph components and visible readiness score explanations.
- Role-based work queue tasks, SLA timers, escalation items, and huddle-board exceptions.
- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M11.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to revcycle-at-service: eligibility, estimates, payments, notices, and financial experience, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M11.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M11-01: Run eligibility, benefits, network, PCP assignment, COB, copay, deductible, coinsurance, out-of-pocket, carve-out, telehealth, lab-network, and payer-specific benefit checks at scheduling, 72-48 hours, and check-in.
- FR-M11-02: Generate patient responsibility estimates and Good Faith Estimate workflows for uninsured or self-pay patients when applicable, with delivery method, timestamp, services, assumptions, and patient questions.
- FR-M11-03: Provide respectful, noncoercive financial scripts and route financial-assistance, payment-plan, charity/sliding-fee, and high-balance questions to financial counselor workflows.
- FR-M11-04: Create time-of-service financial status inside the Visit Readiness Graph without blocking medically necessary urgent care because of payment friction.
- FR-M11-05: Detect ABN or payer-notice needs for likely noncovered or medical-necessity-risk services and require approved notice workflow before elective service delivery where policy requires.
- FR-M11-06: Publish eligibility.verified, benefits.changed, estimate.generated, gfe.delivered, payment.collected, financial.assistance.offered, and rcm.exception.created events.
- FR-M11-07: Integrate with clearinghouse, payer APIs/portals, payment processor, PM system, patient engagement, payer rules library, and Auth module.
- FR-M11-08: Write back only approved financial statuses, estimate metadata, payment link status, and patient financial conversation notes allowed by policy.
- FR-M11-09: Prevent AI from delivering final financial/legal conclusions, coercive collection instructions, or denial of care; AI may draft explanations for staff review.
- FR-M11-10: Expose Revenue Readiness and Front Desk financial views with eligibility status, estimate/GFE status, copay, financial-assistance prompts, and escalation actions.
- FR-M11-11: Maintain payer-specific rule ownership, source links, effective dates, confidence, and review dates.
- FR-M11-12: Calculate RCM readiness score, front-end defect rate, estimate delivery rate, POS collection, financial assistance routing, and patient financial friction.
- FR-M11-13: Allow configuration by payer, service line, visit type, state, site, patient category, and urgency.
- FR-M11-14: Provide APIs for eligibility request, benefit summary, estimate generation, GFE workflow, payment link, financial assistance referral, and financial exception escalation.
- FR-M11-15: Test Medicare Advantage AWV, commercial deductible imaging, self-pay GFE, inactive Medicaid, PCP mismatch, and ABN-required service scenarios.
- FR-M11-16: Fail safely by routing ambiguous payer responses to human review rather than marking revenue readiness complete.
- FR-M11-17: Keep revenue maximization bounded by appropriate, compliant service capture and explicit anti-upcoding, anti-duplicate-billing, anti-coercion controls.
