- X12 mappings should include 270/271 eligibility and, where available, 278 prior authorization and 837/835/277CA revenue-cycle signals.
- Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks tracks must map the same canonical contract to vendor-specific endpoints, app launch mechanisms, webhook capabilities, and writeback limits.

### M25.15 Security, privacy, audit, and compliance controls
- Enforce tenant isolation, least privilege, just-in-time elevated access, session timeout, device/location controls where required, and break-glass audit review.
- Log who saw, changed, approved, rejected, exported, or wrote back each object.
- Treat staff location and productivity data as sensitive operational data; default to aggregate analytics unless individual visibility is operationally necessary.
- Prevent AI from exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users by applying authorization before retrieval, not only before display.
- Preserve all compliance evidence needed for billing, quality, infection-control, privacy, and AI governance review.

### M25.16 Analytics, KPIs, and observability
KPIs include completion rate, defect rate, SLA compliance, unresolved red/black items, source freshness, user override rate, AI acceptance rate, false-positive rate, false-negative defect rate, workflow cycle time, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, and equity variance. Observability must include traces, service metrics, domain-event lag, queue depth, retry volume, external-integration failure rate, model latency, and dashboard projection freshness.

### M25.17 Test cases and acceptance criteria
- TC-M25-01: Create a normal Integration Hub: FHIR/SMART, HL7 v2, X12, Payer APIs, RTLS, Messaging, Devices, and Registries workflow and verify state, task, event, audit, and readiness score updates.
- TC-M25-02: Inject missing source data and verify exception routing, huddle visibility, and no unsafe writeback.
- TC-M25-03: Simulate external EHR/payer/RTLS failure and verify retry, queueing, fallback UI, and user messaging.
- TC-M25-04: Attempt unauthorized access across roles and tenants and verify Entra/RBAC/ABAC enforcement.
- TC-M25-05: Generate an AI recommendation with low confidence and verify it is labeled, source-linked, and blocked from autonomous execution.
- TC-M25-06: Confirm all generated events exclude unnecessary PHI and include trace_id, tenant_id, entity_id, event_time, and schema_version.
- TC-M25-07: Validate dashboard KPI totals against raw events and service database projections.

Acceptance criteria:
- A user can understand the status of Integration Hub: FHIR/SMART, HL7 v2, X12, Payer APIs, RTLS, Messaging, Devices, and Registries for a visit in under 30 seconds without leaving the primary workflow.
- Every action has a named owner, deadline, source evidence, and audit trail.
- The module can operate in demo mode with synthetic EHR, payer, and RTLS fixtures.
- Medium/high-risk actions require approval from the configured role before EHR writeback or patient-facing communication.
- Defects from the module can be logged and routed into the Excellence Loop without manual spreadsheet tracking.

### M26.10 API contract seeds
- GET /api/v1/aura-data-platform/status?tenantId={tenantId}&siteId={siteId} - returns module health, counts, and risk distribution.
- GET /api/v1/aura-data-platform/visits/{visitId} - returns the module-specific view for a visit.
- POST /api/v1/aura-data-platform/visits/{visitId}/evaluate - runs rules, scoring, and AI-safe evaluation.
- POST /api/v1/aura-data-platform/tasks - creates a module-owned task with SLA, owner, evidence, and escalation path.
- PATCH /api/v1/aura-data-platform/tasks/{taskId} - updates task status, outcome, and audit notes.
- POST /api/v1/aura-data-platform/approvals - records human approval or rejection for medium/high-risk actions.
- GET /api/v1/aura-data-platform/audit?entityId={id} - returns immutable action, source, and user history.

### M26.11 Event contract seeds
- DATA_PLATFORM_KNOWLEDGE_.EVALUATED.v1
- DATA_PLATFORM_KNOWLEDGE_.TASK_CREATED.v1
- DATA_PLATFORM_KNOWLEDGE_.STATE_CHANGED.v1
- DATA_PLATFORM_KNOWLEDGE_.EXCEPTION_RAISED.v1
- DATA_PLATFORM_KNOWLEDGE_.APPROVAL_RECORDED.v1
- DATA_PLATFORM_KNOWLEDGE_.DEFECT_LOGGED.v1

Every event uses the canonical envelope: `event_id`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id_hash`, `visit_id`, `producer`, `event_time`, `trace_id`, `idempotency_key`, `payload`, `sensitivity`, and `retention_class`.

### M26.12 AI, rules, and human-in-the-loop behavior
- Rules engine owns deterministic policy, payer, safety, standing-order, stop-logic, eligibility, SLA, and workflow gating decisions.
- Predictive ML may score risk, delay, no-show, denial, readmission, bottleneck, or readiness likelihood, but cannot itself authorize clinical, billing, or patient financial conclusions.
- LLM/RAG may summarize source material, draft messages, draft huddle items, and generate handoff content only with source links and staff verification.
- Optimization models may recommend room, staff, schedule, task, and equipment actions; medium/high-risk recommendations require approval.
- The module must support a simulation mode where rules and models run without writeback to validate impact and safety.

### M26.13 Stop logic, validation gates, and failure modes
- Stop logic is configurable by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, patient risk, infection-control status, and compliance risk.
- Hard stops block continuation until override; overrides require role, reason, source evidence, timestamp, and post-event review flag.
- Soft stops create visible warnings and tasks but allow flow to continue when configured.
- Failure modes include stale data, duplicate chart, payer ambiguity, external service outage, AI uncertainty, conflicting source records, and staff ownership gap.
- Downtime mode must preserve the minimum paper/PDF or cached workflow packet needed to safely continue clinic operations.

### M26.14 Integrations and FHIR/HL7/X12 mapping
- FHIR mappings should use Patient, Appointment, Encounter, Location, Practitioner, Task, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance, Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response, DocumentReference, DiagnosticReport, ServiceRequest, Procedure, CommunicationRequest, and QuestionnaireResponse as applicable.
- HL7 v2 mappings should support SIU scheduling, ADT, ORU results, ORM/orders, and custom vendor feed fallbacks.
- X12 mappings should include 270/271 eligibility and, where available, 278 prior authorization and 837/835/277CA revenue-cycle signals.
- Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks tracks must map the same canonical contract to vendor-specific endpoints, app launch mechanisms, webhook capabilities, and writeback limits.

### M26.15 Security, privacy, audit, and compliance controls
- Enforce tenant isolation, least privilege, just-in-time elevated access, session timeout, device/location controls where required, and break-glass audit review.
- Log who saw, changed, approved, rejected, exported, or wrote back each object.
- Treat staff location and productivity data as sensitive operational data; default to aggregate analytics unless individual visibility is operationally necessary.
- Prevent AI from exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users by applying authorization before retrieval, not only before display.
- Preserve all compliance evidence needed for billing, quality, infection-control, privacy, and AI governance review.

### M26.16 Analytics, KPIs, and observability
KPIs include completion rate, defect rate, SLA compliance, unresolved red/black items, source freshness, user override rate, AI acceptance rate, false-positive rate, false-negative defect rate, workflow cycle time, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, and equity variance. Observability must include traces, service metrics, domain-event lag, queue depth, retry volume, external-integration failure rate, model latency, and dashboard projection freshness.

### M26.17 Test cases and acceptance criteria
- TC-M26-01: Create a normal Data Platform, Knowledge Graph, Warehouse, Search, and Retention workflow and verify state, task, event, audit, and readiness score updates.
- TC-M26-02: Inject missing source data and verify exception routing, huddle visibility, and no unsafe writeback.
- TC-M26-03: Simulate external EHR/payer/RTLS failure and verify retry, queueing, fallback UI, and user messaging.
- TC-M26-04: Attempt unauthorized access across roles and tenants and verify Entra/RBAC/ABAC enforcement.
- TC-M26-05: Generate an AI recommendation with low confidence and verify it is labeled, source-linked, and blocked from autonomous execution.
- TC-M26-06: Confirm all generated events exclude unnecessary PHI and include trace_id, tenant_id, entity_id, event_time, and schema_version.
- TC-M26-07: Validate dashboard KPI totals against raw events and service database projections.

Acceptance criteria:
- A user can understand the status of Data Platform, Knowledge Graph, Warehouse, Search, and Retention for a visit in under 30 seconds without leaving the primary workflow.
- Every action has a named owner, deadline, source evidence, and audit trail.
- The module can operate in demo mode with synthetic EHR, payer, and RTLS fixtures.
- Medium/high-risk actions require approval from the configured role before EHR writeback or patient-facing communication.
- Defects from the module can be logged and routed into the Excellence Loop without manual spreadsheet tracking.

### M26.18 Codex implementation checklist
- Create module package, service interface, database migrations, DTOs, OpenAPI routes, event publishers, repository layer, permission policies, UI routes, shared components, tests, and seed fixtures.
- Implement synthetic fixtures for a Medicare Advantage AWV, TCM visit, chronic-disease follow-up, respiratory-risk same-day visit, telehealth visit, and non-autonomous NP chart-review scenario.
- Include mocked Epic, athenahealth/eClinicalWorks, eligibility, RTLS, SMS, and payment provider adapters.
- Create unit tests for rules, integration tests for API/event behavior, UI tests for role-specific screens, and safety tests for writeback restrictions.
- Ensure the module can be run locally with Docker Compose or dev containers using synthetic data and without real PHI.



## M27 - Telehealth, Virtual Rooming, Remote Monitoring, and Hybrid Care Interface

**Product surface:** AURA Virtual Care.  
**Domain:** `virtual_care`.  
**Primary promise:** makes virtual and hybrid care as operationally rigorous as in-person care.

### M27.1 Functional purpose and institutional value
This module exists so that AURA ClinicOS can operationalize makes virtual and hybrid care as operationally
rigorous as in-person care. It must work for the primary-care reference implementation while also being
configurable for enterprise multispecialty deployment. The module is not a passive dashboard. It is a
production control layer that receives signals, applies rules, coordinates work, generates safe AI support,
records outcomes, and feeds continuous improvement. In the reference clinic, the module must support an NP-led
model with four NPs per site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, a collaborating physician reviewing
charts for three non-autonomous NPs, and a medical director responsible for operational clinical governance.

### M27.2 Users, permissions, and role bundling
Primary personas: NP, MA, front desk, flow captain, clinic manager, medical director, revenue integrity specialist, quality analyst, compliance/privacy lead, patient/caregiver. Small clinics may bundle roles, but the service must still store the true permission source and action provenance. Every screen must show only the minimum data necessary for the user's job. Supervising-physician and medical-director users require separate review, override, and attestation permissions. Administrative configuration requires dual-control for high-risk payer, AI, infection-control, standing-order, and writeback settings.

### M27.3 Inputs and source systems
- EHR/FHIR resources and vendor-specific feeds relevant to virtual_room, telehealth_check, remote_device, rpm_alert, hybrid_visit.
- Practice-management/scheduling context, appointment metadata, patient demographics, and encounter state.
- Payer, eligibility, authorization, quality, registry, RTLS, sensor, messaging, device, or staff-task inputs when relevant.
- AI/RAG source documents, payer policies, clinic protocols, rule versions, and knowledge-graph evidence.
- User-entered corrections, patient-submitted forms, staff-verified data, and audit annotations.

### M27.4 Outputs and downstream effects
- Updated Visit Readiness Graph components and visible readiness score explanations.
- Role-based work queue tasks, SLA timers, escalation items, and huddle-board exceptions.
- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M27.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to telehealth, virtual rooming, remote monitoring, and hybrid care interface, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M27.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M27-01: Support telehealth, virtual pre-rooming, hybrid care, RPM/RTM device workflows, remote data capture, secure links, patient location, emergency backup, privacy, consent, and modality rules.
- FR-M27-02: Validate telehealth eligibility by payer, patient location, NP licensure/scope, modality, visit type, technology access, emergency contact, interpreter, and privacy before NP launch.
- FR-M27-03: Run virtual rooming for identity, location, consent, audio/video, who is present, home vitals, medication list, agenda, forms, patient-reported data, and safety concerns.
- FR-M27-04: Escalate medically unstable patients or unsafe telehealth situations to RN/NP and possible in-person/emergency workflow.
- FR-M27-05: Support RPM/RTM setup with device suitability, consent, data transmission, thresholds, alerts, monthly communication, troubleshooting, and device return/replacement.
- FR-M27-06: Publish telehealth.session.created, telehealth.preroom.completed, telehealth.modality.blocked, rpm.device.connected, remote.reading.received, and remote.alert.created events.
- FR-M27-07: Integrate with Patient Concierge, CareOps, Rooming, RevCycle, Access, EHR, messaging, device platform, and VirtualCare video provider.
- FR-M27-08: Expose VirtualCare console with schedule, waiting room, pre-rooming status, tech status, remote readings, alerts, and escalation controls.
- FR-M27-09: Use AI to summarize remote trends and draft patient instructions only with source links and clinician review for clinical significance.
- FR-M27-10: Prevent billing-ready state when telehealth consent, location, payer rule, or required modality evidence is missing.
- FR-M27-11: Calculate telehealth completion, failed connection, virtual rooming readiness, remote alert response, RPM adherence, device issues, and patient experience.
- FR-M27-12: Provide APIs for telehealth session, virtual rooming, consent, location verification, remote reading ingestion, alert, device assignment, and RPM status.
- FR-M27-13: Test out-of-state patient, failed video, interpreter telehealth, high BP remote reading, RPM setup, device no data, and telehealth payer rule conflict.
- FR-M27-14: Fail safely by converting to staff review or in-person workflow when telehealth cannot be safely or compliantly completed.
- FR-M27-15: Support SMS/web-first access rather than portal-only access.
- FR-M27-16: Preserve recordings only if explicitly configured and compliant; default is no recording.
- FR-M27-17: Feed QualityGuard, CareOps, and Analytics with remote data and completion outcomes.

### M27.7 Technical requirements and service design
- NFR-M27-01: P95 interactive API latency for core read operations should be <= 300 ms under expected production load, excluding external EHR/payer calls.
- NFR-M27-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M27-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.
- NFR-M27-04: PHI fields must be minimized in events; sensitive payloads are referenced by secure identifiers where possible.
- NFR-M27-05: The service must emit OpenTelemetry traces, structured logs, domain events, and KPI metrics for each state transition.

Service boundary requirements:
- The module should run as an independently deployable microservice or extractable bounded context.
- Transactional data should be stored in Azure SQL Database or Azure Database for PostgreSQL, according to the deployment's selected standard.
- Event publishing should use Azure Service Bus for command/workflow events and Azure Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry such as RTLS or device streams.
- Durable orchestration should use Temporal or Azure Durable Functions; the reference design uses Temporal for long-running workflows.
- Secrets and connection strings must live in Azure Key Vault; authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities wherever possible.
- Every external call must include correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, timeout, and circuit-breaker behavior.

### M27.8 UI surfaces and component behavior
- module summary card with red/yellow/green risk status
- work queue table with owner, SLA, priority, evidence, and next action
- patient/visit side panel with timeline, source links, and audit trail
- rule-result panel explaining why an action was recommended or blocked
- AI draft panel with source citations, confidence, user approval buttons, and edit history
- configuration page for authorized administrators with versioning and test mode

UI acceptance behavior:
- Red means action is required before safe completion or workflow continuation.
- Yellow means staff can resolve the issue during the current operating window.
- Green means the module has no unresolved readiness issue for the selected context.
- Black means the configured stop logic requires leadership, NP, physician, compliance, or flow-captain decision before proceeding.
- Every AI-generated text block must display source count, confidence level, last refresh time, and approval state.

### M27.9 Data model entities
- virtual_care_virtual_room: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- virtual_care_telehealth_check: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- virtual_care_remote_device: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- virtual_care_rpm_alert: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- virtual_care_hybrid_visit: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.

Required common fields on all module tables: `id`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`, `row_version`, `source_system`, `source_ref`, `confidence_score`, `audit_hash`, and `metadata_json`.

- FR-M28-04: Require dual approval for high-risk rules affecting payer/billing, medical necessity, standing orders, infection-control room release, AI writeback, patient financial messaging, or clinical escalation.

- FR-M28-17: Prevent staff from bypassing active rules without documented authorized exception.

- patient/visit side panel with timeline, source links, and audit trail
- rule-result panel explaining why an action was recommended or blocked
- AI draft panel with source citations, confidence, user approval buttons, and edit history
- configuration page for authorized administrators with versioning and test mode

UI acceptance behavior:
- Red means action is required before safe completion or workflow continuation.
- Yellow means staff can resolve the issue during the current operating window.
- Green means the module has no unresolved readiness issue for the selected context.
- Black means the configured stop logic requires leadership, NP, physician, compliance, or flow-captain decision before proceeding.
- Every AI-generated text block must display source count, confidence level, last refresh time, and approval state.

### M28.9 Data model entities
- rules_rule_set: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- rules_rule_version: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- rules_decision_table: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- rules_standing_order_protocol: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- rules_configuration_test: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.

### M28.10 API contract seeds
- GET /api/v1/aura-rules-studio/status?tenantId={tenantId}&siteId={siteId} - returns module health, counts, and risk distribution.
- GET /api/v1/aura-rules-studio/visits/{visitId} - returns the module-specific view for a visit.
- POST /api/v1/aura-rules-studio/visits/{visitId}/evaluate - runs rules, scoring, and AI-safe evaluation.

- RULES_STUDIO_PAYER_QUALI.EVALUATED.v1
- RULES_STUDIO_PAYER_QUALI.TASK_CREATED.v1
- RULES_STUDIO_PAYER_QUALI.STATE_CHANGED.v1
- RULES_STUDIO_PAYER_QUALI.EXCEPTION_RAISED.v1
- RULES_STUDIO_PAYER_QUALI.APPROVAL_RECORDED.v1
- RULES_STUDIO_PAYER_QUALI.DEFECT_LOGGED.v1

Every event uses the canonical envelope: `event_id`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id_hash`, `visit_id`, `producer`, `event_time`, `trace_id`, `idempotency_key`, `payload`, `sensitivity`, and `retention_class`.

### M28.12 AI, rules, and human-in-the-loop behavior
- Rules engine owns deterministic policy, payer, safety, standing-order, stop-logic, eligibility, SLA, and workflow gating decisions.
- Predictive ML may score risk, delay, no-show, denial, readmission, bottleneck, or readiness likelihood, but cannot itself authorize clinical, billing, or patient financial conclusions.
- LLM/RAG may summarize source material, draft messages, draft huddle items, and generate handoff content only with source links and staff verification.
- Optimization models may recommend room, staff, schedule, task, and equipment actions; medium/high-risk recommendations require approval.
- The module must support a simulation mode where rules and models run without writeback to validate impact and safety.

### M28.13 Stop logic, validation gates, and failure modes
- Stop logic is configurable by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, patient risk, infection-control status, and compliance risk.
- Hard stops block continuation until override; overrides require role, reason, source evidence, timestamp, and post-event review flag.
- Soft stops create visible warnings and tasks but allow flow to continue when configured.
- Failure modes include stale data, duplicate chart, payer ambiguity, external service outage, AI uncertainty, conflicting source records, and staff ownership gap.
- Downtime mode must preserve the minimum paper/PDF or cached workflow packet needed to safely continue clinic operations.

### M28.14 Integrations and FHIR/HL7/X12 mapping
- FHIR mappings should use Patient, Appointment, Encounter, Location, Practitioner, Task, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance, Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response, DocumentReference, DiagnosticReport, ServiceRequest, Procedure, CommunicationRequest, and QuestionnaireResponse as applicable.
- HL7 v2 mappings should support SIU scheduling, ADT, ORU results, ORM/orders, and custom vendor feed fallbacks.
- X12 mappings should include 270/271 eligibility and, where available, 278 prior authorization and 837/835/277CA revenue-cycle signals.
- Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks tracks must map the same canonical contract to vendor-specific endpoints, app launch mechanisms, webhook capabilities, and writeback limits.

### M28.15 Security, privacy, audit, and compliance controls
- Enforce tenant isolation, least privilege, just-in-time elevated access, session timeout, device/location controls where required, and break-glass audit review.
- Log who saw, changed, approved, rejected, exported, or wrote back each object.
- Treat staff location and productivity data as sensitive operational data; default to aggregate analytics unless individual visibility is operationally necessary.
- Prevent AI from exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users by applying authorization before retrieval, not only before display.
- Preserve all compliance evidence needed for billing, quality, infection-control, privacy, and AI governance review.

### M28.16 Analytics, KPIs, and observability
KPIs include completion rate, defect rate, SLA compliance, unresolved red/black items, source freshness, user override rate, AI acceptance rate, false-positive rate, false-negative defect rate, workflow cycle time, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, and equity variance. Observability must include traces, service metrics, domain-event lag, queue depth, retry volume, external-integration failure rate, model latency, and dashboard projection freshness.

### M28.17 Test cases and acceptance criteria
- TC-M28-01: Create a normal Rules Studio: Payer, Quality, Standing Orders, Infection, Workflow, SLAs, and UI Configuration workflow and verify state, task, event, audit, and readiness score updates.
- TC-M28-02: Inject missing source data and verify exception routing, huddle visibility, and no unsafe writeback.
- TC-M28-03: Simulate external EHR/payer/RTLS failure and verify retry, queueing, fallback UI, and user messaging.
- TC-M28-04: Attempt unauthorized access across roles and tenants and verify Entra/RBAC/ABAC enforcement.
- TC-M28-05: Generate an AI recommendation with low confidence and verify it is labeled, source-linked, and blocked from autonomous execution.
- TC-M28-06: Confirm all generated events exclude unnecessary PHI and include trace_id, tenant_id, entity_id, event_time, and schema_version.
- TC-M28-07: Validate dashboard KPI totals against raw events and service database projections.

Acceptance criteria:
- A user can understand the status of Rules Studio: Payer, Quality, Standing Orders, Infection, Workflow, SLAs, and UI Configuration for a visit in under 30 seconds without leaving the primary workflow.
- Every action has a named owner, deadline, source evidence, and audit trail.
- The module can operate in demo mode with synthetic EHR, payer, and RTLS fixtures.
- Medium/high-risk actions require approval from the configured role before EHR writeback or patient-facing communication.
- Defects from the module can be logged and routed into the Excellence Loop without manual spreadsheet tracking.

### M28.18 Codex implementation checklist
- Create module package, service interface, database migrations, DTOs, OpenAPI routes, event publishers, repository layer, permission policies, UI routes, shared components, tests, and seed fixtures.
- Implement synthetic fixtures for a Medicare Advantage AWV, TCM visit, chronic-disease follow-up, respiratory-risk same-day visit, telehealth visit, and non-autonomous NP chart-review scenario.
- Include mocked Epic, athenahealth/eClinicalWorks, eligibility, RTLS, SMS, and payment provider adapters.
- Create unit tests for rules, integration tests for API/event behavior, UI tests for role-specific screens, and safety tests for writeback restrictions.
- Ensure the module can be run locally with Docker Compose or dev containers using synthetic data and without real PHI.



## M29 - Continuous Improvement, Defect Learning, Training, and Institutional Excellence Loop

**Product surface:** AURA Excellence Loop.  
**Domain:** `improvement`.  
**Primary promise:** turns every failure and near miss into a redesigned process.

### M29.1 Functional purpose and institutional value
This module exists so that AURA ClinicOS can operationalize turns every failure and near miss into a
redesigned process. It must work for the primary-care reference implementation while also being configurable
for enterprise multispecialty deployment. The module is not a passive dashboard. It is a production control
layer that receives signals, applies rules, coordinates work, generates safe AI support, records outcomes, and
feeds continuous improvement. In the reference clinic, the module must support an NP-led model with four NPs
per site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, a collaborating physician reviewing charts for three non-
autonomous NPs, and a medical director responsible for operational clinical governance.

### M29.2 Users, permissions, and role bundling
Primary personas: NP, MA, front desk, flow captain, clinic manager, medical director, revenue integrity specialist, quality analyst, compliance/privacy lead, patient/caregiver. Small clinics may bundle roles, but the service must still store the true permission source and action provenance. Every screen must show only the minimum data necessary for the user's job. Supervising-physician and medical-director users require separate review, override, and attestation permissions. Administrative configuration requires dual-control for high-risk payer, AI, infection-control, standing-order, and writeback settings.

### M29.3 Inputs and source systems
- EHR/FHIR resources and vendor-specific feeds relevant to defect_log, root_cause, training_item, process_change, improvement_experiment.
- Practice-management/scheduling context, appointment metadata, patient demographics, and encounter state.
- Payer, eligibility, authorization, quality, registry, RTLS, sensor, messaging, device, or staff-task inputs when relevant.
- AI/RAG source documents, payer policies, clinic protocols, rule versions, and knowledge-graph evidence.
- User-entered corrections, patient-submitted forms, staff-verified data, and audit annotations.

### M29.4 Outputs and downstream effects
- Updated Visit Readiness Graph components and visible readiness score explanations.
- Role-based work queue tasks, SLA timers, escalation items, and huddle-board exceptions.
- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M29.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to continuous improvement, defect learning, training, and institutional excellence loop, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M29.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M29-01: Operate the no-blame excellence loop that converts defects, denials, delays, safety events, patient friction, quality misses, infection-control misses, and AI failures into system improvements.
- FR-M29-02: Capture pre-visit defects, NP discovery defects, revenue defects, quality defects, infection defects, flow defects, experience defects, integration defects, AI defects, and documentation defects.
- FR-M29-03: Assign each defect root cause, owner, severity, preventability, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, fix type, due date, and verification outcome.
- FR-M29-04: Create improvement actions including rule update, template change, training, workflow redesign, payer library update, integration fix, staffing adjustment, AI prompt/model change, or dashboard update.
- FR-M29-05: Publish defect.logged, rootcause.assigned, improvement.action.created, training.assigned, fix.verified, and excellence.metric.updated events.
- FR-M29-06: Expose Excellence console with defect log, root-cause board, weekly improvement rhythm, training tracker, protocol changes, and outcome verification.
- FR-M29-07: Integrate with every module’s defect signals, analytics, Rules Studio, training system, audit, and leadership dashboards.
- FR-M29-08: Use AI to cluster defects and draft improvement hypotheses, but require manager/compliance approval for protocol or policy changes.
- FR-M29-09: Calculate defect rate, preventable denial rate, NP discovery defects, huddle misses, patient friction, training completion, fix effectiveness, and recurrence.
- FR-M29-10: Provide APIs for defect logging, root-cause assignment, action creation, training assignment, verification, and improvement analytics.
- FR-M29-11: Test missing discharge summary, no-auth denial, dirty room, wrong visit type, AI hallucinated summary, duplicate chart, missing interpreter, and missed quality gap defects.
- FR-M29-12: Fail safely by escalating high-severity safety/compliance defects immediately rather than waiting for weekly review.
- FR-M29-13: Maintain a blameless culture in UI language while preserving accountability through owner and SLA.
- FR-M29-14: Convert repeated defects into candidate hard-stop or rule changes.
- FR-M29-15: Provide implementation coaching dashboards for onboarding new sites.
- FR-M29-16: Archive closed defects with evidence of fix and outcome verification.
- FR-M29-17: Use improvement metrics to move the clinic toward world-class performance.

### M29.7 Technical requirements and service design
- NFR-M29-01: P95 interactive API latency for core read operations should be <= 300 ms under expected production load, excluding external EHR/payer calls.
- NFR-M29-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M29-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.
- NFR-M29-04: PHI fields must be minimized in events; sensitive payloads are referenced by secure identifiers where possible.
- NFR-M29-05: The service must emit OpenTelemetry traces, structured logs, domain events, and KPI metrics for each state transition.

Service boundary requirements:
- The module should run as an independently deployable microservice or extractable bounded context.
- Transactional data should be stored in Azure SQL Database or Azure Database for PostgreSQL, according to the deployment's selected standard.
- Event publishing should use Azure Service Bus for command/workflow events and Azure Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry such as RTLS or device streams.
- Durable orchestration should use Temporal or Azure Durable Functions; the reference design uses Temporal for long-running workflows.
- Secrets and connection strings must live in Azure Key Vault; authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities wherever possible.
- Every external call must include correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, timeout, and circuit-breaker behavior.

- rule-result panel explaining why an action was recommended or blocked
- AI draft panel with source citations, confidence, user approval buttons, and edit history
- configuration page for authorized administrators with versioning and test mode

- Yellow means staff can resolve the issue during the current operating window.
- Green means the module has no unresolved readiness issue for the selected context.
- Black means the configured stop logic requires leadership, NP, physician, compliance, or flow-captain decision before proceeding.

### M30.6 Functional requirements

- FR-M30-02: For each playbook, specify scheduling logic, pre-visit tasks, eligibility/payer checks, forms, records, rooming, equipment/supplies, quality gaps, infection controls, NP decisions, charge candidates, and post-visit follow-up.
- FR-M30-03: Make playbooks executable by Rules Studio, PreVisit, Access, Rooming, QualityGuard, RevCycle, Auth, CareOps, InfectionShield, AssetOps, NP Cockpit, and Charge Integrity.

- FR-M30-07: Expose Playbook Studio with service definition, checklist, state machine, source rules, UI surfaces, API endpoints, events, tests, and KPIs.
- FR-M30-08: Use AI to draft playbook-specific summaries and patient instructions only from approved templates and source evidence.
- FR-M30-09: Prevent playbooks from implying a service should be billed solely because it was prepared; NP documentation and human approval determine final reporting.
- FR-M30-10: Calculate playbook readiness, completion, missed opportunity, denial, defect, outcome, and patient experience metrics.
- FR-M30-11: Provide APIs for playbook query, opportunity, service prep, checklist completion, state transition, and service defect.
- FR-M30-12: Test every initial service playbook with positive, negative, edge, payer-conflict, missing documentation, and patient-declination scenarios.
- FR-M30-13: Fail safely by requiring manual review when service-specific requirements conflict.
- FR-M30-14: Maintain playbook versions by payer, state, site, service line, and performance year.
- FR-M30-15: Support additions for specialty packs without changing core workflow contracts.
- FR-M30-16: Link playbooks to Codex backlog stories so implementation has no vague service scope.
- FR-M30-17: Prioritize Medicare Advantage/value-based primary care service capture and outcomes while preserving FFS/commercial/Medicaid configuration.

### M30.7 Technical requirements and service design
- NFR-M30-01: P95 interactive API latency for core read operations should be <= 300 ms under expected production load, excluding external EHR/payer calls.
- NFR-M30-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M30-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.
- NFR-M30-04: PHI fields must be minimized in events; sensitive payloads are referenced by secure identifiers where possible.
- NFR-M30-05: The service must emit OpenTelemetry traces, structured logs, domain events, and KPI metrics for each state transition.

Service boundary requirements:
- The module should run as an independently deployable microservice or extractable bounded context.
- Transactional data should be stored in Azure SQL Database or Azure Database for PostgreSQL, according to the deployment's selected standard.
- Event publishing should use Azure Service Bus for command/workflow events and Azure Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry such as RTLS or device streams.
- Durable orchestration should use Temporal or Azure Durable Functions; the reference design uses Temporal for long-running workflows.
- Secrets and connection strings must live in Azure Key Vault; authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities wherever possible.
- Every external call must include correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, timeout, and circuit-breaker behavior.

### M30.8 UI surfaces and component behavior
- module summary card with red/yellow/green risk status
- work queue table with owner, SLA, priority, evidence, and next action
- patient/visit side panel with timeline, source links, and audit trail
- rule-result panel explaining why an action was recommended or blocked
- AI draft panel with source citations, confidence, user approval buttons, and edit history
- configuration page for authorized administrators with versioning and test mode

UI acceptance behavior:
- Red means action is required before safe completion or workflow continuation.
- Yellow means staff can resolve the issue during the current operating window.
- Green means the module has no unresolved readiness issue for the selected context.
- Black means the configured stop logic requires leadership, NP, physician, compliance, or flow-captain decision before proceeding.
- Every AI-generated text block must display source count, confidence level, last refresh time, and approval state.

### M30.9 Data model entities
- service_playbooks_service_playbook: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- service_playbooks_eligibility_rule: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- service_playbooks_documentation_requirement: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- service_playbooks_workflow_step: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- service_playbooks_service_packet: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.

Required common fields on all module tables: `id`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`, `row_version`, `source_system`, `source_ref`, `confidence_score`, `audit_hash`, and `metadata_json`.

### M30.10 API contract seeds
- GET /api/v1/aura-playbooks/status?tenantId={tenantId}&siteId={siteId} - returns module health, counts, and risk distribution.
- GET /api/v1/aura-playbooks/visits/{visitId} - returns the module-specific view for a visit.
- POST /api/v1/aura-playbooks/visits/{visitId}/evaluate - runs rules, scoring, and AI-safe evaluation.
- POST /api/v1/aura-playbooks/tasks - creates a module-owned task with SLA, owner, evidence, and escalation path.
- PATCH /api/v1/aura-playbooks/tasks/{taskId} - updates task status, outcome, and audit notes.
- POST /api/v1/aura-playbooks/approvals - records human approval or rejection for medium/high-risk actions.
- GET /api/v1/aura-playbooks/audit?entityId={id} - returns immutable action, source, and user history.

### M30.11 Event contract seeds
- PRIMARY_CARE_SERVICE_PLA.EVALUATED.v1
- PRIMARY_CARE_SERVICE_PLA.TASK_CREATED.v1
- PRIMARY_CARE_SERVICE_PLA.STATE_CHANGED.v1
- PRIMARY_CARE_SERVICE_PLA.EXCEPTION_RAISED.v1
- PRIMARY_CARE_SERVICE_PLA.APPROVAL_RECORDED.v1
- PRIMARY_CARE_SERVICE_PLA.DEFECT_LOGGED.v1

Every event uses the canonical envelope: `event_id`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id_hash`, `visit_id`, `producer`, `event_time`, `trace_id`, `idempotency_key`, `payload`, `sensitivity`, and `retention_class`.

### M30.12 AI, rules, and human-in-the-loop behavior
- Rules engine owns deterministic policy, payer, safety, standing-order, stop-logic, eligibility, SLA, and workflow gating decisions.
- Predictive ML may score risk, delay, no-show, denial, readmission, bottleneck, or readiness likelihood, but cannot itself authorize clinical, billing, or patient financial conclusions.
- LLM/RAG may summarize source material, draft messages, draft huddle items, and generate handoff content only with source links and staff verification.
- Optimization models may recommend room, staff, schedule, task, and equipment actions; medium/high-risk recommendations require approval.
- The module must support a simulation mode where rules and models run without writeback to validate impact and safety.

### M30.13 Stop logic, validation gates, and failure modes
- Stop logic is configurable by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, patient risk, infection-control status, and compliance risk.
- Hard stops block continuation until override; overrides require role, reason, source evidence, timestamp, and post-event review flag.
- Soft stops create visible warnings and tasks but allow flow to continue when configured.
- Failure modes include stale data, duplicate chart, payer ambiguity, external service outage, AI uncertainty, conflicting source records, and staff ownership gap.
- Downtime mode must preserve the minimum paper/PDF or cached workflow packet needed to safely continue clinic operations.

### M30.14 Integrations and FHIR/HL7/X12 mapping
- FHIR mappings should use Patient, Appointment, Encounter, Location, Practitioner, Task, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance, Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response, DocumentReference, DiagnosticReport, ServiceRequest, Procedure, CommunicationRequest, and QuestionnaireResponse as applicable.
- HL7 v2 mappings should support SIU scheduling, ADT, ORU results, ORM/orders, and custom vendor feed fallbacks.
- X12 mappings should include 270/271 eligibility and, where available, 278 prior authorization and 837/835/277CA revenue-cycle signals.
- Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks tracks must map the same canonical contract to vendor-specific endpoints, app launch mechanisms, webhook capabilities, and writeback limits.

### M30.15 Security, privacy, audit, and compliance controls
- Enforce tenant isolation, least privilege, just-in-time elevated access, session timeout, device/location controls where required, and break-glass audit review.
- Log who saw, changed, approved, rejected, exported, or wrote back each object.
- Treat staff location and productivity data as sensitive operational data; default to aggregate analytics unless individual visibility is operationally necessary.
- Prevent AI from exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users by applying authorization before retrieval, not only before display.
- Preserve all compliance evidence needed for billing, quality, infection-control, privacy, and AI governance review.

### M30.16 Analytics, KPIs, and observability
KPIs include completion rate, defect rate, SLA compliance, unresolved red/black items, source freshness, user override rate, AI acceptance rate, false-positive rate, false-negative defect rate, workflow cycle time, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, and equity variance. Observability must include traces, service metrics, domain-event lag, queue depth, retry volume, external-integration failure rate, model latency, and dashboard projection freshness.

### M30.17 Test cases and acceptance criteria
- TC-M30-01: Create a normal Primary Care Service Playbook Engine workflow and verify state, task, event, audit, and readiness score updates.
- TC-M30-02: Inject missing source data and verify exception routing, huddle visibility, and no unsafe writeback.
- TC-M30-03: Simulate external EHR/payer/RTLS failure and verify retry, queueing, fallback UI, and user messaging.
- TC-M30-04: Attempt unauthorized access across roles and tenants and verify Entra/RBAC/ABAC enforcement.
- TC-M30-05: Generate an AI recommendation with low confidence and verify it is labeled, source-linked, and blocked from autonomous execution.
- TC-M30-06: Confirm all generated events exclude unnecessary PHI and include trace_id, tenant_id, entity_id, event_time, and schema_version.
- TC-M30-07: Validate dashboard KPI totals against raw events and service database projections.

Acceptance criteria:
- A user can understand the status of Primary Care Service Playbook Engine for a visit in under 30 seconds without leaving the primary workflow.
- Every action has a named owner, deadline, source evidence, and audit trail.
- The module can operate in demo mode with synthetic EHR, payer, and RTLS fixtures.
- Medium/high-risk actions require approval from the configured role before EHR writeback or patient-facing communication.
- Defects from the module can be logged and routed into the Excellence Loop without manual spreadsheet tracking.

### M30.18 Codex implementation checklist
- Create module package, service interface, database migrations, DTOs, OpenAPI routes, event publishers, repository layer, permission policies, UI routes, shared components, tests, and seed fixtures.
- Implement synthetic fixtures for a Medicare Advantage AWV, TCM visit, chronic-disease follow-up, respiratory-risk same-day visit, telehealth visit, and non-autonomous NP chart-review scenario.
- Include mocked Epic, athenahealth/eClinicalWorks, eligibility, RTLS, SMS, and payment provider adapters.
- Create unit tests for rules, integration tests for API/event behavior, UI tests for role-specific screens, and safety tests for writeback restrictions.
- Ensure the module can be run locally with Docker Compose or dev containers using synthetic data and without real PHI.



## M31 - Specialty Pack Framework and Enterprise Multispecialty Expansion

**Product surface:** AURA Specialty Packs.  
**Domain:** `specialty`.  
**Primary promise:** extends the platform beyond primary care without rebuilding the core.

### M31.1 Functional purpose and institutional value
This module exists so that AURA ClinicOS can operationalize extends the platform beyond primary care without
rebuilding the core. It must work for the primary-care reference implementation while also being configurable
for enterprise multispecialty deployment. The module is not a passive dashboard. It is a production control
layer that receives signals, applies rules, coordinates work, generates safe AI support, records outcomes, and
feeds continuous improvement. In the reference clinic, the module must support an NP-led model with four NPs
per site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, a collaborating physician reviewing charts for three non-
autonomous NPs, and a medical director responsible for operational clinical governance.

### M31.2 Users, permissions, and role bundling
Primary personas: NP, MA, front desk, flow captain, clinic manager, medical director, revenue integrity specialist, quality analyst, compliance/privacy lead, patient/caregiver. Small clinics may bundle roles, but the service must still store the true permission source and action provenance. Every screen must show only the minimum data necessary for the user's job. Supervising-physician and medical-director users require separate review, override, and attestation permissions. Administrative configuration requires dual-control for high-risk payer, AI, infection-control, standing-order, and writeback settings.

### M31.3 Inputs and source systems
- EHR/FHIR resources and vendor-specific feeds relevant to specialty_pack, specialty_workflow, specialty_measure, resource_template, routing_rule.
- Practice-management/scheduling context, appointment metadata, patient demographics, and encounter state.
- Payer, eligibility, authorization, quality, registry, RTLS, sensor, messaging, device, or staff-task inputs when relevant.
- AI/RAG source documents, payer policies, clinic protocols, rule versions, and knowledge-graph evidence.
- User-entered corrections, patient-submitted forms, staff-verified data, and audit annotations.

### M31.4 Outputs and downstream effects
- Updated Visit Readiness Graph components and visible readiness score explanations.
- Role-based work queue tasks, SLA timers, escalation items, and huddle-board exceptions.
- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M31.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to specialty pack framework and enterprise multispecialty expansion, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M31.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M31-01: Provide a reusable specialty-pack framework so primary care is fully specified while enterprise multispecialty workflows can be added without rewriting the platform.
- FR-M31-02: Define specialty packs for cardiology, oncology/infusion, orthopedics, behavioral health, urgent care, procedure-heavy clinics, and ambulatory surgery as configurable extensions.
- FR-M31-03: Allow each specialty pack to declare visit types, rooms/chairs, equipment, quality measures, payer/auth rules, infection controls, forms, service playbooks, charge candidates, and KPIs.
- FR-M31-04: Ensure specialty packs use the same canonical services: readiness graph, task/workflow, RTLS, RevCycle, QualityGuard, InfectionShield, CareOps, Copilot, Rules Studio, and Analytics.
- FR-M31-05: Publish specialtypack.installed, specialtypack.enabled, specialtypack.version.changed, specialty.workflow.created, and specialty.defect.logged events.
- FR-M31-06: Expose Specialty Pack Studio with templates, rule bundles, UI screens, integration requirements, test fixtures, and rollout status.
- FR-M31-07: Prevent specialty pack activation without required rules, RBAC, infection-control policies, payer libraries, screens, tests, and training materials.
- FR-M31-08: Use AI to generate initial specialty content only as draft requiring SME/compliance review.
- FR-M31-09: Provide APIs for specialty pack install, version, enable, disable, fixture run, and configuration export.
- FR-M31-10: Test cardiology ECG/echo, oncology infusion chair/lab/drug auth, orthopedics imaging, behavioral health PHQ/GAD/suicide, urgent care triage, and procedure turnover scenarios.
- FR-M31-11: Fail safely by limiting unconfigured specialty workflows to general primary-care behavior and manual tasking.
- FR-M31-12: Maintain separation of specialty rules from core platform rules while supporting inheritance and overrides.
- FR-M31-13: Calculate specialty performance across flow, revenue, quality, infection, access, and outcomes.
- FR-M31-14: Allow enterprise organizations to deploy multiple specialty packs per site/service line.
- FR-M31-15: Preserve primary-care reference implementation as the canonical v1 build target.
- FR-M31-16: Generate Codex backlog extensions for every specialty pack.
- FR-M31-17: Keep specialty packs auditable and versioned.

- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M32.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to supervision, medical director, credentialing, and chart review operations, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M32.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M32-01: Manage NP autonomy status, supervising/collaborating physician relationships, medical-director governance, credentialing, payer enrollment, chart review obligations, attestations, and supervision policy.
- FR-M32-02: Model the reference site: four NPs per site, owner NP autonomous, three non-autonomous NPs requiring collaborating physician chart reviews, medical director governing operations.
- FR-M32-03: Create chart-review queues by NP, payer, state, site, service, risk, timeframe, required percentage, and policy source.
- FR-M32-04: Route supervising physician tasks for chart review only and medical-director tasks for operational clinical governance, policy review, standing orders, escalations, and quality oversight.
- FR-M32-05: Track credentialing, enrollment, scope, delegation, standing-order eligibility, supervision rules, collaboration agreements, expiration dates, and required documentation.
- FR-M32-06: Publish supervision.relationship.created, chartreview.required, chartreview.completed, credential.expiring, scope.policy.changed, and medicaldirector.review.completed events.
- FR-M32-07: Expose Supervision Console with NP roster, autonomy status, review queues, credentialing, policy exceptions, overdue reviews, and audit evidence.
- FR-M32-08: Prevent scheduling, writeback, order suggestion approval, standing-order use, or billing readiness where required credentialing/supervision configuration is missing.
- FR-M32-09: Use AI only to summarize charts for review; physician/medical director decisions and attestations remain human actions.
- FR-M32-10: Integrate with NP Cockpit, Access, Rules Studio, Govern, Charge Integrity, QualityGuard, and compliance audit.
- FR-M32-11: Calculate chart-review timeliness, completion, findings, NP feedback loops, credentialing expiration, supervision defects, and policy exceptions.
- FR-M32-12: Provide APIs for supervision relationship, autonomy status, chart review queue, review completion, credential, policy exception, and audit export.
- FR-M32-13: Test autonomous owner NP, non-autonomous NP, expired collaboration agreement, missing credentialing, overdue chart review, and medical-director standing-order approval.
- FR-M32-14: Fail safely by blocking affected high-risk actions when supervision status is unknown or expired.
- FR-M32-15: Maintain state-law and payer-policy configuration without hardcoding legal conclusions.
- FR-M32-16: Ensure the application distinguishes review requirements from clinical control of the encounter.
- FR-M32-17: Generate compliance evidence for chart review and supervision audits.

### M32.7 Technical requirements and service design
- NFR-M32-01: P95 interactive API latency for core read operations should be <= 300 ms under expected production load, excluding external EHR/payer calls.
- NFR-M32-02: All write operations must be idempotent, tenant-scoped, traceable, and protected by Entra-backed RBAC/ABAC policy checks.
- NFR-M32-03: External integration failures must degrade to queue-based retry and visible worklist exceptions rather than silent data loss.
- NFR-M32-04: PHI fields must be minimized in events; sensitive payloads are referenced by secure identifiers where possible.
- NFR-M32-05: The service must emit OpenTelemetry traces, structured logs, domain events, and KPI metrics for each state transition.

Service boundary requirements:
- The module should run as an independently deployable microservice or extractable bounded context.
- Transactional data should be stored in Azure SQL Database or Azure Database for PostgreSQL, according to the deployment's selected standard.
- Event publishing should use Azure Service Bus for command/workflow events and Azure Event Hubs for high-volume telemetry such as RTLS or device streams.
- Durable orchestration should use Temporal or Azure Durable Functions; the reference design uses Temporal for long-running workflows.
- Secrets and connection strings must live in Azure Key Vault; authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID and managed identities wherever possible.
- Every external call must include correlation ID, idempotency key, retry policy, timeout, and circuit-breaker behavior.

### M32.8 UI surfaces and component behavior
- module summary card with red/yellow/green risk status
- work queue table with owner, SLA, priority, evidence, and next action
- patient/visit side panel with timeline, source links, and audit trail
- rule-result panel explaining why an action was recommended or blocked
- AI draft panel with source citations, confidence, user approval buttons, and edit history
- configuration page for authorized administrators with versioning and test mode

UI acceptance behavior:
- Red means action is required before safe completion or workflow continuation.
- Yellow means staff can resolve the issue during the current operating window.
- Green means the module has no unresolved readiness issue for the selected context.
- Black means the configured stop logic requires leadership, NP, physician, compliance, or flow-captain decision before proceeding.
- Every AI-generated text block must display source count, confidence level, last refresh time, and approval state.

### M32.9 Data model entities
- clinical_governance_supervision_assignment: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- clinical_governance_chart_review_queue: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- clinical_governance_credentialing_record: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- clinical_governance_medical_director_policy: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.
- clinical_governance_review_attestation: id, tenant_id, site_id, patient_id nullable, visit_id nullable, status, priority, source_system, source_ref, confidence_score, created_by, created_at, updated_at, row_version, metadata_json.

Required common fields on all module tables: `id`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`, `row_version`, `source_system`, `source_ref`, `confidence_score`, `audit_hash`, and `metadata_json`.

### M32.10 API contract seeds
- GET /api/v1/aura-supervision/status?tenantId={tenantId}&siteId={siteId} - returns module health, counts, and risk distribution.
- GET /api/v1/aura-supervision/visits/{visitId} - returns the module-specific view for a visit.
- POST /api/v1/aura-supervision/visits/{visitId}/evaluate - runs rules, scoring, and AI-safe evaluation.
- POST /api/v1/aura-supervision/tasks - creates a module-owned task with SLA, owner, evidence, and escalation path.
- PATCH /api/v1/aura-supervision/tasks/{taskId} - updates task status, outcome, and audit notes.
- POST /api/v1/aura-supervision/approvals - records human approval or rejection for medium/high-risk actions.
- GET /api/v1/aura-supervision/audit?entityId={id} - returns immutable action, source, and user history.

### M32.11 Event contract seeds
- SUPERVISION_MEDICAL_DIRE.EVALUATED.v1
- SUPERVISION_MEDICAL_DIRE.TASK_CREATED.v1
- SUPERVISION_MEDICAL_DIRE.STATE_CHANGED.v1
- SUPERVISION_MEDICAL_DIRE.EXCEPTION_RAISED.v1
- SUPERVISION_MEDICAL_DIRE.APPROVAL_RECORDED.v1
- SUPERVISION_MEDICAL_DIRE.DEFECT_LOGGED.v1

Every event uses the canonical envelope: `event_id`, `event_type`, `schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id_hash`, `visit_id`, `producer`, `event_time`, `trace_id`, `idempotency_key`, `payload`, `sensitivity`, and `retention_class`.

### M32.12 AI, rules, and human-in-the-loop behavior
- Rules engine owns deterministic policy, payer, safety, standing-order, stop-logic, eligibility, SLA, and workflow gating decisions.
- Predictive ML may score risk, delay, no-show, denial, readmission, bottleneck, or readiness likelihood, but cannot itself authorize clinical, billing, or patient financial conclusions.
- LLM/RAG may summarize source material, draft messages, draft huddle items, and generate handoff content only with source links and staff verification.
- Optimization models may recommend room, staff, schedule, task, and equipment actions; medium/high-risk recommendations require approval.
- The module must support a simulation mode where rules and models run without writeback to validate impact and safety.

### M32.13 Stop logic, validation gates, and failure modes
- Stop logic is configurable by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, patient risk, infection-control status, and compliance risk.
- Hard stops block continuation until override; overrides require role, reason, source evidence, timestamp, and post-event review flag.
- Soft stops create visible warnings and tasks but allow flow to continue when configured.
- Failure modes include stale data, duplicate chart, payer ambiguity, external service outage, AI uncertainty, conflicting source records, and staff ownership gap.
- Downtime mode must preserve the minimum paper/PDF or cached workflow packet needed to safely continue clinic operations.

### M32.14 Integrations and FHIR/HL7/X12 mapping
- FHIR mappings should use Patient, Appointment, Encounter, Location, Practitioner, Task, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance, Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response, DocumentReference, DiagnosticReport, ServiceRequest, Procedure, CommunicationRequest, and QuestionnaireResponse as applicable.
- HL7 v2 mappings should support SIU scheduling, ADT, ORU results, ORM/orders, and custom vendor feed fallbacks.
- X12 mappings should include 270/271 eligibility and, where available, 278 prior authorization and 837/835/277CA revenue-cycle signals.
- Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks tracks must map the same canonical contract to vendor-specific endpoints, app launch mechanisms, webhook capabilities, and writeback limits.

### M32.15 Security, privacy, audit, and compliance controls
- Enforce tenant isolation, least privilege, just-in-time elevated access, session timeout, device/location controls where required, and break-glass audit review.
- Log who saw, changed, approved, rejected, exported, or wrote back each object.
- Treat staff location and productivity data as sensitive operational data; default to aggregate analytics unless individual visibility is operationally necessary.
- Prevent AI from exposing sensitive data to unauthorized users by applying authorization before retrieval, not only before display.
- Preserve all compliance evidence needed for billing, quality, infection-control, privacy, and AI governance review.

### M32.16 Analytics, KPIs, and observability
KPIs include completion rate, defect rate, SLA compliance, unresolved red/black items, source freshness, user override rate, AI acceptance rate, false-positive rate, false-negative defect rate, workflow cycle time, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, and equity variance. Observability must include traces, service metrics, domain-event lag, queue depth, retry volume, external-integration failure rate, model latency, and dashboard projection freshness.

### M32.17 Test cases and acceptance criteria
- TC-M32-01: Create a normal Supervision, Medical Director, Credentialing, and Chart Review Operations workflow and verify state, task, event, audit, and readiness score updates.
- TC-M32-02: Inject missing source data and verify exception routing, huddle visibility, and no unsafe writeback.
- TC-M32-03: Simulate external EHR/payer/RTLS failure and verify retry, queueing, fallback UI, and user messaging.
- TC-M32-04: Attempt unauthorized access across roles and tenants and verify Entra/RBAC/ABAC enforcement.
- TC-M32-05: Generate an AI recommendation with low confidence and verify it is labeled, source-linked, and blocked from autonomous execution.
- TC-M32-06: Confirm all generated events exclude unnecessary PHI and include trace_id, tenant_id, entity_id, event_time, and schema_version.
- TC-M32-07: Validate dashboard KPI totals against raw events and service database projections.

Acceptance criteria:
- A user can understand the status of Supervision, Medical Director, Credentialing, and Chart Review Operations for a visit in under 30 seconds without leaving the primary workflow.
- Every action has a named owner, deadline, source evidence, and audit trail.
- The module can operate in demo mode with synthetic EHR, payer, and RTLS fixtures.
- Medium/high-risk actions require approval from the configured role before EHR writeback or patient-facing communication.
- Defects from the module can be logged and routed into the Excellence Loop without manual spreadsheet tracking.

### M32.18 Codex implementation checklist
- Create module package, service interface, database migrations, DTOs, OpenAPI routes, event publishers, repository layer, permission policies, UI routes, shared components, tests, and seed fixtures.
- Implement synthetic fixtures for a Medicare Advantage AWV, TCM visit, chronic-disease follow-up, respiratory-risk same-day visit, telehealth visit, and non-autonomous NP chart-review scenario.
- Include mocked Epic, athenahealth/eClinicalWorks, eligibility, RTLS, SMS, and payment provider adapters.
- Create unit tests for rules, integration tests for API/event behavior, UI tests for role-specific screens, and safety tests for writeback restrictions.
- Ensure the module can be run locally with Docker Compose or dev containers using synthetic data and without real PHI.



## M33 - Value-Based Contract, Risk, Stars, HEDIS, MIPS/MVP, and Payer Performance Studio

**Product surface:** AURA Value Studio.  
**Domain:** `value_based`.  
**Primary promise:** connects patient-level work to contract-level performance and revenue.

### M33.1 Functional purpose and institutional value
This module exists so that AURA ClinicOS can operationalize connects patient-level work to contract-level
performance and revenue. It must work for the primary-care reference implementation while also being
configurable for enterprise multispecialty deployment. The module is not a passive dashboard. It is a
production control layer that receives signals, applies rules, coordinates work, generates safe AI support,
records outcomes, and feeds continuous improvement. In the reference clinic, the module must support an NP-led
model with four NPs per site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, a collaborating physician reviewing
charts for three non-autonomous NPs, and a medical director responsible for operational clinical governance.

### M33.2 Users, permissions, and role bundling
Primary personas: NP, MA, front desk, flow captain, clinic manager, medical director, revenue integrity specialist, quality analyst, compliance/privacy lead, patient/caregiver. Small clinics may bundle roles, but the service must still store the true permission source and action provenance. Every screen must show only the minimum data necessary for the user's job. Supervising-physician and medical-director users require separate review, override, and attestation permissions. Administrative configuration requires dual-control for high-risk payer, AI, infection-control, standing-order, and writeback settings.

### M33.3 Inputs and source systems
- EHR/FHIR resources and vendor-specific feeds relevant to contract, performance_measure, risk_evidence, star_gap, payer_scorecard.
- Practice-management/scheduling context, appointment metadata, patient demographics, and encounter state.
- Payer, eligibility, authorization, quality, registry, RTLS, sensor, messaging, device, or staff-task inputs when relevant.
- AI/RAG source documents, payer policies, clinic protocols, rule versions, and knowledge-graph evidence.
- User-entered corrections, patient-submitted forms, staff-verified data, and audit annotations.

### M33.4 Outputs and downstream effects
- Updated Visit Readiness Graph components and visible readiness score explanations.
- Role-based work queue tasks, SLA timers, escalation items, and huddle-board exceptions.
- Approved EHR writebacks limited to tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and verified pre-visit data.
- Non-final charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, order suggestions, and documentation prompts requiring human approval.
- Module events for analytics, dashboards, defect learning, audit, AI monitoring, and revenue/quality/outcomes reporting.

### M33.5 Core functional workflows
1. Intake flow: receive raw signals relevant to value-based contract, risk, stars, hedis, mips/mvp, and payer performance studio, normalize them into canonical objects, and attach the result to the Visit Readiness Graph.
2. Decision flow: apply rules, role permissions, stop logic, readiness scoring, and AI confidence thresholds before routing work to the correct owner.
3. Execution flow: create tasks, update states, send approved messages, write back permitted data, and preserve full audit provenance.
4. Exception flow: detect missing evidence, overdue SLAs, conflicting sources, or compliance/safety risk; escalate to the correct human role.
5. Learning flow: convert defects, denials, delays, gaps, and user overrides into rule improvements, model features, training items, and dashboard signals.

### M33.6 Functional requirements
- FR-M33-01: Manage value-based contracts, Medicare Advantage performance, HEDIS/STARS, MIPS/MVP, ACO/contract measures, risk adjustment evidence, attribution, gaps, incentives, penalties, and payer performance.
- FR-M33-02: Load contract terms, measures, weights, performance years, attribution lists, gap files, risk adjustment rules, quality deadlines, and reporting requirements with source/version ownership.
- FR-M33-03: Connect panel opportunities, scheduling, PreVisit, QualityGuard, CareOps, RevCycle, Medication Sentinel, and Analytics to contract impact.
- FR-M33-04: Surface risk-adjustment evidence as clinical review prompts only; do not instruct diagnosis coding without NP assessment and documentation.
- FR-M33-05: Publish contract.loaded, attribution.updated, stars.gap.detected, risk.evidence.flagged, contract.performance.updated, and payer.opportunity.prioritized events.
- FR-M33-06: Expose Value-Based Studio with contract dashboard, gaps, attribution, risk evidence, quality performance, revenue opportunity, outreach prioritization, and export status.
- FR-M33-07: Use AI to summarize contract requirements and evidence conflicts with source links; compliance and clinical users approve interpretations.
- FR-M33-08: Prevent outdated contract/gap files from driving active workflows after expiration or supersession.
- FR-M33-09: Calculate Stars/HEDIS performance, MIPS/MVP readiness, AWV/TCM/care management impact, medication adherence, risk evidence review, avoidable utilization, and payer profitability.
- FR-M33-10: Provide APIs for contract import, measure mapping, attribution, gap file, risk evidence, performance snapshot, and payer export.
- FR-M33-11: Test MA quality gap file import, HEDIS gap closure, STARS med adherence, risk evidence review, attribution mismatch, and payer export.
- FR-M33-12: Fail safely by labeling contract data stale and stopping automation when source file dates or measure versions are invalid.
- FR-M33-13: Support mixed payer logic including MA/value-based first, Medicare FFS, commercial, Medicaid, FQHC, and direct primary care.
- FR-M33-14: Maintain patient-centered language and avoid revenue-pressure UI.
- FR-M33-15: Feed executive scorecards and no-blame defect loops.
- FR-M33-16: Map value-based priorities into Access scheduling and PreVisit work queues.
- FR-M33-17: Ensure Codex implements contract configuration rather than hardcoded payer assumptions.
