# 7B. End-to-End Workflow Blueprints

The following workflows show exactly how modules collaborate. Codex should implement them as durable workflow definitions with event-driven steps, task creation, timeout/escalation policies, UI touchpoints, and acceptance tests.

## AWV + Chronic Disease + Recent ED Follow-Up

| Step | System behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger | Panel Intelligence flags AWV due, diabetes/CKD monitoring due, recent ED visit, and transportation barrier. |
| Schedule | Scheduling module recommends extended AWV + follow-up slot, verifies continuity, interpreter need, and payer caveats. |
| Pre-visit | Pre-Visit OS creates HRA, PHQ, fall risk, home BP/glucose, med form, records request, quality gaps, financial clearance, and CHW task. |
| Records/meds | Records Agent pulls ED note/labs; Medication Sentinel flags missed antihypertensive refill and formulary/cost issue. |
| Huddle | Huddle Copilot lists patient as yellow/red if any record, transport, or HRA issue remains. |
| Rooming | MA repeats elevated BP, completes screenings, reconciles meds, checks vaccine registry, and pends protocol labs. |
| NP cockpit | NP receives decision-focused handoff with dizziness priority, elevated BP, labs due, med cost barrier, AWV readiness, and quality gaps. |
| Checkout/claim | Checkout schedules follow-up, closes education tasks, creates charge candidates and claim-readiness review. |
| Acceptance | NP should not discover missing ED record, HRA, transportation barrier, or medication cost issue for first time during encounter. |

## Transitional Care Management

| Step | System behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger | HL7 ADT or discharge report creates TCM candidate event. |
| Initial workflow | Care Management Engine creates RN contact task due within configured business-day window and Records Agent requests discharge data. |
| Medication | Medication Sentinel compares discharge meds, pre-admission meds, active EHR meds, and fill history. |
| Scheduling | Scheduler books face-to-face visit in appropriate window based on complexity and capacity. |
| RCM | Revenue Integrity checks duplicate TCM risk, required dates, and documentation fields. |
| Patient | Patient Concierge sends transition instructions and collects barriers, warning signs, and home needs. |
| Handoff | NP receives discharge diagnosis, med changes, pending tests, home-health/DME, contact status, and decisions needed. |
| Acceptance | TCM episode cannot be marked billing-ready unless contact, face-to-face date, med reconciliation, and duplicate-risk checks are complete or exceptioned. |

## Respiratory Symptom Direct-Rooming and Infection-Control Safe Flow

| Step | System behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger | Patient reports fever/cough in pre-arrival screen or front desk records symptoms. |
| Infection | InfectionShield sets direct-rooming required and PPE requirements. |
| Flow | Flow Optimizer selects a clean-ready room away from immunocompromised/high-risk patients and bypasses waiting room. |
| Patient | Patient Concierge sends direct-to-room instructions and masking message. |
| Rooming | MA sees PPE prompt and infection status; equipment used becomes dirty/cleaning-required after visit. |
| Cleaning | Room vacated event creates cleaning task with contact-time timer and isolation protocol. |
| Acceptance | Room cannot be assigned to another patient until cleaning/contact-time rules release it. |

## Prior Authorization Defect Before Visit

| Step | System behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger | Payer Rules detects auth required for scheduled diagnostic/procedure service. |
| Task | Auth Coordinator receives task with missing documents, payer criteria, deadline, and submission method. |
| AI | Auth Agent drafts packet from source evidence and marks missing clinical facts. |
| Escalation | If pending at 24-hour readiness lock, Visit Readiness becomes red and huddle item is created. |
| Decision | Flow Captain selects proceed, reschedule, convert, notice, or NP review according to policy. |
| Acceptance | Patient should not arrive unaware of a missing authorization for a nonurgent service. |

## RTLS Bottleneck Recovery

| Step | System behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger | Digital Twin detects provider delay, room dwell time, and downstream patients at risk. |
| Simulation | Flow Agent simulates staff redeployment, room reassignment, and patient sequence changes. |
| Recommendation | Command Center shows expected delay reduction, risks, affected patients, and approval requirement. |
| Action | Flow Captain accepts; tasks/messages/room assignments update. |
| Learning | System compares predicted vs actual recovery and updates intervention effectiveness. |
| Acceptance | No recommendation may violate infection-control, clinical safety, or patient dignity rules. |

## Telehealth Pre-Rooming and Modality Safety

| Step | System behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger | Telehealth appointment scheduled or in-person converted. |
| Pre-rooming | Virtual rooming verifies identity, location, emergency backup, privacy, technology, interpreter, consent, and payer caveats. |
| Data | Patient uploads home vitals/device data and medication list through secure channel. |
| Safety | Unstable symptoms or wrong jurisdiction/location creates RN/NP escalation and modality decision. |
| Cockpit | NP sees telehealth readiness, home readings, tech issues, and patient agenda. |
| Acceptance | Telehealth cannot start without location/emergency backup or approved exception. |

## Procedure Visit with Charge Integrity

| Step | System behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger | Procedure scheduled or ordered; room setup and payer rules evaluate. |
| Pre-visit | Auth/referral, consent, equipment, supplies, infection/cleaning, and patient estimate tasks are created. |
| Day of service | RTLS confirms procedure room dwell; equipment/supply use and documentation create charge candidates. |
| Post-visit | Charge Integrity checks consent, procedure note, diagnosis support, modifiers, supplies, and claim readiness. |
| Acceptance | Charge candidate cannot become approved charge without required documentation and human review. |

## Patient Barrier and No-Show Risk

| Step | System behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger | Risk engine predicts late/no-show; patient reports transportation or digital access barrier. |
| Task | CHW/Social Worker task created with patient preference and deadline. |
| Patient | Concierge offers ride support, telehealth conversion if safe, phone intake, or caregiver support. |
| Scheduling | Visit readiness updates and slot risk decreases if barrier resolved. |
| Acceptance | Barrier status is visible at huddle and not rediscovered at check-in. |

## AI Handoff Verification and Correction

| Step | System behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger | NP Handoff Composer drafts handoff from chart, records, forms, and tasks. |
| Verification | MA reviews each section with source links; unverified AI facts remain labeled draft. |
| Correction | Staff rejects an incorrect sentence, records reason, and updates source fact/conflict. |
| Learning | AI feedback event enters evaluation queue and prompt/model monitoring. |
| Acceptance | NP never sees unverified AI content as if it were verified fact. |

## Denial Learning Loop

| Step | System behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger | 835/denial event received or denial entered by billing team. |
| Classification | Revenue Integrity Agent classifies denial as front-end, auth, eligibility, medical necessity, documentation, coding, timely filing, or payer error. |
| Root cause | Owner is assigned; payer rule, checklist, workflow, training, or template fix is linked. |
| Prevention | Rule Studio updates rule and replays historical cases to estimate impact. |
| Acceptance | Repeat preventable denials are visible on executive dashboard and require corrective action. |

# 8. AI Agent Platform and Automation Boundaries

The AI layer is powerful because it is constrained. AURA uses AI to detect, summarize, draft, rank, recommend, and simulate. The platform does not allow AI to silently diagnose, bill, deny care, decide medical necessity, override infection-control protocols, or pressure patients financially.

## 8.1 Agent registry

| Agent | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Panel Pathfinder | Find due/overdue/high-risk/recently discharged patients and recommend outreach. |
| Visit-Type Agent | Classify scheduling request and suggest slot/modality/service opportunities. |
| Clearance Agent | Detect eligibility, benefits, estimate, GFE, ABN, and financial clearance gaps. |
| Auth/Referral Agent | Map payer rules to patient/service evidence and draft auth packets. |
| Records Agent | Retrieve, summarize, and track external documents, HIE data, and pending diagnostics. |
| Chart Scrub Agent | Create pre-visit packet and readiness defects from source-linked data. |
| Quality Agent | Explain care gaps and route appropriate pre-visit/rooming quality tasks. |
| Medication Sentinel | Summarize med list changes, adherence, cost, formulary, and high-risk issues. |
| Care Management Agent | Identify TCM/CCM/APCM/PCM/RPM/BHI/CHI/PIN readiness and consent tasks. |
| Social Barrier Agent | Detect transportation, food, housing, caregiver, literacy, and digital access barriers. |
| InfectionShield Agent | Recommend routing, cleaning, PPE, equipment status, and exposure investigations. |
| Flow Agent | Detect bottlenecks, simulate interventions, and recommend room/staff sequencing. |
| Huddle Copilot | Produce morning exception brief and owner assignments. |
| Rooming Copilot | Generate dynamic intake checklist and red-flag escalation reminders. |
| NP Handoff Composer | Draft concise, source-linked, staff-verifiable NP handoff. |
| Revenue Integrity Agent | Detect charge candidates, documentation gaps, claim-readiness issues, and denial patterns. |
| Executive Insight Agent | Explain KPI movement, root causes, and improvement opportunities. |
| Compliance Sentinel | Detect unsafe AI, privacy, scope, billing, infection-control, and configuration risks. |

## 8.2 AI output schema

```typescript
interface AiRecommendation {
  id: string;
  tenantId: string;
  agentId: string;
  modelVersion: string;
  promptVersion: string;
  subjectType: 'visit' | 'patient' | 'task' | 'room' | 'claim' | 'rule' | 'dashboard';
  subjectId: string;
  recommendationType: string;
  summary: string;
  rationale: string;
  sourceFacts: SourceFactRef[];
  confidence: number; // 0-1
  riskLevel: 'LOW_AUTO' | 'MEDIUM_APPROVAL' | 'HIGH_AUTHORIZED_APPROVAL' | 'CRITICAL_ESCALATE_ONLY';
  allowedActions: string[];
  prohibitedActions: string[];
  requiresHumanRole?: string;
  expiresAt?: string;
  status: 'DRAFT' | 'PENDING_APPROVAL' | 'APPROVED' | 'REJECTED' | 'EXPIRED';
  audit: { createdAt: string; createdBy: 'AI'; correlationId: string; };
}
```

## 8.3 Automation risk tiers

| Risk tier | Examples | Automation rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Low | Create routine form reminder; update dashboard; create internal low-risk task. | Can auto-execute if template/rule-approved and audit logged. |
| Medium | Send patient message with individualized content; reassign noncritical task; mark minor readiness issue. | Draft or perform only with staff approval depending on configuration. |
| High | Change visit sequence, create financial notice, draft auth packet, recommend care-management enrollment, route patient due to infection risk. | Requires authorized role approval and source review. |
| Critical | Clinical triage escalation, suicide-risk workflow, withholding/canceling nonurgent service due to auth, exposure investigation notification. | Escalate only; no autonomous final action. |

## 8.4 Model governance requirements

- Every model/agent has a model card, prompt card, data sources list, intended use, prohibited use, validation evidence, monitoring plan, rollback plan, and owner.
- Predictive models must run silently before activation, comparing recommendations to actual outcomes and human judgments.
- AI summaries must preserve uncertainty and label conflicts. If a source conflict exists, the summary should state the conflict rather than resolve it silently.
- High-impact recommendations must include source facts and rule/model explanations; users must be able to accept, reject, edit, and provide reason.
- The product maintains a regulatory boundary register that classifies features as operational support, administrative support, DSI/CDS, or potential device software for compliance review.

# 9. API, Event, Integration, and FHIR/X12 Specifications

## 9.1 API conventions

- Base path: /api/v1.
- Every request requires tenant context, authenticated user, role claims, and correlation_id.
- Use idempotency keys for POST operations that can be retried by integrations or workflow timers.
- All create/update operations return both resource state and emitted event ids.
- Use optimistic concurrency with version fields for high-contention objects such as tasks, room state, readiness score, and handoff packets.
- Use standardized errors: VALIDATION_ERROR, PERMISSION_DENIED, ILLEGAL_STATE_TRANSITION, EXTERNAL_SYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE, POLICY_REVIEW_REQUIRED, AI_APPROVAL_REQUIRED.

| External standard/interface | AURA usage |

| HL7 v2 ADT/SIU/ORM/ORU | ADT discharge events, scheduling, orders, and results in legacy environments. |
| X12 270/271 | Eligibility and benefits checks through clearinghouse/payer channels. |
| X12 276/277 | Claim status workflows. |
| X12 278 / payer APIs | Prior authorization workflows where applicable. |
| X12 837/835 | Claims/remittance analytics, denial learning, and claim readiness feedback loops. |
| RTLS vendor API/MQTT | Location observations for patients, staff, rooms, and assets. |
| Immunization registry | Vaccine history, forecast, and gap validation. |
| Patient messaging APIs | SMS, email, voice, portal, push notifications, consent-aware communications. |

# 10. Security, Privacy, Compliance, and Governance

AURA handles ePHI, financial information, staff operational data, location data, AI-generated summaries, and patient communications. Security and governance are not optional modules; they are cross-cutting requirements for every feature.

## 10.1 Security controls

- Encryption in transit and at rest for all PHI, documents, tokens, and credentials.
- OIDC/SAML SSO, MFA, device trust, session timeout, and privileged access management.
- RBAC plus ABAC for patient, site, role, relationship, data sensitivity, encounter state, and emergency/break-glass context.
- Comprehensive audit logs for PHI views, edits, AI outputs, location lookups, rule changes, configuration changes, and integration write-backs.
- Secrets manager for integration credentials and certificate rotation.
- Data retention policies for RTLS, messages, documents, logs, AI runs, and audit data.
- Business associate agreement readiness, security risk assessment support, incident response runbooks, and breach investigation logs.

## 10.2 Compliance boundaries

- Revenue workflows support compliant service capture and denial prevention, not upcoding, unnecessary care, duplicate billing, or coercive collections.
- Risk-adjustment prompts show evidence to review, not instructions to code. Final clinical assessment belongs to the NP or qualified clinician.
- Care-management workflows track consent, initiating visit, care plan, time/activity requirements, duplicate billing risk, and payer-specific requirements.
- Infection-control rules override throughput and room utilization recommendations.
- Patient-facing financial communications are template-governed and routed to financial counselor when complex or sensitive.
- AI-generated clinical or financial outputs are drafts unless explicitly verified by authorized human users.
- State scope-of-practice, payer contracts, credentialing, incident-to, supervision, and billing rules must be configured by jurisdiction/customer.

## 10.3 Safety hierarchy

```text
1. Clinical safety
2. Infection-control safety
3. Privacy/security and minimum necessary access
4. Scope-of-practice and supervision
5. Regulatory, payer, and billing compliance
6. Patient dignity, equity, and financial assistance protections
7. Quality and outcomes
8. Flow efficiency
9. Revenue integrity
10. Staff productivity
```

# 11. Analytics, KPIs, Command Centers, and Executive Outcomes System

AURA is designed to manage by data, not anecdote. Every module exposes operational, quality, revenue, safety, patient-experience, equity, and AI-governance metrics. The executive system should make the clinic's world-class trajectory visible every day.

| Dashboard | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Pre-Visit Command Center | Tomorrow's schedule, readiness colors, open defects, missing records, forms, auth, estimates, quality gaps, infection screens, and huddle agenda. |
| Flow Command Center | Live map, patient states, rooms, staff load, equipment, wait predictions, bottlenecks, and interventions. |
| Revenue Readiness Dashboard | Eligibility, estimates, GFE, auth/referral, ABN/notice, charge candidates, claim readiness, denials, and pre-bill holds. |
| Quality and Outcomes Dashboard | Care gaps, measure performance, chronic outcomes, transitions, screenings, immunizations, structured exclusions, and equity. |
| InfectionShield Dashboard | Room states, cleaning backlog, PPE, direct-rooming, exposure investigations, equipment cleaning, and crowding. |
| Care Management Dashboard | TCM, CCM/APCM/PCM/RPM/BHI/CHI/PIN opportunities, consent, active care plans, activities, and outcomes. |
| AI Governance Dashboard | Model status, silent-mode performance, source coverage, overrides, drift, incidents, and approvals. |
| Executive Excellence Board | Top KPIs, trends, site comparisons, revenue leakage, quality gains, patient trust, throughput, equity, and strategic opportunities. |

# 12. Testing, QA, Validation, and Acceptance Criteria

Testing must prove that AURA is safe, reliable, auditable, and useful before production activation. Build tests at unit, integration, contract, workflow, simulation, UI, security, AI evaluation, and UAT levels.

## 12.1 Test suites

- Unit tests: rule conditions/actions, readiness scoring, state transitions, data validators, permission checks, event schema validators.
- Integration tests: FHIR/HL7/X12 mappings, RTLS ingest, messaging delivery, eligibility mock responses, auth mock flows, EHR launch context.
- Workflow tests: TCM, AWV, chart scrub, huddle, check-in, rooming, infection cleaning, claim readiness, pre-bill hold, denial learning.
- UI tests: role-specific dashboards, cockpit, work queues, handoff editor, command centers, patient forms, mobile views.
- Security tests: tenant isolation, role access, break-glass, audit logs, consent/ROI enforcement, staff location privacy.
- AI tests: source attribution, hallucination detection, prompt injection defense, output risk tiering, approval flows, bias/drift monitoring.
- Performance tests: RTLS high-volume ingest, dashboard live updates, event replay, huddle board load, analytics refresh, search latency.
- Downtime tests: manual export/print, queue recovery, integration outage fallback, event replay after recovery.

## 12.2 Definition of done for every module

- Database migrations and seed fixtures exist.
- API endpoints have OpenAPI schemas, authorization policies, validation, error handling, and tests.
- Events have schema definitions, producers, consumers, idempotency, and replay tests.
- UI screens are role-scoped, responsive, accessible, and instrumented.
- Rules are configurable, versioned, testable, and auditable.
- AI features are optional, source-linked, risk-tiered, monitored, and human-reviewable.
- Operational logs, metrics, traces, and dashboards exist.
- Acceptance criteria in the module section pass in staging/UAT.

## 12.3 UAT scenarios

- 72-year-old Medicare Advantage patient due for AWV, diabetes/CKD monitoring, recent ED dizziness visit, transportation barrier, medication cost issue, and vaccine uncertainty.
- TCM patient discharged from hospital with pending labs, medication changes, home-health need, and required interactive contact workflow.
- Same-day respiratory-symptom patient requiring direct rooming, PPE, room cleaning, and waiting-room bypass.
- Procedure visit with prior auth requirement, consent, room setup, equipment status, charge candidate, and claim readiness.
- Telehealth chronic-care visit with patient location, emergency backup, device data, payer caveat, and virtual rooming.
- No-show-risk patient with transportation and digital divide barriers; system routes CHW and alternate intake path.
- Auth denial discovered 24 hours before visit; system routes decision options and prevents surprise at check-in.
- AI-generated handoff contains a source conflict; staff rejects incorrect sentence and logs AI feedback.

## Appendix B: Sample rule definitions

```text
rule TCM_INTERACTIVE_CONTACT_REQUIRED v1 {
  when visit.type == 'TCM' and discharge.date exists and tcm.first_successful_contact is null
  then create_task(
    queue='RN_CARE_MANAGER',
    severity='RED',
    due_at=business_days_after(discharge.date, 2),
    title='Complete TCM interactive contact',
    completion_criteria=['contact_attempt_documented', 'patient_needs_addressed_or_escalated']
  )
}

rule ROOM_ASSIGNMENT_REQUIRES_INFECTION_READY v1 {
  when visit.room_assignment_requested == true
  require room.operational_state in ['AVAILABLE']
  require room.infection_state == 'CLEAN_READY'
  require room.equipment_profile satisfies visit.required_equipment
  else block_action('Room is not assignable; infection/operational readiness failed')
}

rule AWV_HRA_REQUIRED v1 {
  when visit.type in ['AWV_INITIAL','AWV_SUBSEQUENT'] and questionnaire.HRA.status != 'COMPLETE'
  then create_task(queue='MA_PREVISIT', severity='YELLOW', title='Complete HRA before AWV')
}

rule ESTIMATE_SELF_PAY_REQUIRED v1 {
  when coverage.status == 'SELF_PAY' and appointment.scheduled_more_than_threshold == true
  then create_task(queue='FINANCIAL_COUNSELOR', severity='RED', title='Deliver Good Faith Estimate workflow')
}
```

## Appendix E: Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| RTLS | Real-time location system used to infer patient/staff/equipment/room location and dwell time. |
| Visit Readiness Graph | The canonical graph linking all facts, tasks, states, and decisions for a visit. |
| Readiness defect | Any unresolved issue that can affect care, flow, revenue, quality, infection control, or patient experience. |
| NP handoff | The concise, source-linked packet delivered immediately before the NP enters or launches the encounter. |
| Charge candidate | A potential service/supply charge signal that requires documentation and human review before billing. |
| Clean-ready room | A room satisfying operational, cleaning, contact-time, equipment, and infection-control requirements. |
| AI run | A logged execution of an AI agent with prompt, model, sources, output, risk level, and review status. |
| Defect learning | No-blame process of turning missed preparation, flow, quality, revenue, infection, or AI issues into process fixes. |

# 15. Version 4 Deep Functional and Technical Module Build Specifications


## M00 - Platform Shell, Tenant Administration, and Configuration Studio

### Module purpose and operating role

**Mission.** Provide the multi-tenant application shell, tenant configuration, sites/clinics/pods, feature flags, rule packs, branding, localization, and admin controls that make AURA configurable without code changes.

**Primary implementation package/service:** `platform-admin`.

**Primary functional domain:** configuration versioning, tenant hierarchy, rule pack governance, feature flags.

**Primary personas:** System Admin, Tenant Admin, Implementation Lead, Compliance Lead, IT/Automation Analyst.

**Why this module matters to institutional excellence.** This module converts a historically fragmented clinic function into an owned, measurable, auditable software workflow. It must improve quality, outcomes, flow, safety, patient experience, staff reliability, and appropriate compliant revenue without creating unsafe automation or administrative burden.

### Functional scope

- Tenant onboarding wizard
- Clinic/site/pod/team hierarchy
- Role and feature-flag configuration
- Rule-pack versioning
- Template builder for handoffs, forms, tasks, messages, and dashboards
- Environment and integration status dashboard
- Configuration audit and rollback
- Payer/quality/infection rule governance calendar

### Key lifecycle states

- `draft`
- `validated`
- `approved`
- `published`
- `rolled_back`
- `disabled`

### User stories

- As a **primary user**, I can see the current state, risk level, owner, next action, and source evidence for this module without searching multiple systems.
- As a **queue owner**, I can claim, complete, defer, reassign, or escalate module work with required evidence and audit logging.
- As a **manager/flow captain**, I can identify aging work, bottlenecks, defect patterns, and patients/visits at risk.
- As a **compliance or governance user**, I can trace every recommendation, rule firing, AI output, override, and external write-back to source evidence.
- As **Codex**, I can implement this module by creating the service package, database models, API routes, event handlers, UI screens, permissions, tests, and telemetry described here.

### Feature implementation cards


#### Feature 1: Tenant onboarding wizard

- **User behavior:** Users can initiate, view, update, complete, defer, or escalate this capability according to role. The UI must display current state, owner, due date, source evidence, unresolved blockers, and next best action.
- **System behavior:** The service evaluates relevant rules, writes a state record, emits a module event, updates the Visit Readiness Graph when patient/visit-specific, and creates downstream tasks when prerequisites are missing.
- **Data contract:** Persist a feature-specific record linked to one or more of: `Tenant, Site, ClinicPod, FeatureFlag, ConfigSet`. Include `tenant_id`, `status`, `source_refs`, `confidence`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `version`, and audit correlation.

### API contracts


### API: `GET /tenants/{id}/config`

- **Auth:** require tenant-scoped authenticated user/service account and module-specific permission.
- **Request validation:** validate path IDs, tenant ownership, required body fields, idempotency key for mutating methods, and state transition rules.
- **Response:** return typed DTO with `id`, `status`, `links`, `source_refs`, `audit_correlation_id`, and `next_actions` where applicable.
- **Side effects:** write audit log; for mutating endpoints emit state-change event; update VisitGraph/readiness when patient or visit context changes.
- **Failure handling:** return one of `VALIDATION_ERROR, ACCESS_DENIED, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, RULE_BLOCKED, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE, DOWNSTREAM_FAILURE, STALE_DATA, DUPLICATE_EVENT` with remediation details.

### Events and event handlers


### Event: `tenant.created`

- **Trigger:** emitted when the module reaches the corresponding lifecycle milestone or when an external integration normalizes that state.
- **Payload minimum:** `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id` if applicable, `visit_id` if applicable, module object ID, previous status, new status, source refs, actor, occurred_at, and idempotency key.
- **Consumers:** Visit Readiness Graph, Workflow Engine, Analytics, Audit, and any module that depends on this state.
- **Idempotency:** event handler must ignore duplicate `event_id`/`idempotency_key` and avoid duplicate task or fact creation.

### AI, rules, and automation

- Suggest configuration defaults from clinic profile
- Detect inconsistent rule settings
- Draft implementation checklist
- Summarize configuration drift

**Automation boundary.** AI and rules may detect, summarize, draft, rank, or recommend. Human approval is required when the action affects diagnosis, treatment, clinical triage, medical necessity, billing/coding, payer notice, patient financial obligation, infection-control clearance, patient safety, staff discipline, or external write-back beyond approved low-risk workflows.

### UI implementation requirements

- Provide module landing page with list/board view, filters, status counts, aging/SLA indicators, and role-based next actions.
- Provide detail drawer/page for every module object with status history, source evidence, tasks, related VisitGraph facts, audit trail, and comments.
- Provide create/edit/complete/defer/escalate dialogs with required validation and accessible form design.
- Provide empty states, error states, loading skeletons, offline/degraded banners for integration outages, and keyboard-accessible controls.
- Provide contextual launch links from schedule, pre-visit board, huddle, rooming, NP cockpit, flow board, analytics, and related modules.

### Permissions and access control

- platform-admin.read
- platform-admin.write
- platform-admin.manage
- platform-admin.override
- platform-admin.export

Every permission must be evaluated with tenant, site, pod, care relationship, purpose of access, sensitivity tags, consent restrictions, and module-specific policy.

### Observability

- Metrics: request count, latency, error rate, queue size, object count by status, event handler lag, duplicate event count, task aging, automation acceptance/rejection, and user override rate.
- Logs: structured, correlation-ID-linked, PHI-minimized logs for service actions and integration events.
- Traces: distributed traces for API -> service -> repository -> event publication -> workflow handling.
- Alerts: stale data, SLA breach, integration degradation, failed write-back, unexpected event volume, elevated override rate, and policy-denied spikes.

### KPIs and management dashboards

- configuration change lead time
- rollback count
- unreviewed rules
- integration uptime
- tenant onboarding time

### Security, safety, and compliance controls

- Apply RBAC/ABAC and field-level filtering before data leaves the service.
- Store all changes with audit log and immutable event history.
- Require reason and approval for overrides that affect safety, billing, privacy, infection, or clinical workflow.
- Preserve source links and rule/model version for every recommendation.
- Apply tenant retention policy and data minimization.
- Provide downtime/degraded mode behavior where the module is critical to same-day operations.

### Failure modes and edge cases

- External integration unavailable: show stale data banner, use manual fallback, keep task open, and record integration outage.
- Duplicate inbound event: ignore idempotently and do not duplicate tasks/facts/candidates.
- Conflicting source data: create conflict item, downgrade confidence/readiness, assign owner, and show source comparison.
- Stale data: block high-risk decision or mark advisory only until refreshed.
- Unauthorized access: deny, audit, and display minimal safe error message.
- User override: require reason, log audit, emit override event, and route to review if high risk.

### Acceptance criteria

- Tenant admin can configure clinic pods, roles, queues, and SLAs without developer intervention.
- Every configuration change creates a versioned audit record with editor, reason, timestamp, diff, and rollback option.
- Published rule packs can be tested in sandbox before production activation.

### Required tests

- Unit tests for validators, state transitions, rule evaluation, access policy, and idempotency.
- API tests for each endpoint, including happy path, validation failure, access denial, stale data, duplicate idempotency key, and invalid transition.
- Event tests for each consumed/published event, including replay and duplicate handling.
- UI tests for board/list, detail view, create/edit/complete/defer/escalate, permissions, and accessibility.
- Integration tests with mocked external systems when the module reads or writes external data.
- AI tests for source citation, output schema validation, human-review workflow, and blocked high-risk automation when applicable.

## M01 - Identity, Access, RBAC/ABAC, Consent, and Privacy Enforcement

### Module purpose and operating role

**Mission.** Protect ePHI and operational data through SSO, MFA, role-based and attribute-based access, minimum-necessary enforcement, break-glass access, consent-aware visibility, and full auditability.

**Primary implementation package/service:** `identity-access`.

**Primary functional domain:** RBAC/ABAC, consent, privacy preferences, break-glass, audit.

**Primary personas:** All Staff, Compliance Lead, Privacy Officer, Security Admin, Auditor.

**Why this module matters to institutional excellence.** This module converts a historically fragmented clinic function into an owned, measurable, auditable software workflow. It must improve quality, outcomes, flow, safety, patient experience, staff reliability, and appropriate compliant revenue without creating unsafe automation or administrative burden.

### Functional scope

- OIDC/SAML SSO
- MFA policy
- RBAC role matrix
- ABAC based on clinic, pod, patient relationship, data sensitivity, location, and emergency state
- Break-glass workflow
- Consent and ROI enforcement
- Caregiver/guardian access tracking
- PHI view audit logs
- Staff-location privacy policy controls
- Session timeout and device trust

### Key lifecycle states

- `provisioned`
- `active`
- `suspended`
- `break_glass_open`
- `break_glass_closed`

### User stories

- As a **primary user**, I can see the current state, risk level, owner, next action, and source evidence for this module without searching multiple systems.
- As a **queue owner**, I can claim, complete, defer, reassign, or escalate module work with required evidence and audit logging.
- As a **manager/flow captain**, I can identify aging work, bottlenecks, defect patterns, and patients/visits at risk.
- As a **compliance or governance user**, I can trace every recommendation, rule firing, AI output, override, and external write-back to source evidence.
- As **Codex**, I can implement this module by creating the service package, database models, API routes, event handlers, UI screens, permissions, tests, and telemetry described here.

### Feature implementation cards


#### Feature 1: OIDC/SAML SSO

- **User behavior:** Users can initiate, view, update, complete, defer, or escalate this capability according to role. The UI must display current state, owner, due date, source evidence, unresolved blockers, and next best action.
- **System behavior:** The service evaluates relevant rules, writes a state record, emits a module event, updates the Visit Readiness Graph when patient/visit-specific, and creates downstream tasks when prerequisites are missing.
- **Data contract:** Persist a feature-specific record linked to one or more of: `User, Role, Permission, Policy, AccessGrant`. Include `tenant_id`, `status`, `source_refs`, `confidence`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `version`, and audit correlation.

### API contracts


### API: `GET /me`

- **Auth:** require tenant-scoped authenticated user/service account and module-specific permission.
- **Request validation:** validate path IDs, tenant ownership, required body fields, idempotency key for mutating methods, and state transition rules.
- **Response:** return typed DTO with `id`, `status`, `links`, `source_refs`, `audit_correlation_id`, and `next_actions` where applicable.
- **Side effects:** write audit log; for mutating endpoints emit state-change event; update VisitGraph/readiness when patient or visit context changes.
- **Failure handling:** return one of `VALIDATION_ERROR, ACCESS_DENIED, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, RULE_BLOCKED, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE, DOWNSTREAM_FAILURE, STALE_DATA, DUPLICATE_EVENT` with remediation details.


### API: `POST /auth/break-glass`

- **Auth:** require tenant-scoped authenticated user/service account and module-specific permission.
- **Request validation:** validate path IDs, tenant ownership, required body fields, idempotency key for mutating methods, and state transition rules.

- **Failure handling:** return one of `VALIDATION_ERROR, ACCESS_DENIED, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, RULE_BLOCKED, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE, DOWNSTREAM_FAILURE, STALE_DATA, DUPLICATE_EVENT` with remediation details.


### API: `GET /audit/privacy`

- **Auth:** require tenant-scoped authenticated user/service account and module-specific permission.
- **Request validation:** validate path IDs, tenant ownership, required body fields, idempotency key for mutating methods, and state transition rules.
- **Response:** return typed DTO with `id`, `status`, `links`, `source_refs`, `audit_correlation_id`, and `next_actions` where applicable.
- **Side effects:** write audit log; for mutating endpoints emit state-change event; update VisitGraph/readiness when patient or visit context changes.
- **Failure handling:** return one of `VALIDATION_ERROR, ACCESS_DENIED, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, RULE_BLOCKED, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE, DOWNSTREAM_FAILURE, STALE_DATA, DUPLICATE_EVENT` with remediation details.

### AI, rules, and automation

- Detect anomalous access patterns
- Summarize break-glass justification for review
- Recommend least-privilege role changes

**Automation boundary.** AI and rules may detect, summarize, draft, rank, or recommend. Human approval is required when the action affects diagnosis, treatment, clinical triage, medical necessity, billing/coding, payer notice, patient financial obligation, infection-control clearance, patient safety, staff discipline, or external write-back beyond approved low-risk workflows.

### UI implementation requirements

- Provide module landing page with list/board view, filters, status counts, aging/SLA indicators, and role-based next actions.
- Provide detail drawer/page for every module object with status history, source evidence, tasks, related VisitGraph facts, audit trail, and comments.
- Provide create/edit/complete/defer/escalate dialogs with required validation and accessible form design.
- Provide empty states, error states, loading skeletons, offline/degraded banners for integration outages, and keyboard-accessible controls.
- Provide contextual launch links from schedule, pre-visit board, huddle, rooming, NP cockpit, flow board, analytics, and related modules.

### Permissions and access control

- identity-access.read
- identity-access.write
- identity-access.manage
- identity-access.override
- identity-access.export

Every permission must be evaluated with tenant, site, pod, care relationship, purpose of access, sensitivity tags, consent restrictions, and module-specific policy.

### Observability

- Metrics: request count, latency, error rate, queue size, object count by status, event handler lag, duplicate event count, task aging, automation acceptance/rejection, and user override rate.
- Logs: structured, correlation-ID-linked, PHI-minimized logs for service actions and integration events.
- Traces: distributed traces for API -> service -> repository -> event publication -> workflow handling.
- Alerts: stale data, SLA breach, integration degradation, failed write-back, unexpected event volume, elevated override rate, and policy-denied spikes.

### KPIs and management dashboards

- access denials by reason
- break-glass review completion
- inactive account age
- least-privilege violations
- consent mismatch incidents

### Security, safety, and compliance controls

- Apply RBAC/ABAC and field-level filtering before data leaves the service.
- Store all changes with audit log and immutable event history.
- Require reason and approval for overrides that affect safety, billing, privacy, infection, or clinical workflow.
- Preserve source links and rule/model version for every recommendation.
- Apply tenant retention policy and data minimization.
- Provide downtime/degraded mode behavior where the module is critical to same-day operations.

### Failure modes and edge cases

- External integration unavailable: show stale data banner, use manual fallback, keep task open, and record integration outage.
- Duplicate inbound event: ignore idempotently and do not duplicate tasks/facts/candidates.
- Conflicting source data: create conflict item, downgrade confidence/readiness, assign owner, and show source comparison.
- Stale data: block high-risk decision or mark advisory only until refreshed.
- Unauthorized access: deny, audit, and display minimal safe error message.
- User override: require reason, log audit, emit override event, and route to review if high risk.

### Acceptance criteria

- A user cannot open a patient record unless access policy permits it or break-glass is invoked.
- Every break-glass session requires reason, expires automatically, and appears in compliance review queue.
- Patient-level sensitive modules can be restricted by role, care relationship, site, and active encounter status.

### Required tests

- Unit tests for validators, state transitions, rule evaluation, access policy, and idempotency.
- API tests for each endpoint, including happy path, validation failure, access denial, stale data, duplicate idempotency key, and invalid transition.
- Event tests for each consumed/published event, including replay and duplicate handling.
- UI tests for board/list, detail view, create/edit/complete/defer/escalate, permissions, and accessibility.
- Integration tests with mocked external systems when the module reads or writes external data.
- AI tests for source citation, output schema validation, human-review workflow, and blocked high-risk automation when applicable.

## M02 - Clinic Digital Twin and RTLS Fusion Engine

### Module purpose and operating role

**Mission.** Maintain a live, privacy-preserving operational model of patients, staff, rooms, zones, equipment, and movement by fusing RTLS, schedule, EHR, task, room, and sensor signals.

**Primary implementation package/service:** `digital-twin-rtls`.

**Primary functional domain:** location fusion, dwell segments, room/equipment state, live map.

**Primary personas:** Flow Captain, MA, RN, Provider, EVS, Operations Manager, Infection Preventionist.

**Why this module matters to institutional excellence.** This module converts a historically fragmented clinic function into an owned, measurable, auditable software workflow. It must improve quality, outcomes, flow, safety, patient experience, staff reliability, and appropriate compliant revenue without creating unsafe automation or administrative burden.

### Functional scope

- RTLS tag/device registry
- UWB/BLE/RFID/Wi-Fi vendor adapters
- Signal normalization and confidence scoring
- Zone and room inference
- Patient/staff/equipment live map
- Dwell-time timers
- Badge association/disassociation
- Geofence events
- Location replay for audit/infection investigation
- Privacy-preserving staff analytics
- Equipment search and utilization

### Key lifecycle states

- `signal_received`
- `location_inferred`
- `confidence_low`
- `overridden`
- `stale`

### User stories

- As a **primary user**, I can see the current state, risk level, owner, next action, and source evidence for this module without searching multiple systems.
- As a **queue owner**, I can claim, complete, defer, reassign, or escalate module work with required evidence and audit logging.
- As a **manager/flow captain**, I can identify aging work, bottlenecks, defect patterns, and patients/visits at risk.
- As a **compliance or governance user**, I can trace every recommendation, rule firing, AI output, override, and external write-back to source evidence.
- As **Codex**, I can implement this module by creating the service package, database models, API routes, event handlers, UI screens, permissions, tests, and telemetry described here.

### Feature implementation cards


#### Feature 1: RTLS tag/device registry

- **User behavior:** Users can initiate, view, update, complete, defer, or escalate this capability according to role. The UI must display current state, owner, due date, source evidence, unresolved blockers, and next best action.

### Data model and persistence details


### Object: `RtlsTag`

- **Suggested table/model:** `rtls_tag`.
- **Required fields:** `id`, `tenant_id`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `version`, `source_system`, `external_id`, `source_refs`, `sensitivity_tags`.
- **Recommended relationships:** link to `patient_id`, `visit_id`, `appointment_id`, `task_id`, `workflow_instance_id`, `rule_trace_id`, or `ai_run_id` when applicable.
- **Indexes:** `(tenant_id, status)`, `(tenant_id, updated_at)`, external reference index when integrated, and patient/visit indexes when patient-specific.
- **Audit:** create audit rows for create, update, status change, delete/archive, override, and external write-back.


### Object: `LocationObservation`

- **Suggested table/model:** `location_observation`.
- **Required fields:** `id`, `tenant_id`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `version`, `source_system`, `external_id`, `source_refs`, `sensitivity_tags`.

### API contracts


### API: `POST /rtls/observations`

- **Auth:** require tenant-scoped authenticated user/service account and module-specific permission.
- **Request validation:** validate path IDs, tenant ownership, required body fields, idempotency key for mutating methods, and state transition rules.
- **Response:** return typed DTO with `id`, `status`, `links`, `source_refs`, `audit_correlation_id`, and `next_actions` where applicable.
- **Side effects:** write audit log; for mutating endpoints emit state-change event; update VisitGraph/readiness when patient or visit context changes.
- **Failure handling:** return one of `VALIDATION_ERROR, ACCESS_DENIED, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, RULE_BLOCKED, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE, DOWNSTREAM_FAILURE, STALE_DATA, DUPLICATE_EVENT` with remediation details.

### Events and event handlers


### Event: `rtls.observation.received`

- **Trigger:** emitted when the module reaches the corresponding lifecycle milestone or when an external integration normalizes that state.
- **Payload minimum:** `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id` if applicable, `visit_id` if applicable, module object ID, previous status, new status, source refs, actor, occurred_at, and idempotency key.
- **Consumers:** Visit Readiness Graph, Workflow Engine, Analytics, Audit, and any module that depends on this state.
- **Idempotency:** event handler must ignore duplicate `event_id`/`idempotency_key` and avoid duplicate task or fact creation.

### AI, rules, and automation

- Resolve conflicting location signals
- Predict equipment demand
- Detect abnormal dwell patterns
- Recommend room reassignment to prevent bottleneck

**Automation boundary.** AI and rules may detect, summarize, draft, rank, or recommend. Human approval is required when the action affects diagnosis, treatment, clinical triage, medical necessity, billing/coding, payer notice, patient financial obligation, infection-control clearance, patient safety, staff discipline, or external write-back beyond approved low-risk workflows.

### UI implementation requirements

- Provide module landing page with list/board view, filters, status counts, aging/SLA indicators, and role-based next actions.
- Provide detail drawer/page for every module object with status history, source evidence, tasks, related VisitGraph facts, audit trail, and comments.
- Provide create/edit/complete/defer/escalate dialogs with required validation and accessible form design.
- Provide empty states, error states, loading skeletons, offline/degraded banners for integration outages, and keyboard-accessible controls.
- Provide contextual launch links from schedule, pre-visit board, huddle, rooming, NP cockpit, flow board, analytics, and related modules.

### Permissions and access control

- digital-twin-rtls.read
- digital-twin-rtls.write
- digital-twin-rtls.manage
- digital-twin-rtls.override
- digital-twin-rtls.export

Every permission must be evaluated with tenant, site, pod, care relationship, purpose of access, sensitivity tags, consent restrictions, and module-specific policy.

### Observability

- Metrics: request count, latency, error rate, queue size, object count by status, event handler lag, duplicate event count, task aging, automation acceptance/rejection, and user override rate.
- Logs: structured, correlation-ID-linked, PHI-minimized logs for service actions and integration events.
- Traces: distributed traces for API -> service -> repository -> event publication -> workflow handling.
- Alerts: stale data, SLA breach, integration degradation, failed write-back, unexpected event volume, elevated override rate, and policy-denied spikes.

### KPIs and management dashboards

- location accuracy by zone
- location confidence
- mean equipment search time
- room utilization
- unexplained dwell events
- RTLS data latency

### Security, safety, and compliance controls

- Apply RBAC/ABAC and field-level filtering before data leaves the service.
- Store all changes with audit log and immutable event history.
- Require reason and approval for overrides that affect safety, billing, privacy, infection, or clinical workflow.
- Preserve source links and rule/model version for every recommendation.
- Apply tenant retention policy and data minimization.
- Provide downtime/degraded mode behavior where the module is critical to same-day operations.

### Failure modes and edge cases

- External integration unavailable: show stale data banner, use manual fallback, keep task open, and record integration outage.
- Duplicate inbound event: ignore idempotently and do not duplicate tasks/facts/candidates.
- Conflicting source data: create conflict item, downgrade confidence/readiness, assign owner, and show source comparison.
- Stale data: block high-risk decision or mark advisory only until refreshed.
- Unauthorized access: deny, audit, and display minimal safe error message.
- User override: require reason, log audit, emit override event, and route to review if high risk.

### Acceptance criteria

- A patient entering a room updates the Visit state only when signal confidence and contextual rules meet threshold.
- Staff location is visible only under configured operational need and is audited.
- Equipment search returns last known location, confidence, timestamp, responsible area, and cleaning status.

### Required tests

- Unit tests for validators, state transitions, rule evaluation, access policy, and idempotency.
- API tests for each endpoint, including happy path, validation failure, access denial, stale data, duplicate idempotency key, and invalid transition.
- Event tests for each consumed/published event, including replay and duplicate handling.
- UI tests for board/list, detail view, create/edit/complete/defer/escalate, permissions, and accessibility.
- Integration tests with mocked external systems when the module reads or writes external data.
- AI tests for source citation, output schema validation, human-review workflow, and blocked high-risk automation when applicable.

## M03 - Visit Readiness Graph and Shared Encounter State

### Module purpose and operating role

**Mission.** Provide the canonical graph of a visit, linking patient, appointment, coverage, care gaps, tasks, rooms, records, quality, infection, RCM, AI outputs, handoff, and encounter state.

**Primary implementation package/service:** `visit-graph`.

**Primary functional domain:** Visit Readiness Graph, facts, source evidence, readiness score.

**Primary personas:** All modules, Implementation Engineers, Data Architects, Analytics Team.

**Why this module matters to institutional excellence.** This module converts a historically fragmented clinic function into an owned, measurable, auditable software workflow. It must improve quality, outcomes, flow, safety, patient experience, staff reliability, and appropriate compliant revenue without creating unsafe automation or administrative burden.

### Functional scope

- Visit graph materialized view
- Readiness score service
- Graph timeline
- Entity relationship explorer
- Source/provenance tracking
- Conflict detection
- Data freshness engine
- Cross-module dependencies
- Graph snapshot for audit and handoff

### Key lifecycle states

- `graph_created`
- `facts_pending`
- `conflict_detected`
- `readiness_recalculated`
- `handoff_ready`

### User stories

- As a **primary user**, I can see the current state, risk level, owner, next action, and source evidence for this module without searching multiple systems.
- As a **queue owner**, I can claim, complete, defer, reassign, or escalate module work with required evidence and audit logging.
- As a **manager/flow captain**, I can identify aging work, bottlenecks, defect patterns, and patients/visits at risk.
- As a **compliance or governance user**, I can trace every recommendation, rule firing, AI output, override, and external write-back to source evidence.
- As **Codex**, I can implement this module by creating the service package, database models, API routes, event handlers, UI screens, permissions, tests, and telemetry described here.

### Feature implementation cards


#### Feature 1: Visit graph materialized view

- **User behavior:** Users can initiate, view, update, complete, defer, or escalate this capability according to role. The UI must display current state, owner, due date, source evidence, unresolved blockers, and next best action.
- **System behavior:** The service evaluates relevant rules, writes a state record, emits a module event, updates the Visit Readiness Graph when patient/visit-specific, and creates downstream tasks when prerequisites are missing.
- **Data contract:** Persist a feature-specific record linked to one or more of: `Visit, VisitNode, VisitEdge, ReadinessScore, ReadinessDomainScore`. Include `tenant_id`, `status`, `source_refs`, `confidence`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `version`, and audit correlation.
- **API pattern:** Add or map this behavior to `POST /visit-graph/visit-graph-materialized-view`, `GET /visit-graph/visit-graph-materialized-view/{id}`, `PATCH /visit-graph/visit-graph-materialized-view/{id}`, and a list endpoint with filters unless an endpoint below already covers it.
- **Event pattern:** Publish `m03.visit-graph-materialized-view.created`, `m03.visit-graph-materialized-view.updated`, and `m03.visit-graph-materialized-view.completed` or map to the module events listed below.
- **Validation:** Reject missing required context, invalid state transitions, stale source data, duplicate idempotency keys, missing consent/policy, or unapproved high-risk automation.
- **Testing:** Include unit tests for validation, API tests for create/update/list, event tests for publication/idempotency, and UI tests for empty/error/loading/completed states.

### API contracts


### API: `GET /visits/{id}/graph`

- **Auth:** require tenant-scoped authenticated user/service account and module-specific permission.
- **Request validation:** validate path IDs, tenant ownership, required body fields, idempotency key for mutating methods, and state transition rules.
- **Response:** return typed DTO with `id`, `status`, `links`, `source_refs`, `audit_correlation_id`, and `next_actions` where applicable.
- **Side effects:** write audit log; for mutating endpoints emit state-change event; update VisitGraph/readiness when patient or visit context changes.
- **Failure handling:** return one of `VALIDATION_ERROR, ACCESS_DENIED, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, RULE_BLOCKED, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE, DOWNSTREAM_FAILURE, STALE_DATA, DUPLICATE_EVENT` with remediation details.

### Events and event handlers


### Event: `visit.graph.updated`

- **Trigger:** emitted when the module reaches the corresponding lifecycle milestone or when an external integration normalizes that state.
- **Payload minimum:** `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id` if applicable, `visit_id` if applicable, module object ID, previous status, new status, source refs, actor, occurred_at, and idempotency key.
- **Consumers:** Visit Readiness Graph, Workflow Engine, Analytics, Audit, and any module that depends on this state.
- **Idempotency:** event handler must ignore duplicate `event_id`/`idempotency_key` and avoid duplicate task or fact creation.

### AI, rules, and automation

- Explain readiness score
- Prioritize unresolved defects
- Summarize graph changes since last review
- Detect likely missing nodes

**Automation boundary.** AI and rules may detect, summarize, draft, rank, or recommend. Human approval is required when the action affects diagnosis, treatment, clinical triage, medical necessity, billing/coding, payer notice, patient financial obligation, infection-control clearance, patient safety, staff discipline, or external write-back beyond approved low-risk workflows.

### UI implementation requirements

- Provide module landing page with list/board view, filters, status counts, aging/SLA indicators, and role-based next actions.
- Provide detail drawer/page for every module object with status history, source evidence, tasks, related VisitGraph facts, audit trail, and comments.
- Provide create/edit/complete/defer/escalate dialogs with required validation and accessible form design.
- Provide empty states, error states, loading skeletons, offline/degraded banners for integration outages, and keyboard-accessible controls.
- Provide contextual launch links from schedule, pre-visit board, huddle, rooming, NP cockpit, flow board, analytics, and related modules.

### Permissions and access control

- visit-graph.read
- visit-graph.write
- visit-graph.manage
- visit-graph.override
- visit-graph.export

Every permission must be evaluated with tenant, site, pod, care relationship, purpose of access, sensitivity tags, consent restrictions, and module-specific policy.

### Observability

- Metrics: request count, latency, error rate, queue size, object count by status, event handler lag, duplicate event count, task aging, automation acceptance/rejection, and user override rate.
- Logs: structured, correlation-ID-linked, PHI-minimized logs for service actions and integration events.
- Traces: distributed traces for API -> service -> repository -> event publication -> workflow handling.
- Alerts: stale data, SLA breach, integration degradation, failed write-back, unexpected event volume, elevated override rate, and policy-denied spikes.

### KPIs and management dashboards

- graph freshness
- readiness score distribution
- source conflict rate
- unresolved decisions at NP entry
- graph data completeness

### Security, safety, and compliance controls

- Apply RBAC/ABAC and field-level filtering before data leaves the service.
- Store all changes with audit log and immutable event history.
- Require reason and approval for overrides that affect safety, billing, privacy, infection, or clinical workflow.
- Preserve source links and rule/model version for every recommendation.
- Apply tenant retention policy and data minimization.
- Provide downtime/degraded mode behavior where the module is critical to same-day operations.

### Failure modes and edge cases

- External integration unavailable: show stale data banner, use manual fallback, keep task open, and record integration outage.
- Duplicate inbound event: ignore idempotently and do not duplicate tasks/facts/candidates.
- Conflicting source data: create conflict item, downgrade confidence/readiness, assign owner, and show source comparison.
- Stale data: block high-risk decision or mark advisory only until refreshed.
- Unauthorized access: deny, audit, and display minimal safe error message.
- User override: require reason, log audit, emit override event, and route to review if high risk.

### Acceptance criteria

- Every readiness score has source facts and contributing rule/model explanations.
- Every module writes to shared graph through typed APIs/events, not hidden local state.
- A graph snapshot is created at huddle, rooming completion, NP handoff, checkout, and claim readiness.

### Required tests

- Unit tests for validators, state transitions, rule evaluation, access policy, and idempotency.
- API tests for each endpoint, including happy path, validation failure, access denial, stale data, duplicate idempotency key, and invalid transition.
- Event tests for each consumed/published event, including replay and duplicate handling.
- UI tests for board/list, detail view, create/edit/complete/defer/escalate, permissions, and accessibility.
- Integration tests with mocked external systems when the module reads or writes external data.
- AI tests for source citation, output schema validation, human-review workflow, and blocked high-risk automation when applicable.

## M04 - Event Fabric, Workflow Engine, Task Orchestration, and Work Queues

### Module purpose and operating role

**Mission.** Turn signals into work by managing events, durable workflows, tasks, queue routing, SLAs, escalation, ownership, and audit trails across all modules.

**Primary implementation package/service:** `workflow-tasks`.

**Primary functional domain:** durable workflows, work queues, SLAs, escalation, event replay.

**Primary personas:** All Staff, Flow Captain, Operations Manager, IT/Automation Analyst.

**Why this module matters to institutional excellence.** This module converts a historically fragmented clinic function into an owned, measurable, auditable software workflow. It must improve quality, outcomes, flow, safety, patient experience, staff reliability, and appropriate compliant revenue without creating unsafe automation or administrative burden.

### Functional scope

- Event ingestion and schema validation
- Task creation and assignment
- Queue routing by role/site/pod/SLA/severity
- Workflow timers and escalations
- Due-date and dependency management
- Bulk reassignment
- Huddle exception board
- Task comments and attachments
- Queue aging analytics
- Runbooks and downtime printouts

### Key lifecycle states

- `created`
- `queued`
- `assigned`
- `in_progress`
- `waiting`
- `completed`
- `deferred`
- `escalated`
- `overdue`

### User stories

- As a **primary user**, I can see the current state, risk level, owner, next action, and source evidence for this module without searching multiple systems.
- As a **queue owner**, I can claim, complete, defer, reassign, or escalate module work with required evidence and audit logging.
- As a **manager/flow captain**, I can identify aging work, bottlenecks, defect patterns, and patients/visits at risk.
- As a **compliance or governance user**, I can trace every recommendation, rule firing, AI output, override, and external write-back to source evidence.
- As **Codex**, I can implement this module by creating the service package, database models, API routes, event handlers, UI screens, permissions, tests, and telemetry described here.

### API contracts


### API: `POST /tasks`

- **Auth:** require tenant-scoped authenticated user/service account and module-specific permission.
- **Request validation:** validate path IDs, tenant ownership, required body fields, idempotency key for mutating methods, and state transition rules.
- **Response:** return typed DTO with `id`, `status`, `links`, `source_refs`, `audit_correlation_id`, and `next_actions` where applicable.
- **Side effects:** write audit log; for mutating endpoints emit state-change event; update VisitGraph/readiness when patient or visit context changes.
- **Failure handling:** return one of `VALIDATION_ERROR, ACCESS_DENIED, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, RULE_BLOCKED, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE, DOWNSTREAM_FAILURE, STALE_DATA, DUPLICATE_EVENT` with remediation details.

### Events and event handlers


### Event: `task.created`

- **Trigger:** emitted when the module reaches the corresponding lifecycle milestone or when an external integration normalizes that state.
- **Payload minimum:** `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id` if applicable, `visit_id` if applicable, module object ID, previous status, new status, source refs, actor, occurred_at, and idempotency key.

- **Idempotency:** event handler must ignore duplicate `event_id`/`idempotency_key` and avoid duplicate task or fact creation.

### AI, rules, and automation

- Recommend task owner
- Summarize queue overload
- Predict SLA breach
- Draft patient/staff messages for task completion

**Automation boundary.** AI and rules may detect, summarize, draft, rank, or recommend. Human approval is required when the action affects diagnosis, treatment, clinical triage, medical necessity, billing/coding, payer notice, patient financial obligation, infection-control clearance, patient safety, staff discipline, or external write-back beyond approved low-risk workflows.

### UI implementation requirements

- Provide module landing page with list/board view, filters, status counts, aging/SLA indicators, and role-based next actions.
- Provide detail drawer/page for every module object with status history, source evidence, tasks, related VisitGraph facts, audit trail, and comments.
- Provide create/edit/complete/defer/escalate dialogs with required validation and accessible form design.
- Provide empty states, error states, loading skeletons, offline/degraded banners for integration outages, and keyboard-accessible controls.
- Provide contextual launch links from schedule, pre-visit board, huddle, rooming, NP cockpit, flow board, analytics, and related modules.

### Permissions and access control

- workflow-tasks.read
- workflow-tasks.write
- workflow-tasks.manage
- workflow-tasks.override
- workflow-tasks.export

Every permission must be evaluated with tenant, site, pod, care relationship, purpose of access, sensitivity tags, consent restrictions, and module-specific policy.

### Observability

- Metrics: request count, latency, error rate, queue size, object count by status, event handler lag, duplicate event count, task aging, automation acceptance/rejection, and user override rate.
- Logs: structured, correlation-ID-linked, PHI-minimized logs for service actions and integration events.
- Traces: distributed traces for API -> service -> repository -> event publication -> workflow handling.
- Alerts: stale data, SLA breach, integration degradation, failed write-back, unexpected event volume, elevated override rate, and policy-denied spikes.

### KPIs and management dashboards

- task completion time
- SLA breach rate
- queue aging
- task reassignment count
- workload balance
- manual override rate

### Security, safety, and compliance controls

- Apply RBAC/ABAC and field-level filtering before data leaves the service.
- Store all changes with audit log and immutable event history.
- Require reason and approval for overrides that affect safety, billing, privacy, infection, or clinical workflow.
- Preserve source links and rule/model version for every recommendation.
- Apply tenant retention policy and data minimization.
- Provide downtime/degraded mode behavior where the module is critical to same-day operations.

### Failure modes and edge cases

- External integration unavailable: show stale data banner, use manual fallback, keep task open, and record integration outage.
- Duplicate inbound event: ignore idempotently and do not duplicate tasks/facts/candidates.
- Conflicting source data: create conflict item, downgrade confidence/readiness, assign owner, and show source comparison.
- Stale data: block high-risk decision or mark advisory only until refreshed.
- Unauthorized access: deny, audit, and display minimal safe error message.
- User override: require reason, log audit, emit override event, and route to review if high risk.

### Acceptance criteria

- Every task has owner role, owner user when assigned, due time, severity, source trigger, patient impact, and completion requirement.
- Workflow timers survive service restarts and can be replayed.
- Users can see why a task exists, what must be done, and what happens if it is missed.

### Required tests

- Unit tests for validators, state transitions, rule evaluation, access policy, and idempotency.
- API tests for each endpoint, including happy path, validation failure, access denial, stale data, duplicate idempotency key, and invalid transition.
- Event tests for each consumed/published event, including replay and duplicate handling.
- UI tests for board/list, detail view, create/edit/complete/defer/escalate, permissions, and accessibility.
- Integration tests with mocked external systems when the module reads or writes external data.
- AI tests for source citation, output schema validation, human-review workflow, and blocked high-risk automation when applicable.

## M05 - Panel Intelligence and Proactive Outreach Engine

### Module purpose and operating role

**Mission.** Identify patients who need care before they request it and route proactive outreach for preventive care, chronic care, transitions, behavioral health, social need, medication safety, and value-based performance.

**Primary implementation package/service:** `panel-outreach`.

**Primary functional domain:** panel registries, risk tiers, proactive outreach, campaign yield.

**Primary personas:** Population Health Analyst, Scheduler, Quality Analyst, Care Manager, CHW, Manager.

**Why this module matters to institutional excellence.** This module converts a historically fragmented clinic function into an owned, measurable, auditable software workflow. It must improve quality, outcomes, flow, safety, patient experience, staff reliability, and appropriate compliant revenue without creating unsafe automation or administrative burden.

### Functional scope

- Panel registry
- Risk tiering
- Care-gap campaigns
- TCM discharge candidate detection
- No-show/late-arrival risk
- Outreach prioritization
- Patient preference/channel optimization
- Barrier-aware scheduling
- Campaign outcomes tracking
- Panel huddle lists

### Key lifecycle states

- `opportunity_created`
- `suppressed`
- `outreach_started`
- `contacted`
- `scheduled`
- `declined`
- `closed`

### User stories

- As a **primary user**, I can see the current state, risk level, owner, next action, and source evidence for this module without searching multiple systems.
- As a **queue owner**, I can claim, complete, defer, reassign, or escalate module work with required evidence and audit logging.
- As a **manager/flow captain**, I can identify aging work, bottlenecks, defect patterns, and patients/visits at risk.
- As a **compliance or governance user**, I can trace every recommendation, rule firing, AI output, override, and external write-back to source evidence.
- As **Codex**, I can implement this module by creating the service package, database models, API routes, event handlers, UI screens, permissions, tests, and telemetry described here.

### Feature implementation cards


#### Feature 1: Panel registry

- **User behavior:** Users can initiate, view, update, complete, defer, or escalate this capability according to role. The UI must display current state, owner, due date, source evidence, unresolved blockers, and next best action.
- **System behavior:** The service evaluates relevant rules, writes a state record, emits a module event, updates the Visit Readiness Graph when patient/visit-specific, and creates downstream tasks when prerequisites are missing.
- **Data contract:** Persist a feature-specific record linked to one or more of: `PanelMember, RiskTier, OutreachCampaign, OutreachAttempt, CareGap`. Include `tenant_id`, `status`, `source_refs`, `confidence`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `version`, and audit correlation.
- **API pattern:** Add or map this behavior to `POST /panel-outreach/panel-registry`, `GET /panel-outreach/panel-registry/{id}`, `PATCH /panel-outreach/panel-registry/{id}`, and a list endpoint with filters unless an endpoint below already covers it.
- **Event pattern:** Publish `m05.panel-registry.created`, `m05.panel-registry.updated`, and `m05.panel-registry.completed` or map to the module events listed below.
- **Validation:** Reject missing required context, invalid state transitions, stale source data, duplicate idempotency keys, missing consent/policy, or unapproved high-risk automation.
- **Testing:** Include unit tests for validation, API tests for create/update/list, event tests for publication/idempotency, and UI tests for empty/error/loading/completed states.

### Data model and persistence details


### Object: `PanelMember`

- **Suggested table/model:** `panel_member`.
- **Required fields:** `id`, `tenant_id`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `version`, `source_system`, `external_id`, `source_refs`, `sensitivity_tags`.
- **Recommended relationships:** link to `patient_id`, `visit_id`, `appointment_id`, `task_id`, `workflow_instance_id`, `rule_trace_id`, or `ai_run_id` when applicable.
- **Indexes:** `(tenant_id, status)`, `(tenant_id, updated_at)`, external reference index when integrated, and patient/visit indexes when patient-specific.
- **Audit:** create audit rows for create, update, status change, delete/archive, override, and external write-back.

### API contracts


### API: `GET /panel/cohorts`

- **Auth:** require tenant-scoped authenticated user/service account and module-specific permission.
- **Request validation:** validate path IDs, tenant ownership, required body fields, idempotency key for mutating methods, and state transition rules.
- **Response:** return typed DTO with `id`, `status`, `links`, `source_refs`, `audit_correlation_id`, and `next_actions` where applicable.
- **Side effects:** write audit log; for mutating endpoints emit state-change event; update VisitGraph/readiness when patient or visit context changes.
- **Failure handling:** return one of `VALIDATION_ERROR, ACCESS_DENIED, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, RULE_BLOCKED, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED, INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE, DOWNSTREAM_FAILURE, STALE_DATA, DUPLICATE_EVENT` with remediation details.

- **Auth:** require tenant-scoped authenticated user/service account and module-specific permission.

### Events and event handlers


### Event: `panel.member_due`

- **Trigger:** emitted when the module reaches the corresponding lifecycle milestone or when an external integration normalizes that state.
- **Payload minimum:** `tenant_id`, `site_id`, `patient_id` if applicable, `visit_id` if applicable, module object ID, previous status, new status, source refs, actor, occurred_at, and idempotency key.
- **Consumers:** Visit Readiness Graph, Workflow Engine, Analytics, Audit, and any module that depends on this state.
- **Idempotency:** event handler must ignore duplicate `event_id`/`idempotency_key` and avoid duplicate task or fact creation.


### Event: `outreach.task_created`

- **Trigger:** emitted when the module reaches the corresponding lifecycle milestone or when an external integration normalizes that state.
