# AURA ClinicOS

Decision-Locked Full Functional and Technical Application Specification

Version 5.0 | May 2026 | Codex-ready build blueprint for a world-class primary care reference implementation and enterprise multispecialty target architecture.

This document is written so that an engineering team or AI coding agent can convert the specification into product modules, services, data models, APIs, event handlers, user interfaces, workflow engines, AI agent controls, security policies, tests, and deployment artifacts.

Important compliance note: this is a product specification, not legal, clinical, coding, billing, regulatory, or security advice. Every clinical, billing, payer, infection-control, AI, and patient-financial workflow must be reviewed by qualified clinical leadership, compliance, legal counsel, revenue-cycle leadership, privacy/security leadership, and infection-prevention leadership before production use.

---

# 0. Decision-Locked Build Assumptions

The following assumptions are locked into v5 based on owner decisions and should be treated by Codex as default build constraints unless a future configuration profile overrides them.

| Decision area | Locked v5 assumption |
| --- | --- |
| Commercial product name | AURA ClinicOS, with modules AURA Flow, AURA PreVisit, AURA RevCycle, AURA QualityGuard, AURA InfectionShield, AURA CareOps, AURA Copilot, and AURA Command Center. |
| Initial ideal customer | NP-led or NP-heavy primary care groups operating in Medicare Advantage/value-based care, with high AWV, TCM, CCM/APCM, quality-gap, risk-adjustment, and revenue-cycle upside. Physician-owned primary care groups and other primary care clinic structures remain supported target customers. |
| Product scope | Enterprise multispecialty core architecture with primary care as the fully specified reference implementation. |
| Reference clinic operating model | NP-owned and NP-led clinic; supervising/collaborating physician reviews charts for three non-autonomous NPs; owner NP is autonomous; medical director handles clinical governance beyond chart review; typical site has four NPs and one MA per NP; most visits are 30 minutes; NPs see all visit types. |
| Payer optimization | Primary commercial optimization for Medicare Advantage/value-based primary care, preserving configurable payer logic for Medicare FFS, commercial, Medicaid, FQHC/RHC, and cash-pay variants. |
| Revenue posture | Maximize appropriate compliant revenue by eliminating preventable denials, missed legitimate services, documentation gaps, and quality/risk-capture defects. Do not use coercive collections, duplicate billing, upcoding, or unnecessary care. |
| Automation posture | v1 is Level 3/4 automation: task routing, drafting, decision support, low-risk controlled actions, and human-in-loop review. Level 5 governed enterprise autopilot is documented as future-state only. |
| RTLS assumption | Hybrid BLE/UWB by default: UWB for room/procedure precision; BLE for broad outpatient movement and asset tracking; vendor-neutral adapters; privacy-preserving staff analytics. |
| EHR/PM integration | Vendor-neutral FHIR/HL7 architecture with concrete tracks for Epic and athenahealth/eClinicalWorks. |
| Writeback philosophy | Automatically write back tasks, statuses, structured intake, forms, handoff summaries, patient messages, and staff-verified pre-visit data. Create charge candidates, diagnosis evidence, and order suggestions, but require human approval. Never autonomously finalize diagnoses, codes, medical necessity, charges, or clinical orders. |
| AI/logic architecture | Rules engine, predictive ML, LLM/RAG, optimization models, knowledge graph, simulation engine, and human-in-loop review. Vendor/model agnostic but technically specific. |
| Patient engagement | SMS/web-first patient engagement with optional portal integration. |
| Role model | Design all roles separately, then allow role bundling for smaller clinics. |
| Readiness scoring | Dynamic visit-type weighting with full drilldown into each component score, evidence source, owner, timestamp, and unresolved blocker. |
| Stop logic | Configurable hard/soft stop logic by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, compliance risk, infection-control status, and clinical-safety risk. |
| Quality focus | Primary care v1 prioritizes HEDIS/STARS, MIPS/MVP, and internal outcomes. |
| Infection-control scope | Enterprise architecture includes room, equipment, PPE, isolation routing, exposure reconstruction, and hand-hygiene/environmental monitoring. v1 prioritizes room/equipment cleaning, respiratory screening, direct-rooming, PPE prompts, and infection-control-ready room status. |
| Initial service library | Fully specify AWV, TCM, RPM, injections, spirometry, procedure visits, CCM/APCM, preventive + E/M, vaccines, ECG, labs, telehealth, and chronic-disease follow-up. |
| Delivery model | Full enterprise product built module by module so it becomes functional early and adds sophistication progressively. |
| UI depth | Wireframe-level screen definitions and component-by-component behavior are required. |
| Stack | Recommended Azure-first cloud stack: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server or Azure SQL where required; Microsoft Entra ID; AKS; Azure API Management; Azure Event Hubs/Service Bus; Azure Cache for Redis; Azure AI Search/vector search; Azure Data Lake/Fabric/Synapse; Application Insights; optional Azure Health Data Services FHIR service. Vendor-neutral alternatives are documented. |
| Architecture | Hybrid microservices with a strong lean toward full microservices, event-driven workflow orchestration, and extractable service boundaries. |
| Schemas | Add logical and physical schemas for all core modules, FHIR mappings, and event payloads. |
| Testing | Every module requires unit, integration, UI, security, workflow, AI safety, RCM compliance, infection-control, FHIR/API contract, RTLS simulation, load, downtime, and audit-log tests. |
| Deployment | SaaS platform with optional on-prem/edge gateway for RTLS and integration, plus SMART-on-FHIR embedded launch. |

# 1. Product North Star

AURA ClinicOS is an AI-native outpatient operating system designed to turn a clinic into a world-class institution: higher quality, stronger outcomes, cleaner revenue, better access, safer infection-control operations, more reliable staff execution, and less NP cognitive waste.

The primary care reference implementation is built around a high-performing NP-led site where the NP enters the encounter only after the patient is financially cleared, clinically prepared, risk-stratified, quality-gap mapped, infection-control safe, and ready for decisions. The attached Pre-Visit Operating System is treated as a controlling operational source for this model.

The application should not behave like a passive EHR dashboard. It should operate as an event-driven command system that senses state, calculates readiness, creates work, routes ownership, escalates blockers, drafts safe support content, simulates the day, and learns from every defect.

- World-class quality: every visit becomes a gap-closure and outcomes-improvement event.
- World-class revenue: appropriate, compliant services are identified, prepared, documented, and claim-ready before avoidable denial risk is created.
- World-class flow: rooms, staff, equipment, patient movement, and NP sequence are optimized without compromising safety or compliance.
- World-class readiness: each appointment has a dynamic readiness score with drilldown, evidence, blockers, owners, and next actions.
- World-class governance: AI, rules, payer logic, infection control, privacy, scope, chart review, and billing workflows are auditable and human accountable.

# 2. Commercial Application Stack

AURA ClinicOS is organized as a commercial, modular, API-first, event-driven SaaS platform with strong microservice boundaries. v1 may share infrastructure and repositories, but every module must be code-structured so it can later be independently deployed, scaled, tested, and governed.

| Layer | Recommended Azure-first build | Vendor-neutral alternative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Frontend | Next.js + React + TypeScript, hosted through Azure Static Web Apps or App Service, with SMART-on-FHIR launch support | React/Angular/Vue on any cloud frontend platform |
| Backend services | FastAPI or NestJS microservices on AKS, with Azure API Management as API gateway | Spring Boot, Go, .NET, or Node microservices on Kubernetes |
| Identity | Microsoft Entra ID, OIDC/SAML, SCIM provisioning, conditional access, step-up auth | Okta, Auth0, Ping, Keycloak, other OIDC/SAML IdP |
| Relational database | Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server; Azure SQL where Microsoft SQL is required | PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL with compatible schema strategy |
| Event bus | Azure Event Hubs for streaming, Azure Service Bus for commands/queues | Kafka/Redpanda, NATS, RabbitMQ |
| Workflow orchestration | Temporal deployed on AKS; Durable Functions acceptable for selected workflows | Camunda, Zeebe, AWS Step Functions, custom orchestrator |
| Cache/session | Azure Cache for Redis | Redis-compatible cache |
| Search/vector/RAG | Azure AI Search with vector indexes; optional pgvector for smaller deployments | OpenSearch, Elasticsearch, Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector |
| FHIR/data interoperability | Azure Health Data Services FHIR where appropriate; FHIR facade and canonical mapping layer | HAPI FHIR, Smile CDR, Firely, EHR-native FHIR only |
| Analytics | Azure Data Lake + Fabric/Synapse + Power BI; operational analytics in ClickHouse-compatible or PostgreSQL read models | Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Looker, Tableau |
| Observability | Application Insights, Azure Monitor, OpenTelemetry, Log Analytics, SIEM integration | Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, Splunk |
| Edge/RTLS gateway | Containerized gateway on site or in private network; device adapters publish canonical RTLS events | Vendor appliance, MQTT gateway, on-prem Kubernetes, secure tunnel |
| Secrets/keys | Azure Key Vault, managed identities, customer-managed keys where required | Vault, AWS KMS/Secrets Manager, GCP KMS |

# 3. Automation Levels

Automation must be explicit, configurable, and auditable. v1 is built for Level 3/4 automation while preserving Level 5 as a controlled enterprise future state.

| Level | Allowed behavior | Examples | Approval |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Visibility | Show state and analytics | Readiness score, room state, quality gaps, denial risk | No approval |
| 2 Task routing | Create/assign/escalate tasks | Missing record task, auth task, HRA reminder | Configurable auto-routing |
| 3 Drafting | Draft but do not send/finalize | NP handoff, patient message, auth packet, payer summary | Human review before clinical/financial use |
| 4 Controlled action | Perform low-risk actions within policy | Send routine SMS reminder, mark task complete from verified event, update operational status | Policy-gated; audit required |
| 5 Governed autopilot | Re-sequence rooms/staff/appointments or execute complex actions | Dynamic rooming autopilot, staffing redeployments, pre-approved schedule changes | Future-state; governance, simulation, override, and rollback required |

# 4. Reference Primary Care Operating Model

The primary care reference implementation is an NP-led, value-based primary care clinic. This reference model is concrete enough for implementation, while configuration profiles allow physician-owned primary care, health-system primary care, FQHC/RHC, and multispecialty extensions.

| Operating element | Reference implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Site staffing | Four NPs per site; one MA assigned per NP; centralized/shared roles for RN care management, eligibility, authorization, financial counseling, quality, pharmacy, CHW/social work, revenue integrity, IT/automation, compliance, and flow captain. |
| Governance | Owner NP is autonomous. Three NPs require collaborating physician chart review. Medical director owns clinical protocol governance, quality, escalation, and scope policy. Collaborating physician performs chart reviews only unless configured otherwise. |
| Visits | Mostly 30-minute visits. NPs see new patients, established follow-up, urgent/same-day, AWV/IPPE, preventive, chronic disease, TCM, procedures, injections, vaccines, ECG/labs/spirometry, telehealth, RPM setup/follow-up, and care-management enrollment visits. |
| Pod model | Each NP/MA pair is a pod unit; shared resources float according to readiness, risk, queue aging, payer deadlines, infection-control state, and day-of-flow risk. |
| Morning huddle | Flow captain leads a brief exception-based huddle using next-day readiness lock and same-day RTLS/flow constraints. |
| NP handoff | Source-linked, staff-verified, decision-focused packet with patient agenda, safety flags, clinical data, quality gaps, revenue caveats, infection status, tasks completed, and NP decisions needed. |
| Chart review | Chart review routing must distinguish autonomous owner NP, supervised NP, collaborating physician reviewer, medical director oversight, and compliance/audit review. |

# 6. Shared Domain Model

The shared domain model must be implemented before feature-specific modules. Modules may own their tables, but they must publish canonical events and use shared IDs for tenant, site, pod, patient, appointment, encounter, task, user, role, rule, evidence, and audit records.

| Entity | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Tenant | Multi-tenant legal/customer entity; owns configuration, users, feature flags, and data retention policy. |
| Site | Physical or virtual clinic location; includes address, timezone, hours, room inventory, service lines, and integration endpoints. |
| ClinicPod | Operational NP/MA pod with assigned rooms, schedule template, service line, role bundle, and escalation rules. |
| User | Human or service account; authenticated through Entra/OIDC; bound to roles, scopes, and audit identity. |
| Patient | Internal patient identity linked to EHR patient IDs, payer IDs, communication preferences, consents, and privacy rules. |
| Appointment | Scheduled care activity, usually mapped to FHIR Appointment. |
| Encounter | Actual care activity, usually mapped to FHIR Encounter. |
| VisitGraph | Graph object linking appointment, encounter, patient state, readiness, tasks, evidence, payer, quality, room, staff, and NP decision items. |
| Task | Named unit of work with owner, SLA, queue, dependencies, evidence, status, and escalation. |
| EvidenceNode | Source-linked data point used by readiness, quality, AI, RCM, chart review, and governance workflows. |
| Rule | Versioned decision logic for payer, quality, standing orders, stop logic, infection control, scoring, workflow, and UI behavior. |
| EventEnvelope | Canonical event wrapper containing tenant, source, correlation, causation, privacy classification, payload, version, and audit metadata. |
| AuditLog | Immutable log of access, actions, writes, rule changes, AI outputs, approvals, and break-glass events. |

# 7. FHIR, HL7, X12, and Integration Mapping

AURA ClinicOS uses a canonical internal model but maps to external standards. Codex should implement mapping adapters rather than hard-coding a single EHR vendor model.

| AURA object | FHIR/HL7/X12 mapping | Writeback posture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patient | FHIR Patient; HL7 ADT PID | Read/write demographics only where configured and staff verified |
| Appointment | FHIR Appointment; HL7 SIU where available | Read/write scheduling statuses and AURA operational statuses where EHR supports it |
| Encounter | FHIR Encounter; HL7 ADT/PV1 | Read actual encounter; write operational handoff/status summaries only when approved |
| Location/Room | FHIR Location; RTLS canonical Zone/Room | Write operational room status to AURA; EHR writeback optional |
| Task | FHIR Task where supported; EHR work queues otherwise | Write tasks and statuses when configured |
| Observation/Vitals | FHIR Observation | Write staff-verified structured intake and vitals where allowed |
| Document/Record | FHIR DocumentReference; C-CDA; HIE payload | Read and summarize; write source-linked handoff only after staff verification |
| Coverage/Eligibility | FHIR Coverage, CoverageEligibilityRequest/Response; X12 270/271 | Read payer response; write AURA eligibility status/task not payer adjudication |
| Prior Authorization | FHIR Da Vinci PAS/CRD/DTR where available; payer portal/fax fallback | Submit/support where permitted; maintain status and evidence |
| Claim/Charge Candidate | FHIR Claim/ClaimResponse conceptually; PM/clearinghouse export | Create candidates/reviews; never auto-finalize charges |
| Communication | FHIR Communication/CommunicationRequest; SMS/web/portal | Send routine patient messages under policy; log delivery and responses |

## M00 - AURA Admin Studio: Platform Shell, Tenant Administration, and Configuration Studio

**Stage:** Foundation/MVP

**Mission:** Provide the multi-tenant application shell, tenant configuration, sites/clinics/pods, feature flags, rule packs, branding, localization, and admin controls that make AURA configurable without code changes.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Configure the reference primary-care site as a four-NP pod structure with one MA per NP, one autonomous owner NP, three supervised NPs requiring collaborating-physician chart review, one medical director, bundled small-clinic roles, and Medicare Advantage/value-based rule packs enabled by default.

### Functional responsibilities

- Tenant onboarding wizard
- Clinic/site/pod/team hierarchy
- Role and feature-flag configuration
- Rule-pack versioning
- Template builder for handoffs, forms, tasks, messages, and dashboards
- Environment and integration status dashboard
- Configuration audit and rollback
- Payer/quality/infection rule governance calendar
- Tenant onboarding must ask for clinic ownership model, NP autonomy status, supervising physician coverage, site hours, primary-care service list, payer mix, MA ratios, pod assignment, chart-review rules, and go-live scope. The system then seeds queues, role bundles, rule packs, score weights, and dashboards.

### AI, rules, and automation boundaries

- AI may suggest configuration defaults from clinic profile when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may detect inconsistent rule settings when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may draft implementation checklist when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may summarize configuration drift when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- Module-specific AI/rules behavior: Suggest initial clinic configuration from specialty, payer mix, staffing, operating hours, and visit types.; Detect conflicting rules, unreachable queue states, missing owner assignments, and inconsistent SLA calendars.; Draft implementation checklists and training plans based on enabled modules.
- The module must not independently diagnose, bill, code, determine medical necessity, deny care, override infection-control policy, or finalize high-impact patient-financial conclusions.

### Business rules and validation gates

- No production rule can activate without owner, source, review date, rollback plan, and affected-module list.
- Feature flags must be scoped by tenant, site, role, and environment.
- Configuration changes affecting billing, clinical protocol, infection control, or privacy require dual approval.
- Apply dynamic stop logic by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, compliance risk, infection-control state, and clinical-safety risk.
- Every command validates tenant scope, role permission, data confidence, source freshness, required approvals, and downstream writeback eligibility.

### Security, privacy, and compliance controls

- Enforce Entra/OIDC identity, tenant isolation, RBAC/ABAC, least privilege, break-glass logging, and step-up authentication for high-risk actions.
- Classify every record and event as operational, PHI, financial, security, or AI-governance evidence; apply retention and audit policy accordingly.
- Encrypt data in transit and at rest; use Azure Key Vault/managed identity; prohibit secrets in code or logs.
- Log all PHI reads, EHR writebacks, AI outputs, patient messages, rule changes, chart-review actions, and approvals.
- Use privacy-preserving staff-location analytics; individual staff location is restricted to operationally necessary roles and audited.

### Observability and KPIs

- configuration change lead time
- rollback count
- unreviewed rules
- integration uptime
- tenant onboarding time
- Module health: queue age, event lag, failed jobs, API latency, rule errors, AI draft rejection rate, writeback failure rate, and audit exceptions.

### Acceptance criteria

1. Tenant admin can configure clinic pods, roles, queues, and SLAs without developer intervention.
2. Every configuration change creates a versioned audit record with editor, reason, timestamp, diff, and rollback option.
3. Published rule packs can be tested in sandbox before production activation.
4. Admin can configure a new tenant end-to-end without code changes.
5. A published rule pack can be rolled back and all dependent queues recalculate.
6. Audit log captures before/after diff, user, timestamp, reason, and affected entities.

### Codex build checklist

- Create `aura_admin_studio` service, repository, policy, event handlers, tests, and UI route.
- Implement non-AI rules and deterministic workflows before adding LLM/RAG or predictive automation.
- Create migrations for listed objects and link them to shared tenant/patient/appointment/task/audit IDs.
- Create OpenAPI schemas and DTOs for commands, queries, events, and read-model responses.
- Create UI components with loading, empty, error, permission-denied, draft-review, source-link, and audit-history states.
- Create unit, integration, E2E, security, PHI audit, workflow, API contract, and failure-mode tests.


## M01 - AURA Trust: Identity, Access, RBAC/ABAC, Consent, and Privacy Enforcement

**Stage:** Foundation/MVP

**Mission:** Protect ePHI and operational data through SSO, MFA, role-based and attribute-based access, minimum-necessary enforcement, break-glass access, consent-aware visibility, and full auditability.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Enforce Entra-backed identity, role separation, chart-review privileges for the collaborating physician, medical director governance rights, NP owner override rights, and least-privilege access to PHI, revenue, RTLS, and AI governance artifacts.

### Functional responsibilities

- OIDC/SAML SSO
- MFA policy
- RBAC role matrix
- ABAC based on clinic, pod, patient relationship, data sensitivity, location, and emergency state
- Break-glass workflow
- Consent and ROI enforcement
- Caregiver/guardian access tracking
- PHI view audit logs
- Staff-location privacy policy controls
- Session timeout and device trust
- A user signs in through Entra ID/OIDC, receives tenant/site/pod scoped claims, and can only see workflows matching their role bundle. High-risk actions require step-up authentication, dual approval, or named attestation depending on policy.

### Primary users and role behavior

- **All Staff:** uses AURA Trust to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Compliance Lead:** uses AURA Trust to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Privacy Officer:** uses AURA Trust to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Security Admin:** uses AURA Trust to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Auditor:** uses AURA Trust to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.

### Security, privacy, and compliance controls

- Enforce Entra/OIDC identity, tenant isolation, RBAC/ABAC, least privilege, break-glass logging, and step-up authentication for high-risk actions.
- Classify every record and event as operational, PHI, financial, security, or AI-governance evidence; apply retention and audit policy accordingly.
- Encrypt data in transit and at rest; use Azure Key Vault/managed identity; prohibit secrets in code or logs.
- Log all PHI reads, EHR writebacks, AI outputs, patient messages, rule changes, chart-review actions, and approvals.
- Use privacy-preserving staff-location analytics; individual staff location is restricted to operationally necessary roles and audited.

### Observability and KPIs

- access denials by reason
- break-glass review completion
- inactive account age
- least-privilege violations
- consent mismatch incidents
- Module health: queue age, event lag, failed jobs, API latency, rule errors, AI draft rejection rate, writeback failure rate, and audit exceptions.

### Acceptance criteria

1. A user cannot open a patient record unless access policy permits it or break-glass is invoked.
2. Every break-glass session requires reason, expires automatically, and appears in compliance review queue.
3. Patient-level sensitive modules can be restricted by role, care relationship, site, and active encounter status.
4. MA cannot see financial-assistance details unless assigned to relevant task.
5. Compliance officer can replay access history for one patient encounter.
6. Break-glass access expires automatically and is flagged for review.

## M02 - AURA Flow RTLS: Clinic Digital Twin and RTLS Fusion Engine

**Stage:** MVP lite, enterprise full

**Mission:** Maintain a live, privacy-preserving operational model of patients, staff, rooms, zones, equipment, and movement by fusing RTLS, schedule, EHR, task, room, and sensor signals.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Use hybrid BLE/UWB as the default RTLS assumption: UWB for room/procedure precision and BLE for broader patient/staff/equipment movement, with vendor-neutral adapters and privacy-preserving staff analytics.

### Functional responsibilities

- RTLS tag/device registry
- UWB/BLE/RFID/Wi-Fi vendor adapters
- Signal normalization and confidence scoring
- Zone and room inference
- Patient/staff/equipment live map
- Dwell-time timers
- Badge association/disassociation
- Geofence events
- Location replay for audit/infection investigation
- Privacy-preserving staff analytics
- Equipment search and utilization
- Location pings are fused into visit states, room occupancy, staff proximity events, equipment availability, infection-control room readiness, and waiting-time clocks. Confidence and stale-signal handling are explicit.

### Primary users and role behavior

- **Flow Captain:** uses AURA Flow RTLS to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **MA:** uses AURA Flow RTLS to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.

### Primary workflows

1. RTLS adapters ingest UWB, BLE, Wi-Fi, RFID, NFC, device, and occupancy signals, normalize them, and calculate patient/staff/equipment presence by zone.
2. Location inference resolves noisy pings into stable states such as waiting room, exam room, lab, checkout, infusion chair, procedure room, hallway, or offsite.
3. Room state combines occupancy, schedule assignment, infection-control status, cleaning status, equipment readiness, maintenance blocks, and expected need.
4. Digital twin exposes real-time spatial state to flow optimization, infection control, charge-capture signals, huddle dashboards, and patient wayfinding.
5. Location pings are fused into visit states, room occupancy, staff proximity events, equipment availability, infection-control room readiness, and waiting-time clocks. Confidence and stale-signal handling are explicit.

### Business rules and validation gates

- Apply dynamic stop logic by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, compliance risk, infection-control state, and clinical-safety risk.
- Every command validates tenant scope, role permission, data confidence, source freshness, required approvals, and downstream writeback eligibility.

### Security, privacy, and compliance controls

- Enforce Entra/OIDC identity, tenant isolation, RBAC/ABAC, least privilege, break-glass logging, and step-up authentication for high-risk actions.
- Classify every record and event as operational, PHI, financial, security, or AI-governance evidence; apply retention and audit policy accordingly.
- Encrypt data in transit and at rest; use Azure Key Vault/managed identity; prohibit secrets in code or logs.
- Log all PHI reads, EHR writebacks, AI outputs, patient messages, rule changes, chart-review actions, and approvals.
- Use privacy-preserving staff-location analytics; individual staff location is restricted to operationally necessary roles and audited.

### Observability and KPIs

- location accuracy by zone
- location confidence
- mean equipment search time
- room utilization
- unexplained dwell events
- RTLS data latency
- Module health: queue age, event lag, failed jobs, API latency, rule errors, AI draft rejection rate, writeback failure rate, and audit exceptions.

### Acceptance criteria

1. A patient entering a room updates the Visit state only when signal confidence and contextual rules meet threshold.
2. Staff location is visible only under configured operational need and is audited.
3. Equipment search returns last known location, confidence, timestamp, responsible area, and cleaning status.
4. Patient entering room changes visit state only after dwell-time and confidence thresholds.
5. Dirty room is not offered by optimizer even if vacant.
6. RTLS outage falls back to manual room status with visible degraded-mode banner.

## M03 - AURA Visit Graph: Visit Readiness Graph and Shared Encounter State

**Stage:** Foundation/MVP

**Mission:** Provide the canonical graph of a visit, linking patient, appointment, coverage, care gaps, tasks, rooms, records, quality, infection, RCM, AI outputs, handoff, and encounter state.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Create the dissectible Visit Readiness Graph with dynamic visit-type weighting. Primary care defaults weight AWV, TCM, chronic follow-up, urgent, procedure, telehealth, RPM, and care-management visits differently.

### Functional responsibilities

- Visit graph materialized view
- Readiness score service
- Graph timeline
- Entity relationship explorer
- Source/provenance tracking
- Conflict detection
- Data freshness engine
- Cross-module dependencies
- Graph snapshot for audit and handoff
- Every appointment produces a graph connecting patient, payer, NP, MA, room, readiness domains, quality gaps, RCM status, infection readiness, tasks, and NP decision items. Users can click each score to see evidence, owner, timestamp, source, and next action.

### Primary users and role behavior

- **All modules:** uses AURA Visit Graph to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Implementation Engineers:** uses AURA Visit Graph to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.

### Primary workflows

1. When an appointment is created, the system initializes a VisitGraph node with readiness domains, required tasks, rule evaluations, known risks, and module dependencies.
2. Every task completion, eligibility response, chart-scrub finding, RTLS transition, quality gap, patient message, or rooming update recalculates readiness.
3. Graph edges connect patient, appointment, encounter, payer, provider, room, tasks, authorizations, gaps, records, medications, devices, and infection-control constraints.
4. Readiness lock snapshots the graph 24 hours before and again at huddle, check-in, rooming, NP entry, checkout, and claim readiness.
5. Every appointment produces a graph connecting patient, payer, NP, MA, room, readiness domains, quality gaps, RCM status, infection readiness, tasks, and NP decision items. Users can click each score to see evidence, owner, timestamp, source, and next action.

## M04 - AURA WorkOS: Event Fabric, Workflow Engine, Task Orchestration, and Work Queues

**Stage:** Foundation/MVP

**Mission:** Turn signals into work by managing events, durable workflows, tasks, queue routing, SLAs, escalation, ownership, and audit trails across all modules.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Operate the clinic through work queues rather than inbox chaos. Every task must have owner, SLA, escalation path, patient impact, revenue impact, quality impact, safety impact, AI confidence, and audit trail.

### Functional responsibilities

- Event ingestion and schema validation
- Task creation and assignment
- Queue routing by role/site/pod/SLA/severity
- Workflow timers and escalations
- Due-date and dependency management
- Bulk reassignment
- Huddle exception board
- Task comments and attachments
- Queue aging analytics
- Runbooks and downtime printouts
- Events trigger workflow definitions in Temporal-like orchestration. Work is routed by role, pod, urgency, service line, payer, and skill. Overdue or blocked tasks escalate to flow captain, manager, medical director, or compliance lead.

### AI, rules, and automation boundaries

- AI may recommend task owner when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may summarize queue overload when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may predict sla breach when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may draft patient/staff messages for task completion when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- Module-specific AI/rules behavior: Cluster related tasks into a single exception packet.; Draft task instructions from rule context and source evidence.; Predict tasks at risk of missing SLA and suggest reassignment.
- The module must not independently diagnose, bill, code, determine medical necessity, deny care, override infection-control policy, or finalize high-impact patient-financial conclusions.

### Business rules and validation gates

- No queue may exist without owner role, SLA, backup role, and escalation path.
- Clinical, infection-control, privacy, billing, and patient-facing tasks require separate approval classes.
- Expired tasks must remain visible until resolved, canceled with reason, or explicitly deferred.
- Apply dynamic stop logic by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, compliance risk, infection-control state, and clinical-safety risk.
- Every command validates tenant scope, role permission, data confidence, source freshness, required approvals, and downstream writeback eligibility.

### Security, privacy, and compliance controls

- Enforce Entra/OIDC identity, tenant isolation, RBAC/ABAC, least privilege, break-glass logging, and step-up authentication for high-risk actions.
- Classify every record and event as operational, PHI, financial, security, or AI-governance evidence; apply retention and audit policy accordingly.
- Encrypt data in transit and at rest; use Azure Key Vault/managed identity; prohibit secrets in code or logs.
- Log all PHI reads, EHR writebacks, AI outputs, patient messages, rule changes, chart-review actions, and approvals.
- Use privacy-preserving staff-location analytics; individual staff location is restricted to operationally necessary roles and audited.

### Observability and KPIs

- task completion time
- SLA breach rate
- queue aging
- task reassignment count
- workload balance
- manual override rate
- Module health: queue age, event lag, failed jobs, API latency, rule errors, AI draft rejection rate, writeback failure rate, and audit exceptions.

### Acceptance criteria

1. Every task has owner role, owner user when assigned, due time, severity, source trigger, patient impact, and completion requirement.
2. Workflow timers survive service restarts and can be replayed.
3. Users can see why a task exists, what must be done, and what happens if it is missed.
4. Eligibility failure creates financial-clearance task with correct owner and SLA.
5. Overdue auth task escalates before visit lock.
6. Dead-lettered events are visible and replayable after correction.

- Create unit, integration, E2E, security, PHI audit, workflow, API contract, and failure-mode tests.


## M05 - AURA Panel Pathfinder: Panel Intelligence and Proactive Outreach Engine

**Stage:** MVP for MA/value-based primary care

**Mission:** Identify patients who need care before they request it and route proactive outreach for preventive care, chronic care, transitions, behavioral health, social need, medication safety, and value-based performance.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Drive MA/value-based panel management: AWV due, TCM candidates, HEDIS/STARS gaps, chronic disease gaps, med adherence, risk-adjustment review opportunities, no-show risk, ED/hospital follow-up, and care-management eligibility.

### Functional responsibilities

- Panel registry
- Risk tiering
- Care-gap campaigns
- TCM discharge candidate detection
- No-show/late-arrival risk
- Outreach prioritization
- Patient preference/channel optimization
- Barrier-aware scheduling
- Campaign outcomes tracking
- Panel huddle lists
- The panel engine refreshes daily, ranks patients by clinical risk, quality upside, value-based contract impact, revenue opportunity, outreach feasibility, and equity barriers, then creates campaigns and scheduling recommendations.

### Primary users and role behavior

- **Population Health Analyst:** uses AURA Panel Pathfinder to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.

### Primary workflows

1. Panel scans identify overdue care, recent discharges, rising-risk patients, missed follow-ups, medication nonadherence, high ED use, uncontrolled chronic disease, and care-management candidates.
2. Outreach campaigns prioritize patients by clinical risk, quality impact, access urgency, patient preference, equity barriers, and capacity availability.
3. Campaign outcomes update the Visit Readiness Graph and Scheduling module: reached, declined, scheduled, barrier found, care-management referred, or unable to contact.
4. Population health staff tune registries, value sets, measure mappings, outreach scripts, and exclusion logic.
5. The panel engine refreshes daily, ranks patients by clinical risk, quality upside, value-based contract impact, revenue opportunity, outreach feasibility, and equity barriers, then creates campaigns and scheduling recommendations.

## M06 - AURA Access: Scheduling, Access, Visit-Type Optimization, and Capacity Design

**Stage:** MVP

**Mission:** Classify visit requests into correct visit type, modality, acuity, slot length, continuity path, service opportunity, and payer-aware scheduling route.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Primary-care reference scheduling assumes four NPs/site, one MA per NP, mostly 30-minute visits, NPs see all visit families, and complex visits should receive readiness-driven prework rather than default overbooking.

### Functional responsibilities

- Visit-type decision tree
- Slot-length recommendation
- Modality suitability check
- TCM/AWV/care-management opportunity flags
- Interpreter and accommodation booking
- Continuity routing
- Same-day conversion logic
- Waitlist and cancellation fill
- Late-arrival risk
- Capacity simulation
- Requests are classified into visit families, slot lengths, modality, continuity preference, payer constraints, and service opportunities. The scheduler sees recommended slot, prep work, patient script, and escalation if wrong visit type is suspected.

### Primary users and role behavior

- **Scheduler:** uses AURA Access to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Access Center:** uses AURA Access to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Flow Captain:** uses AURA Access to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **NP:** uses AURA Access to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Manager:** uses AURA Access to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.

### Primary workflows

1. Scheduler captures request source, patient-stated agenda, acuity clues, modality preference, continuity preference, language/access needs, payer, and service family.
2. Visit-Type Agent recommends new/established, AWV, TCM, chronic follow-up, urgent, behavioral health, procedure, lab-only, nurse/MA protocol, care-management enrollment, RPM setup, or telehealth.
3. Capacity engine uses slot templates, staff availability, room needs, visit duration prediction, payer constraints, equipment needs, and care-team continuity to book the optimal slot.
4. Scheduling outcome initializes pre-visit workflows, clearance tasks, patient forms, records requests, and huddle risk flags.
5. Requests are classified into visit families, slot lengths, modality, continuity preference, payer constraints, and service opportunities. The scheduler sees recommended slot, prep work, patient script, and escalation if wrong visit type is suspected.

### AI, rules, and automation boundaries

- AI may classify visit request when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may recommend slot length when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may suggest combining services when clinically appropriate when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may forecast schedule bottleneck before booking when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- Module-specific AI/rules behavior: Predict visit duration and complexity from agenda, history, quality gaps, and patient barriers.; Recommend slot length and modality while flagging services that need human approval.; Identify same-day combinations that may be clinically appropriate without making billing decisions.
- The module must not independently diagnose, bill, code, determine medical necessity, deny care, override infection-control policy, or finalize high-impact patient-financial conclusions.

### Business rules and validation gates

- Urgent symptoms must route to RN/NP triage protocol rather than routine scheduling.
- TCM and AWV eligibility flags are advisory until verified.
- Telehealth requires location, technology readiness, payer policy, and emergency backup workflow.
- Apply dynamic stop logic by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, compliance risk, infection-control state, and clinical-safety risk.
- Every command validates tenant scope, role permission, data confidence, source freshness, required approvals, and downstream writeback eligibility.

### Security, privacy, and compliance controls

- Enforce Entra/OIDC identity, tenant isolation, RBAC/ABAC, least privilege, break-glass logging, and step-up authentication for high-risk actions.
- Classify every record and event as operational, PHI, financial, security, or AI-governance evidence; apply retention and audit policy accordingly.
- Encrypt data in transit and at rest; use Azure Key Vault/managed identity; prohibit secrets in code or logs.
- Log all PHI reads, EHR writebacks, AI outputs, patient messages, rule changes, chart-review actions, and approvals.
- Use privacy-preserving staff-location analytics; individual staff location is restricted to operationally necessary roles and audited.

### Observability and KPIs

- third next available
- wrong visit type rate
- slot overrun rate
- TCM window compliance
- AWV capture opportunity
- late cancellation fill rate
- Module health: queue age, event lag, failed jobs, API latency, rule errors, AI draft rejection rate, writeback failure rate, and audit exceptions.

### Acceptance criteria

1. Scheduler sees recommended visit type with reason, required forms, slot length, financial caveats, and care-gap opportunities.
2. TCM booking enforces discharge window visibility and creates care-manager tasks.
3. Modality check prevents telehealth booking when patient location, technology, payer, or safety constraints fail.
4. Potential TCM request books within required timing window and starts TCM workflow.
5. A complex patient with multiple gaps receives longer slot recommendation.
6. Scheduler cannot book procedure without required room/equipment constraints.

## M07 - AURA PreVisit: Pre-Visit OS, Chart Scrub, Readiness Lock, and Huddle Engine

**Stage:** MVP core

**Mission:** Operationalize all staff work before the NP encounter: chart scrub, readiness scoring, records retrieval, quality mapping, financial clearance, patient readiness, huddle exceptions, and final handoff prep.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Implement the attached Pre-Visit Operating System as a first-class engine: weeks-before panel intelligence, 7-day chart scrub, 48-hour financial clearance, 24-hour readiness lock, morning huddle, same-day exception handling, and NP handoff.

### Functional responsibilities

- Seven-day chart scrub checklist
- 48-hour financial clearance checklist
- 24-hour readiness lock
- Green/yellow/red/black status
- Role-based defect queues
- Morning huddle board
- Pre-visit packet
- Source-linked handoff builder
- Open decision list
- No-blame defect logging
- The PreVisit engine creates a staged checklist by visit type and payer. It calculates readiness, assigns owners, tracks unresolved defects, generates the huddle brief, and produces a source-linked NP handoff that staff verify.

### Primary users and role behavior

- **MA:** uses AURA PreVisit to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **RN:** uses AURA PreVisit to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Pre-Visit Owner:** uses AURA PreVisit to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Flow Captain:** uses AURA PreVisit to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **NP:** uses AURA PreVisit to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.

- **Revenue Integrity:** uses AURA PreVisit to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Financial Clearance:** uses AURA PreVisit to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.

### Primary workflows

1. Seven-day chart scrub validates visit type, identity, eligibility, auth/referral, estimates, forms, HIE/records, utilization, meds, care gaps, standing orders, labs, risk prompts, care-management eligibility, barriers, and handoff readiness.
2. Day-before readiness lock classifies visits as green, yellow, red, or black and routes unresolved issues to named owners before the morning huddle.
3. Morning huddle groups exceptions by patient impact, time sensitivity, owner, and clinic-flow risk; routine green visits are summarized without wasting time.
4. NP Handoff Composer produces a concise, source-linked, staff-verified briefing containing patient agenda, safety flags, RCM caveats, clinical data, quality gaps, care-management opportunities, infection status, completed tasks, and NP decisions needed.
5. The PreVisit engine creates a staged checklist by visit type and payer. It calculates readiness, assigns owners, tracks unresolved defects, generates the huddle brief, and produces a source-linked NP handoff that staff verify.

## M08 - AURA FrontDesk: Registration, Patient Identity, Consent, and Front Desk Readiness

**Stage:** MVP

**Mission:** Make identity, demographic, consent, contact, guardian/caregiver, interpreter, accessibility, and privacy data reliable before the patient enters clinical workflow.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Front desk becomes a financial, identity, consent, language, infection-risk, and patient-experience gate with warm scripts and escalation rules, not a passive check-in desk.

### Functional responsibilities

- Two-identifier check-in
- Demographic verification
- Duplicate chart detection
- Insurance card capture
- Guardian/caregiver/ROI workflow
- Consent management
- Language/interpreter workflow
- Accessibility/accommodation flags
- Portal activation
- Front-desk exception scripts
- At arrival, FrontDesk verifies identity, coverage, forms, consent, copay/estimate status, interpreter, infection screen, and patient agenda, then routes exceptions to eligibility, financial counselor, flow captain, or MA.

### Primary users and role behavior

- **Front Desk:** uses AURA FrontDesk to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Registration Specialist:** uses AURA FrontDesk to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Patient:** uses AURA FrontDesk to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Caregiver:** uses AURA FrontDesk to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Privacy Officer:** uses AURA FrontDesk to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.

### Primary workflows

1. At check-in, staff verifies two identifiers, demographics, contact preferences, language, interpreter, caregiver/proxy, consent status, forms, insurance, and visit purpose.
2. Same-day eligibility recheck runs for high-risk payers or stale eligibility responses and updates financial-readiness tasks.
3. Front-desk exceptions use respectful scripts and route to financial counselor, flow captain, or RN without humiliating or delaying patients unnecessarily.
4. Patient arrival event triggers RTLS flow state, waiting-time timer, InfectionShield screen, rooming queue, and patient-facing status updates.
5. At arrival, FrontDesk verifies identity, coverage, forms, consent, copay/estimate status, interpreter, infection screen, and patient agenda, then routes exceptions to eligibility, financial counselor, flow captain, or MA.

### AI, rules, and automation boundaries

- AI may suggest duplicate chart candidates when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may draft warm patient scripts when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may detect conflicting demographics when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may prioritize front-desk exceptions when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- Module-specific AI/rules behavior: Detect duplicate-chart risk and demographic conflicts.; Draft patient-friendly scripts for coverage, estimate, forms, and delay exceptions.; Prioritize arrivals by appointment time, acuity flag, and readiness blockers.
- The module must not independently diagnose, bill, code, determine medical necessity, deny care, override infection-control policy, or finalize high-impact patient-financial conclusions.

### Business rules and validation gates

- Identity and consent checks must complete before nonurgent clinical workflow advances.
- Financial issues do not block urgent clinical assessment.
- Sensitive demographics and proxy rules require privacy-aware display.
- Apply dynamic stop logic by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, compliance risk, infection-control state, and clinical-safety risk.
- Every command validates tenant scope, role permission, data confidence, source freshness, required approvals, and downstream writeback eligibility.

### Security, privacy, and compliance controls

- Enforce Entra/OIDC identity, tenant isolation, RBAC/ABAC, least privilege, break-glass logging, and step-up authentication for high-risk actions.
- Classify every record and event as operational, PHI, financial, security, or AI-governance evidence; apply retention and audit policy accordingly.
- Encrypt data in transit and at rest; use Azure Key Vault/managed identity; prohibit secrets in code or logs.
- Log all PHI reads, EHR writebacks, AI outputs, patient messages, rule changes, chart-review actions, and approvals.
- Use privacy-preserving staff-location analytics; individual staff location is restricted to operationally necessary roles and audited.

### Observability and KPIs

- duplicate chart rate
- registration error rate
- check-in rework
- missing consent at NP entry
- interpreter booking completion
- portal activation
- Module health: queue age, event lag, failed jobs, API latency, rule errors, AI draft rejection rate, writeback failure rate, and audit exceptions.

### Acceptance criteria

1. Check-in cannot be completed without resolving required identity and consent gates or documenting an approved exception.
2. Duplicate chart alerts include evidence and resolution workflow.
3. Financial issues are routed respectfully to counselor without front-desk confrontation.
4. Inactive coverage creates exception task but does not remove patient from clinical queue automatically.
5. Duplicate-chart warning appears before rooming.
6. Interpreter need is carried forward to rooming and NP cockpit.

## M09 - AURA Records: Records, HIE, ADT, Diagnostics, and External Data Retrieval

**Stage:** MVP lite, enterprise full

**Mission:** Prevent missing-information encounters by retrieving, reconciling, summarizing, and tracking external records, discharge data, labs, imaging, immunizations, consults, and diagnostic dependencies.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Primary care requires aggressive HIE/ADT/discharge/specialist/lab/imaging retrieval to prevent NP discovery work, especially for TCM, ED follow-up, chronic care, and risk-adjustment evidence review.

### Functional responsibilities

- HIE query and CCD ingestion
- ADT discharge alerts
- Outside record request queue
- Lab/imaging portal links
- Immunization registry integration
- Diagnostic dependency tracker
- Missing critical record escalation
- Source-linked summaries
- Pending result tracking
- Record freshness/conflict detection
- Records Agent pulls or requests documents, summarizes relevance, marks missing-critical items, and links sources into the handoff. Critical gaps trigger red/black readiness depending on visit purpose.

- **Records Coordinator:** uses AURA Records to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.

## M10 - AURA Medication Sentinel: Medication Sentinel and Pharmacy Intelligence

**Stage:** MVP lite, phase 2 deep

**Mission:** Improve medication safety, adherence, affordability, quality performance, and visit readiness through fill history, formulary, interaction, high-risk medication, refill, and reconciliation intelligence.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Medication Sentinel supports MA/value-based outcomes: adherence, statins, antihypertensives, diabetes meds, cost barriers, refill gaps, discharge med changes, high-risk meds, and pharmacy preference.

### Functional responsibilities

- Medication fill-history pull
- eRx reconciliation
- OTC/supplement capture
- Allergy reconciliation
- High-risk medication flags
- Duplicate therapy detection
- Renal-dose concerns
- PDMP workflow integration point
- Adherence/cost barrier detection
- Formulary/benefit check
- Refill synchronization
- Medication questions for NP

### Primary users and role behavior

- **Pharmacy Tech:** uses AURA Medication Sentinel to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Pharmacist:** uses AURA Medication Sentinel to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **MA:** uses AURA Medication Sentinel to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **RN:** uses AURA Medication Sentinel to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **NP:** uses AURA Medication Sentinel to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Care Manager:** uses AURA Medication Sentinel to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.

### Primary workflows

1. Medication Sentinel imports EHR medication list, eRx history, fill history, discharge meds, patient-reported meds, OTC/supplements, pharmacy preference, allergies, and formulary data.
2. It identifies discrepancies, high-risk meds, duplicate therapy, adherence gaps, renal-dose concerns, interactions, controlled-substance workflow needs, and affordability barriers.
3. Rooming staff and pharmacy tech reconcile what can be gathered; NP receives decisions that require clinical judgment.
4. Medication findings feed quality measures, care-management eligibility, risk adjustment evidence, and patient engagement.
5. Medication data from EHR, patient intake, fill history, discharge documents, and pharmacy benefit signals are reconciled into a pre-NP med intelligence packet with confidence and unresolved discrepancies.

5. Missed refill appears in NP handoff as adherence concern, not diagnosis.
6. Formulary barrier creates financial/pharmacy workflow without auto-changing drug.

## M11 - AURA RevCycle: RevCycle-at-Service: Eligibility, Estimates, Payments, Notices, and Financial Experience

**Stage:** MVP

**Mission:** Make the encounter financially clean, transparent, and respectful before and during service through eligibility, benefits, estimates, GFE, ABN/payer notices, copay, financial assistance, and patient-responsibility workflows.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Optimize appropriate compliant revenue at time of service: eligibility, benefits, estimates/GFE, copay, financial assistance, ABN/payer notice, no coercive collections, and MA/value-based service readiness.

### Functional responsibilities

- 270/271/API eligibility runs
- Coverage and benefits dashboard
- PCP/network/COB checks
- Copay/deductible/coinsurance capture
- Estimate workflow
- GFE workflow for self-pay/uninsured
- ABN/payer notice workflow
- Financial assistance and payment plan routing
- Compassionate collections scripts
- Check-in financial exceptions
- Estimate variance tracking
- The RCM engine runs pre-arrival and same-day checks, generates patient-friendly estimates, routes affordability concerns, creates payer-notice tasks, and flags services with payer caveats without blocking urgent medically needed care.

### Primary users and role behavior

- **Eligibility Specialist:** uses AURA RevCycle to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **Financial Counselor:** uses AURA RevCycle to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.

### Primary workflows

1. Eligibility runs at booking, 72-48 hours before visit, and check-in for selected risk groups; responses populate coverage, benefits, network, PCP assignment, secondary payer, and cost-share fields.
2. Estimate engine calculates likely patient responsibility using contracted rates, benefit data, visit type, expected services, and known limitations; self-pay/uninsured workflows trigger GFE support when applicable.
3. Financial counselor workflow documents patient questions, assistance screening, payment plan, copay collection, and exceptions.
4. Financial status becomes part of readiness but does not override clinical safety or urgent care needs.

### Business rules and validation gates

- Estimates must clearly state assumptions and are not final payer adjudication.
- Self-pay/uninsured GFE workflows must track delivery date/method and requested services.
- Collections workflows must not pressure patients away from medically necessary urgent care.

- Every command validates tenant scope, role permission, data confidence, source freshness, required approvals, and downstream writeback eligibility.

### Security, privacy, and compliance controls

- Enforce Entra/OIDC identity, tenant isolation, RBAC/ABAC, least privilege, break-glass logging, and step-up authentication for high-risk actions.
- Classify every record and event as operational, PHI, financial, security, or AI-governance evidence; apply retention and audit policy accordingly.
- Encrypt data in transit and at rest; use Azure Key Vault/managed identity; prohibit secrets in code or logs.
- Log all PHI reads, EHR writebacks, AI outputs, patient messages, rule changes, chart-review actions, and approvals.
- Use privacy-preserving staff-location analytics; individual staff location is restricted to operationally necessary roles and audited.

- eligibility pass rate
- POS collection rate
- estimate delivery rate
- GFE timeliness
- ABN completion
- financial dispute rate
- front-end denial rate
- Module health: queue age, event lag, failed jobs, API latency, rule errors, AI draft rejection rate, writeback failure rate, and audit exceptions.

### Acceptance criteria

1. Financial status cannot block urgent medically necessary care; exception pathway and patient financial assistance workflow must be available.
2. Every estimate/GFE stores assumptions, service bundle, delivery method, timestamp, and patient questions.
3. Check-in view shows only actionable financial items and routes complex issues to counselor.
4. Inactive coverage creates clearance task and front-desk exception script.
5. GFE-required patient cannot arrive without documented GFE workflow unless same-day urgent exception.
6. Payment transaction updates check-in and claim-readiness state.

## M12 - AURA PayerOps: Payer Rules, Referrals, Prior Authorization, Medical Necessity, and Denial Prevention

**Stage:** MVP for high-value services

**Mission:** Maintain a versioned payer-rules library and workflow engine for referrals, prior authorization, medical-necessity checks, approvals, denials, expirations, units, and appeal tasks.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Support payer rules for MA/value-based primary care while preserving configurable FFS/commercial/Medicaid logic; fully handle referrals, auth, medical necessity, lab network, telehealth, and service-specific requirements.

## M13 - AURA QualityGuard: QualityGuard: Measure Logic, Care Gaps, Outcomes, and Structured Reporting

**Stage:** MVP for HEDIS/STARS/MIPS/internal outcomes

**Mission:** Turn quality reporting into real-time visit operations by identifying, routing, documenting, and closing preventive, chronic-care, behavioral-health, transition, and value-based care gaps.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Primary care v1 prioritizes HEDIS/STARS, MIPS/MVP, and internal outcomes. QualityGuard must make every visit a gap-closure event without burying measures in free text.

### Functional responsibilities

- Measure registry
- Care-gap engine
- Denominator/numerator/exclusion logic
- Structured declination/contraindication capture
- Standing-order opportunity detection
- Gap closure during waiting time
- eCQM/value-based reporting extracts
- Quality dashboard
- Outcome trend tracking
- Equity stratification
- Measure logic evaluates denominator, numerator, exclusion, gap status, evidence source, and next best action. Staff prepare closure actions, NP gets decision prompts, and structured data is written back after verification.

### Primary users and role behavior

- **Quality Analyst:** uses AURA QualityGuard to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.
- **MA:** uses AURA QualityGuard to execute the module mission within site/pod, role, and policy scope. Actions must be logged and filtered through tenant configuration, PHI access, and workflow ownership.

### Primary workflows

1. Quality engine evaluates each patient against measure logic, internal protocols, payer quality programs, registry rules, immunization schedules, chronic-disease gaps, preventive gaps, and exclusions.
2. Gaps are classified as ready to close today, needs NP decision, needs outside record, already completed elsewhere, not due, contraindicated/excluded, or declined.
3. Quality tasks are pushed to pre-visit, rooming, NP cockpit, checkout, and outreach workflows.
4. Closed gaps are stored in structured fields required for reporting, not buried in free text.
5. Measure logic evaluates denominator, numerator, exclusion, gap status, evidence source, and next best action. Staff prepare closure actions, NP gets decision prompts, and structured data is written back after verification.

### AI, rules, and automation boundaries

- AI may explain why a gap is due when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may find outside evidence that gap was completed when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may suggest ma-completable tasks when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may prioritize gaps by clinical impact and time available when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- Module-specific AI/rules behavior: Explain why a care gap is due and what evidence is missing.; Detect outside-record evidence that closes a gap.; Suggest which gaps can be completed during rooming versus requiring NP decision.
- The module must not independently diagnose, bill, code, determine medical necessity, deny care, override infection-control policy, or finalize high-impact patient-financial conclusions.

### Business rules and validation gates

- Measure logic must be versioned and source-linked.
- Patient declinations and contraindications must be captured respectfully and with required structured reason.
- Quality gap prompts must never override patient preference or clinical judgment.
- Apply dynamic stop logic by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, compliance risk, infection-control state, and clinical-safety risk.
- Every command validates tenant scope, role permission, data confidence, source freshness, required approvals, and downstream writeback eligibility.

### Security, privacy, and compliance controls

- Enforce Entra/OIDC identity, tenant isolation, RBAC/ABAC, least privilege, break-glass logging, and step-up authentication for high-risk actions.
- Classify every record and event as operational, PHI, financial, security, or AI-governance evidence; apply retention and audit policy accordingly.
- Encrypt data in transit and at rest; use Azure Key Vault/managed identity; prohibit secrets in code or logs.
- Log all PHI reads, EHR writebacks, AI outputs, patient messages, rule changes, chart-review actions, and approvals.
- Use privacy-preserving staff-location analytics; individual staff location is restricted to operationally necessary roles and audited.

### Observability and KPIs

- gap closure per visit
- structured exclusion rate
- measure performance
- outcomes by panel
- quality defects
- equity variance
- Module health: queue age, event lag, failed jobs, API latency, rule errors, AI draft rejection rate, writeback failure rate, and audit exceptions.

### Acceptance criteria

1. Care gap status must include due reason, source evidence, action owner, completion pathway, and reporting field mapping.
2. Closed gaps are recorded in structured fields, not just note text.
3. QualityGuard can defer a gap with reason: not due, outside completed, contraindicated, declined, needs NP decision, or needs outside record.
4. Outside retinal exam closes diabetes eye gap after record verification.
5. BP repeat protocol changes quality status only after valid second reading.
6. Patient decline is reported with correct structured reason and follow-up plan.

### Codex build checklist

- Create `aura_qualityguard` service, repository, policy, event handlers, tests, and UI route.
- Implement non-AI rules and deterministic workflows before adding LLM/RAG or predictive automation.
- Create migrations for listed objects and link them to shared tenant/patient/appointment/task/audit IDs.
- Create OpenAPI schemas and DTOs for commands, queries, events, and read-model responses.
- Create UI components with loading, empty, error, permission-denied, draft-review, source-link, and audit-history states.
- Create unit, integration, E2E, security, PHI audit, workflow, API contract, and failure-mode tests.


## M14 - AURA InfectionShield: InfectionShield: Outpatient Infection Control, Room Safety, PPE, Cleaning, and Exposure Tools

**Stage:** MVP infection-ready room state, enterprise exposure reconstruction

**Mission:** Embed infection-prevention controls into pre-arrival screening, room assignment, equipment state, PPE prompts, cleaning workflows, exposure reconstruction, and room-release logic.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** Enterprise architecture includes five infection-control levels; v1 builds room/equipment cleaning, respiratory screening, direct-rooming, PPE prompts, and infection-control-ready room status.

### Functional responsibilities

- Pre-arrival symptom/exposure screening
- Direct-rooming logic
- Clean/dirty/isolation room states
- PPE prompts
- Hand-hygiene opportunity logging where configured
- Equipment contamination/cleaning state
- Disinfectant contact-time timers
- UV-C/adjuvant cleaning log where used
- Exposure window reconstruction
- Waiting-room crowding alerts
- High-risk patient routing
- Pre-arrival screening and RTLS combine to route respiratory-risk or immunocompromised patients, hold dirty rooms, enforce cleaning contact-time timers, flag equipment cleaning, and provide auditable room release.

### Primary workflows

1. Pre-visit screening identifies respiratory/GI/rash/exposure symptoms, immunocompromised status, direct-rooming needs, and telehealth conversion opportunities.
2. Room readiness merges occupancy, cleaning status, required cleaning type, contact-time timer, isolation compatibility, equipment readiness, and PPE supply.
3. Patient routing bypasses waiting room when appropriate and prevents high-risk patient overlap with incompatible infection-control states.
4. Exposure investigation reconstructs time/space overlap across patients, staff, rooms, equipment, and cleaning events under restricted access.
5. Pre-arrival screening and RTLS combine to route respiratory-risk or immunocompromised patients, hold dirty rooms, enforce cleaning contact-time timers, flag equipment cleaning, and provide auditable room release.

### Acceptance criteria

1. Flow Optimizer cannot assign a patient to a room unless room state satisfies infection-control rules.
2. Cleaning task requires protocol, responsible role, start/end/contact-time, and release confirmation.
3. Exposure reconstruction uses limited, authorized, auditable access to location history.
4. Positive respiratory screen routes patient to direct-rooming workflow.
5. Dirty isolation room is unavailable to optimizer.
6. Equipment used in isolation room becomes unavailable until cleaned.

## M15 - AURA CareOps: Care Management Opportunity Engine: TCM, CCM, APCM, PCM, RPM/RTM, BHI/CoCM, CHI/PIN

**Stage:** MVP AWV/TCM/CCM/APCM/RPM prioritization

**Mission:** Identify, prepare, consent, task, track, and govern longitudinal care-management services when clinically appropriate and payer-compliant.

**Reference primary-care behavior:** CareOps detects and prepares AWV/IPPE, TCM, CCM, APCM, PCM, RPM/RTM, BHI/CoCM, CHI/PIN, ACP, and social-care workflows without letting AI or staff decide final billing.

- AI may draft care-plan skeletons when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may summarize barriers and goals when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- AI may recommend care-team assignments when the output is draft, source-linked, confidence-scored, and reviewable.
- Module-specific AI/rules behavior: Identify care-management candidates and summarize why.; Draft care-plan skeletons from problems, goals, and barriers.; Detect duplicate-service risk and missing consent/time documentation.
- The module must not independently diagnose, bill, code, determine medical necessity, deny care, override infection-control policy, or finalize high-impact patient-financial conclusions.

### Business rules and validation gates

- Staff prepares eligibility and documentation; NP or qualified billing provider approves clinical plan and service selection.
- Programs with consent/cost-share requirements cannot activate without captured consent.
- Duplicate-billing conflicts hold charge candidates until review.
- Apply dynamic stop logic by service line, payer, visit type, urgency, compliance risk, infection-control state, and clinical-safety risk.
- Every command validates tenant scope, role permission, data confidence, source freshness, required approvals, and downstream writeback eligibility.

### Security, privacy, and compliance controls

- Enforce Entra/OIDC identity, tenant isolation, RBAC/ABAC, least privilege, break-glass logging, and step-up authentication for high-risk actions.
- Classify every record and event as operational, PHI, financial, security, or AI-governance evidence; apply retention and audit policy accordingly.
- Encrypt data in transit and at rest; use Azure Key Vault/managed identity; prohibit secrets in code or logs.
- Log all PHI reads, EHR writebacks, AI outputs, patient messages, rule changes, chart-review actions, and approvals.
- Use privacy-preserving staff-location analytics; individual staff location is restricted to operationally necessary roles and audited.

### Observability and KPIs

- TCM contact within window
- care-management enrollment
- care-plan completion
- monthly activity completion
- hospitalization/ED follow-up
- duplicate billing risk
- Module health: queue age, event lag, failed jobs, API latency, rule errors, AI draft rejection rate, writeback failure rate, and audit exceptions.

### Acceptance criteria

1. Eligibility opportunity cannot become active service without consent workflow and NP/qualified user approval where required.
2. TCM workflow tracks discharge date, contact attempts, successful contact, face-to-face deadline, medication reconciliation, and duplicate reporting risk.
3. Care-management billing readiness is separated from clinical appropriateness and requires revenue integrity checks.
4. ADT event creates TCM case and interactive-contact task.
5. CCM candidate requires consent and care plan before enrollment active.
6. Monthly time tracker prevents billing-support status until threshold and activity requirements pass.
